description: Historic St. James's auction house doubles as a free gallery for fine art and rare collectibles. Rotating pre-sale exhibitions fill a maze of rooms, displaying museum-tier pieces just before they enter private collections.

name: Three Colts Tavern
description: Moody, navy-walled East End pub pouring Exale Brewing pints and natural wine. The room runs loud on weekends with Italian-American tavern pizzas, shuffleboard, and DJ sets.

name: William The Fourth | Leyton
description: Renovated Leyton pub pouring fresh craft beer and cask ale from nearby Exale Brewing. The laid-back space fills up for live sports on the big screen, weekend DJ sets, and award-winning thin-crust pizzas.

name: Lawn Road Flats
description: Built in 1934, the Lawn Road Flats were a revolutionary experiment in urban living. Now, the structure serves as a modernist monument that houses the Isokon Gallery - a public exhibition detailing the building's history.

name: Screen On The Green
description: With its recognizable neon sign, this single screen venue is one of the oldest running cinemas in the country. Bought by the Everyman brand in 2018, Screen on the Green continues to welcome movie-goers.

name: Short Road Pizza
description: East London pizza kitchen running out of two lively neighborhood pubs. The ultra-thin pies blend Romana and New York styles, arriving blistered and paired with hot honey dips and steady pints.

name: Mercato Metropolitano
description: Sprawling food market in a former paper factory with dozens of international street food vendors – from Neapolitan pizza to Korean barbecue. The industrial space spills out into a festoon-lit garden where groups gather at long communal tabl

name: AGORA souvla bar
description: Lively ground-floor Greek spot on the edge of Borough Market running heavily on walk-ins. Communal tables stay packed for fresh flatbreads, dips, and spit-roasted meats pulled off a massive central charcoal rotisserie.

name: CRATE Bar & Pizzeria Hackney Wick
description: Lively canalside brewery built into a raw Hackney Wick factory. Reclaimed pallet tables fill the loud industrial room, while the outdoor terrace sits right on the water for afternoon beers, thin-crust pizza, and evening DJ sets.

name: The Harwood Arms
description: Relaxed Fulham neighborhood pub serving Michelin-starred British game. Venison scotch eggs and seasonal plates land on antique pine tables surrounded by taxidermy and scuffed leather chairs.

name: Zealand Road Coffee
description: Hearty brunch plates blend English classics with Mediterranean options like shakshuka and grilled halloumi. The sunny, exposed-brick room is a neighborhood fixture, especially for weekend brunch.

name: Moko Made Cafe
description: Home-style Japanese cafe serving matcha cheesecakes and salmon onigiri on mismatched vintage crockery. The small, curated space fills up quickly – expect weekend queues and a no-laptop policy during lunch.

name: Josephine Bouchon - Chelsea
description: Bustling Lyonnaise bouchon serving hearty French classics in a tightly packed Chelsea dining room. Colorful posters line dark wood walls above small tables piled with onion soup, cheese soufflés, and glasses of Rhône wine.

name: Clissold Park Tavern
description: Laid-back neighborhood pub across from Clissold Park pouring local craft beer and serving wood-fired pizza. Screens for live sports line the copper-topped bar and fill the massive heated beer garden.

name: Lodestar Coffee
description: Destination coffee shop pouring a constantly changing lineup of single-origin beans from international guest roasters. The owner is usually behind the counter – pulling shots on a La Marzocco and talking coffee with a welcoming crowd of reg

name: The Duke of Edinburgh
description: Sprawling 1930s Brixton pub with a massive rear beer garden lined with long benches, outdoor screens, and its own bar. Pints and jerk chicken flow through the yard until an early curfew shifts drinking into the historic wood-paneled bar.

name: Bank of Friendship
description: Classic Highbury pub pouring a steady rotation of cask ales. The dark, wood-paneled interior packs out on Arsenal match days, pushing the overflow into a large heated rear garden.

name: Yeast Bakery
description: Viennoiserie bakery on the Regent's Canal with an open kitchen turning out classic French pastries. Outdoor tables on the towpath fill up with runners and walkers stopping for coffee.

name: Brooks Butchers
description: Traditional neighborhood butcher shop specializing in free-range meat and game. Knowledgeable staff advise on the day’s best cuts – from sirloin steaks to wild boar sausages – with tips on preparation.

name: Tamesis Dock
description: Casual floating pub on a converted 1930s Dutch barge permanently moored on the Thames. Pints and hand-stretched pizzas cover tables on the open-air deck facing Parliament, with live bands playing down in the hull.

name: Pub On The Park
description: Classic Hackney neighborhood pub on the edge of London Fields with a massive wraparound beer garden. The sprawling outdoor terrace runs steady on summer weekends with garden barbecues, local pints, and live sports on the big screens.

name: Berwick Street Market
description: Long-running Soho street market now defined by its international food stalls. Lunchtime crowds queue for everything from Jerusalem falafel to Japanese miso, while traditional fruit sellers still line the pavement.

name: From The Ashes BBQ | Hackney | London
description: Live-fire smokehouse set in the courtyard of Hackney's Five Points Brewery. Cooks pull 12-hour smoked wagyu brisket and beef short ribs from the pits, pairing heavy plates of barbecue with fresh pints in the open air.

name: The Engineer
description: Classic Primrose Hill pub running a traditional front bar alongside modern dining rooms. Pints of craft ale and aged beef Sunday roasts head out to a walled beer garden under a wooden pergola.

name: Chesham Arms
description: Traditional Victorian pub on a residential Hackney corner. The single-room bar pours rotating cask ales alongside delivered boxes of Yard Sale Pizza, with seating split between two working fireplaces and a large summer garden.

name: The Edinboro Castle
description: Traditional British pub near Regent's Park with a massive, chalet-lined beer garden. Sunny afternoons pack the outdoor tables, with a dedicated garden bar and barbecue running steady into the evening.

name: Pear Tree Cafe
description: Breezy cafe in Battersea Park sitting right on the edge of the boating lake. The kitchen serves seasonal brunch plates and house-made pizzas across a massive outdoor terrace that fills up fast on sunny days.

name: People's Park Tavern
description: Sprawling East London pub and microbrewery backing directly onto Victoria Park. The massive beer garden stretches toward the green, pouring house-brewed pints from an outdoor bar alongside a BBQ kitchen and mini golf course.

name: Pavilion Cafe Victoria Park
description: Blue-domed lakeside cafe and bakery running a busy counter for fresh sourdough and morning coffee. Covered tables sit right by the Victoria Park boating lake for hot dhal and Sri Lankan coconut pancakes.

name: Emirates Stadium
description: Modern, glass-wrapped football stadium and home to Arsenal FC. The 60,000-seat tiered bowl gets loud on match days, with pre-game energy filling the nearby Holloway pubs and building around the statues outside.

name: Vicinity
description: Riverfront dining room and heated terrace sitting right at the foot of Tower Bridge. Outdoor fire pits warm the riverside lounge, while the glass-walled interior fills up for steaks, cocktails, and direct views of the Thames.

name: 12th Knot
description: This fancy rooftop bar can be found atop the Sea Containers hotel. Its glass box structure offers the perfect spot to watch the sunset with a cocktail, or glass of wine, in hand. Light bites can be ordered when peckish. Book ahead.

name: Ham Yard Hotel
description: Part of the Firmdale family, all of the 91 rooms are uniquely designed by award-winning designer Kit Kemp. The hotel is built around a lush, tree-filled courtyard which makes for great alfresco dining. There's a bowling alley too 🎳.

name: Grand Hotel Bellevue London
description: Victorian townhouse hotel facing Norfolk Square right by Paddington Station. Boldly colored lounges mix dark wood and vintage furniture, leading up to compact, cabin-style rooms built for short city trips.

name: Cecil Sharp House
description: The art venue for, and home of, the English Folk Dance and Song Society. Not only does Cecil Sharp House offer live events, classes, and courses in all things folk, but it is also home to one of the genre's largest archives.

name: London School of Economics and Political Science
description: Energetic university campus spread across the central streets between Covent Garden and Holborn. A highly international student crowd fills the mix of old stone buildings and modern lecture halls to study economics and politics.

name: Sims Reed Gallery
description: Modernist gallery featuring print works by iconic and emerging artists.

name: Museum of the Home
description: Museum exploring home interiors from throughout London’s history. A place to observe societal change, as well as the evolution of style and taste. A rainy-day spot.

name: Drupe Cafe • Broadway Market
description: Bustling Broadway Market cafe serving specialty coffee and Middle Eastern-inspired brunch. The open front spills directly onto the street, bringing plates of warm shakshuka and fresh salads right into the steady neighborhood hum.

name: Mare Street Market Hackney
description: Massive Hackney food hall and market occupying a former 1960s office block. The plant-draped floor runs steady from daytime laptop sessions to evening pizzas, pints, and weekend DJ sets under heavy chandeliers.

name: Sen Noods
description: Mobile food van serving East Asian noodles and chili oil dumplings from bustling open-air markets. Hot bowls of rich Dan Dan noodles and tonkotsu ramen move quickly across the counter to tarp-covered outdoor benches.

name: Blackfriars Bridge
description: Victorian wrought-iron bridge moving a steady flow of bikes, cars, and foot traffic across the Thames. Broad pedestrian paths run along both edges, with clear sightlines straight to St. Paul's Cathedral and the Tate Modern.

name: Dom's Subs @ Rasputins
description: No-frills takeaway counter turning out massive Italian-American subs on house-baked semolina rolls. Heavy, fully loaded sandwiches cross the counter fast, stacked with classic cold cuts or spicy Thai chicken for a filling lunch.

name: Bella Vita - Broadway
description: Neighbourhood Italian staple on Broadway Market slinging wood-fired pizzas and fresh pasta. Large front windows face the street while the brick-lined dining room stays packed and buzzing through the evening.

name: Mexclub Hackney
description: Hackney Bridge food stall turning out slow-cooked birria tacos, tortas, and loaded nachos. Plates of rich, family-recipe street food and cups of warm consommé move straight from the counter to shared mezzanine seating.

name: Carbobar
description: Former Hackney Wick pub turned warm, family-run Italian kitchen and bar. Fresh pasta, artisanal pizzas, and craft cocktails fill the tables, while the room shifts from cozy dinners to late drinks on the canalside terrace.

name: Caloroso Neapolitan Pizza & Bar (Hackney)
description: Compact Hackney pizzeria with a roaring wood-fired oven and a TV playing Italian walking tours. The energetic dining room runs on blistered Neapolitan pies, classic cocktails, and gluten-free or vegan versions of every single dish.

name: Colour Factory
description: Black-owned Hackney Wick warehouse club throwing unpolished raves and live gigs. Sweaty electronic sets run under a giant disco ball in the raw main room, while a massive heated terrace serves street food year-round.

name: Elephant Hackney
description: Restored Victorian pub serving generous, family-style Southern Italian cooking. Candlelit tables beneath a salvaged stained-glass skylight crowd with Negronis, Neapolitan pizzas, and shared plates of slow-cooked beef ragu.

name: Zapata Burger London
description: Lively London Fields burger shop layering classic beef patties with Anatolian spices. The relaxed dining room runs steady with orders of soft buns stuffed with Turkish pastirma or charred aubergine alongside generous fries.

name: All My Friends
description: Hackney Wick warehouse bar shifting from afternoon record shopping and pizza to loud late-night DJ sets. A custom hi-fi system and red-tiled DJ booth sit in the middle of the room as bartenders pour local craft beer and natural wine.

name: Berberè Pizzeria Westfield Stratford
description: Colorful Westfield Stratford pizzeria serving 24-hour fermented sourdough. The open kitchen turns out light pizzas loaded with Italian ingredients and sliced into eight pieces for sharing.

name: Randy's Wing Bar (Hackney Wick)
description: Industrial canalside spot pairing platters of sticky wings with local craft beer on tap. Rolls of paper towels sit on every table, and the open-fronted dining room spills straight out onto the waterfront grass.

name: You Call The Shots
description: Intimate Hackney cocktail bar serving creative drinks alongside a rotating lineup of guest chefs. A spinning disco ball hangs over the leopard-print floor as bartenders sling mezcal margaritas and beer-and-shot combos.

name: University College London
description: Active Bloomsbury campus anchored by a neoclassical quadrangle and a grand stone portico. Public paths cut through the academic grounds, leading to niche zoology and archaeology museums alongside the preserved body of Jeremy Bentham.

name: 101 Thai Kitchen
description: Canteen-style Hammersmith dining room serving fiercely spicy Isaan and Southern Thai cooking. Long tables fill a pink-walled space, crowded with plates of som tum, sticky rice, and baskets of fresh vegetables and pork scratchings.

name: Royal China (Chinatown)
description: Modern dining room on Gerrard Street serving traditional Cantonese cooking and handmade dim sum. Dark wood screens surround large round tables loaded with roast duck and massive plates of noodles.

name: Speedboat Bar
description: Loud, neon-lit Soho canteen slinging spicy Thai-Chinese plates late into the night. Tables quickly fill with aromatic noodles, whisky sodas, and tall towers of Singha beer under TVs showing Thai sports.

name: Mexican Seoul
description: Casual Bow Wharf restaurant slinging Mexican-Korean street food on the edge of Victoria Park. The exposed-brick dining room and vine-draped patio run heavy on bulgogi beef tacos, gochujang wings, and rounds of soju.

name: Angel Dabang
description: Narrow Korean bakery and takeaway tucked into an Islington alleyway. The grab-and-go counter hands over twisted doughnuts, fried bread sandwiches, and spicy rice cakes that regularly sell out before closing.

name: The Red Lion & Sun
description: Proper neighborhood pub with a serious kitchen dishing up rustic, modern British food. The daily menu is a draw, but the Sunday roast is the main event – book ahead for a spot by the fire or in the garden.

name: Bar Levan
description: Candlelit Peckham wine bar pouring low-intervention bottles alongside French snacks like comté fries and devilled eggs. The small room runs steady through the evening with shared plates, conversation, and spinning vinyl.

name: Love Supreme Projects
description: Bright yoga studio filling a converted 19th-century brick church on Golborne Road. Busy Jivamukti and chanting classes run under high ceilings, finishing with hot chai, samosas, and quiet journaling in the sunlit room.

name: Crystal Palace Antiques
description: Four-story Victorian warehouse stocked with restored mid-century furniture from independent dealers. Sunlight fills the spacious upper floors, landing on a steady rotation of wood sideboards, Danish chairs, and vintage lighting.

name: Calluna
description: Notting Hill floral studio designing sculptural event arrangements from unusual, wilder blooms. The Golborne Road storefront sells a rotating mix of curious seasonal cut stems, indoor plants, and vases.

name: Norbert's
description: Tiny East Dulwich rotisserie serving expertly roasted chicken and rich pepper butter. The 16-seat walk-in room runs on a tight menu of half birds, chicken fat potatoes, and margaritas rimmed with crispy skin salt.

name: Café Oto
description: Café by day, Oto turns into one of the best ways to enjoy live music by night. Expect alternative line-ups and experimental set lists. Open seven days a week - so turn up at random, or keep an eye on the event calendar.

name: The Zetter Townhouse
description: Eccentric hotel taled to once house a fictional great aunt that collected souvenirs from around the world. The entrance of the hotel presents an apothecary-style bar where patrons will be offered a gin cocktail upon arrival.

name: Rellik
description: Long-running Portobello vintage shop packed with rare, decades-old designer fashion. Dense racks hold tightly curated Vivienne Westwood, Alexander McQueen, and John Galliano pieces regularly pulled by working stylists.

name: Kawan by Uncle Roger
description: Bright, informal Chinatown dining room serving pan-Asian share plates over a soundtrack of Malaysian city pop. Closely packed tables fill with bowls of chilli jam fried rice and the signature crispy puff chicken Wellington.

name: Electric Cinema
description: Edwardian picture house with leather seats and cashmere blankets. Screening both mainstream and art house films. Enjoy a night at the cinema with beer or wine in hand.

name: Royal Academy of Arts
description: Holds the prestigious title of Britain's first art school. The Royal Academy exhibits all mediums of craftwork and creativity - from landmark collections to amateur-driven showcases. Entry is free year-round.

name: Fred Bakery Oxford Circus
description: Split-level Fitzrovia bakery turning out fresh pastries, focaccia pizzas, and coffee. The bright ground floor handles a fast takeaway line, while the quieter basement runs at a slower pace with open laptops and lingering.

name: Coppa Club Tower Bridge
description: Unique dining experience alongside the Thames. Headlined by a set of igloos, Coppa Club allows patrons to eat beneath the sun or stars whilst remaining sheltered and warm - the venue also has a full interior. Here, aesthetics come first.

name: Ikoyi
description: Modern fine dining establishment in London offering West African and European fusion.

name: The Hoxton, Southwark
description: Located within striking distance of the Thames, the upscale Hoxton Southwark offers charming rooms, two hip restaurants (one with lovely city views), and close proximity to Tate Modern.

name: La Maritxu Connaught - Basque Cheesecake
description: Tiny Connaught Village bakery serving thick slices of Basque cheesecake. Wedges with dark, caramelized tops and custard-soft centers come on paper plates, usually grabbed to go when the two sidewalk tables are taken.

name: The Standard, London
description: A 5-star hotel with a multitude of amenities. Alongside plush rooms, the venue boasts a live music studio, a library, a selection of dining options, and a pair of bars - one, an indoor cocktail venue; the other, a rooftop terrace.

name: Towpath
description: Open-air cafe running out of four shallow kiosks along the Regent's Canal. Communal tables line the waterside towpath for daily-changing seasonal plates, coffee, and wine from spring through autumn.

name: Parliament Hill Fields Lido
description: Unheated open-air swimming pool 🏊 that is open for swimmers 365 days a year. Summers bring in many guests wanting to bask in the sun ☀️ and let their kids play. Come early during the summer if you want a calmer environment.

name: Ria's
description: Casual pizzeria serving thick Detroit-style pies with crispy, caramelized cheese edges and a tight list of natural wines. The pepperoni comes drizzled with hot honey; dessert is a deep-fried Mars bar with soft serve.

name: Cô Thành
description: Southern Vietnamese spot paying tribute to Saigon’s legendary “Lunch Lady” and her signature noodle soups. The room is unfussy, with exposed brick and metal tables designed to evoke her original street food stall.

name: The Photographers' Gallery
description: Five-story Soho photography gallery occupying a converted brick warehouse. Three upper floors of contemporary and historical exhibitions lead down to a specialist bookshop, a street-level café, and a working analogue photo booth.

name: Victoria and Albert Museum
description: With over 150 galleries spread across seven floors, there is something for everyone at the Victoria & Albert Museum. It is especially renowned for its collection of Renaissance Italian sculpture and applied arts from across the globe.

name: Omotesando Koffee
description: Minimalist Fitzrovia coffee shop built around a timber cube where baristas in white coats methodically prepare pour-overs and matcha. A handful of fold-out stools line the window, keeping the daily rhythm fast and focused.

name: Sexy Fish Mayfair
description: Opulent Mayfair dining room serving sushi and Robata-grilled seafood alongside a massive Japanese whisky collection. Bronze mermaids and glowing fish lamps surround the bar while daily DJ sets keep the room loud late into the night.

name: Khao So-i
description: Northern Thai spot specializing in Khao Soi – a complex coconut curry noodle soup from a 40-year-old family recipe. Shareable small plates include Chiang Mai sausage; the Thai tea cheesecake is the essential finish.

name: Basement Sate
description: Subterranean Soho cocktail bar pairing seasonal drinks with elaborate plated desserts. Dimly lit booths and leather sofas sit against dark wood and exposed brick, with weekend DJs playing late into the night.

name: Blacklock Covent Garden
description: Subterranean chophouse serving thick steaks and piles of chops in a lively, brick-lined basement. Waiters navigate the busy dining room pushing tableside cocktail trolleys and pouring wine straight from the tap.

name: Loaf - Clerkenwell
description: Fast-paced Clerkenwell lunch counter slinging thick brioche sandwiches for quick midday meals. The fully halal menu sticks to heavy, stacked options like hot honey fried chicken, smash burgers, and French butter steak.

name: TANGRA
description: Vegetarian Indo-Chinese restaurant serving spicy sharing plates from a retro-futurist Soho space. Neon signs glow over dishes like Manchurian kofta and Hakka-style tacos, with creative cocktails poured late into the night.

name: The Big Plate Cafe
description: Traditional London greasy spoon turning out massive fry-ups and hearty British lunches. Quick service keeps the cozy room moving as heavy portions of eggs, beans, and black pudding hit the tables.

name: 3Gorges London
description: Three-story Fitzrovia dining room finished with blue-black paneling, marble floors, and silk lanterns. Service moves at a measured pace, bringing out intricate dim sum, caviar Peking duck, and elaborate tasting menus.

name: Blue Shop Gallery
description: Intimate South London gallery showing emerging contemporary art with a fast rotation of pop-ups and exhibitions. The unpretentious space operates as an active neighborhood hub, running regular artist talks and hands-on workshops.

name: Voodoo Ray's Dalston
description: Late-night Dalston pizza shop slinging massive New York-style slices from a long tile counter. Loud hip-hop and bright neon run through the fast-paced room, with frozen margaritas spinning steadily in slush machines.

name: Discount Suit Company
description: Spitalfields basement bar hidden behind the faded storefront of an old suit shop. Bartenders slide classic cocktails across a repurposed cloth-cutting table as a Northern Soul soundtrack fills the tight, low-ceilinged room.

name: Canopy Market
description: Covered King's Cross market running beneath a restored Victorian steel canopy. Mid-week stalls serve strictly street food, while weekends expand into a full lineup of artisan bakers, craft stalls, and rotating food vendors.

name: Serpentine Galleries
description: Since 1970 this gallery offers a robust program of exhibitions, architecture, education, and live events. Split between two venues, both in Kensington Gardens, they exhibit established and emerging artists alike.

name: The Connaught Bar
description: Celebrated bar within its namesake hotel. Known for martinis and its upmarket atmosphere, The Connaught Bar has earned itself a place on the "World's 50 Best Bars" list. There is also a concise food menu to order from.

name: Bob Bob Ricard Soho
description: Glamorous, all-booth dining room designed like a vintage luxury train carriage. Brass tableside buttons summon champagne on demand alongside classic Beef Wellington and caviar in a plush, adults-only setting.

name: ChaTraMue - The Original Thai Tea
description: Tiny Soho takeaway counter pouring authentic Thai iced milk tea. The grab-and-go setup mixes bright orange brews to custom sugar levels and sells bags of the signature tea mix for home.

name: Where The Pancakes Are - Flat Iron Square
description: Bright railway arch restaurant serving sweet and savory buttermilk pancake stacks and oven-baked Dutch babies. Plants hang from the curved ceiling above busy brunch tables, with heated outdoor seats facing The Shard.

name: Godfrey’s Popcorn
description: Retro Covent Garden shop popping small-batch popcorn fresh throughout the day. Sweet and savory flavors – like caramel and mild cheddar – get mixed into a single bag, often grabbed alongside a glass bottle of Coke.

name: Cantoast Bakery
description: Bright yellow Marylebone bakery turning out Asian-inspired baked goods from an open kitchen. The counter fills with deep-fried Hong Kong French toast, bolo buns, and stuffed Korean salt breads made with house shokupan.

name: Weezie's
description: Relaxed Belgravia pizzeria serving thin-crust pies, small plates, and cocktails. The warm dining room and courtyard tables run steady with walk-ins, catching groups finishing drinks at the adjoining sister wine studio.

name: Taverna Ermou London
description: Relaxed Marylebone taverna serving unhurried, shared Greek meals. Marble tables fill with thick pitta, white taramasalata, and plates of charred octopus under soft globe lighting.

name: Marian Goodman Projects
description: The Marian Goodman Gallery was established in NYC to foster dialogue between European artists and the US public. Marian Goodman Projects, the gallery's new initiative, now serves to exhibit artwork throughout London and other major cities.

name: Delizie D'italia
description: Compact Pimlico deli packed with imported Italian groceries and hanging panettone. The busy lunch counter serves massive made-to-order ciabatta paninis, hot Sicilian arancini, and fresh espresso for takeout or the few tables outside.

name: Flat Iron Soho
description: Bustling Soho steakhouse running a stripped-back menu focused entirely on one affordable cut of beef. Signature steaks arrive on wooden boards alongside mini cleavers, followed by complimentary soft serve on the way out.

name: Cafe Kick
description: Part food joint part bar. Cafe Kick is a hybrid space offering hearty dishes, cold beers, cocktails, table football, and live sports coverage. A popular hangout from midday till late.

name: Min Jiang
description: Tenth-floor Chinese dining room looking out over Hyde Park and the London skyline. Chefs carve wood-fired Beijing duck tableside while groups share dim sum and Cantonese plates.

name: 28-50 Wine Workshop and Kitchen
description: The first of three London locations. 28-50 in Marylebone offers an extensive wine list that has been thoughtfully curated to pair with a selection of seasonal European plates. The venue itself is stylish and refined.

name: Donostia
description: Not many restaurants in the city offer real Basque cuisine. Donostia does traditional yet unique pintxos & tapas. Try the Arriza, monk fish served with black rice, and the cordero, succulent lamb cutlets grilled to perfection.

name: Dim Sum Duck King’s Cross Road
description: Tiny, cash-only Cantonese dining room turning out handmade dim sum and roast duck. The twenty closely packed seats turn over quickly, with orders taken straight from the line outside.

name: The British Museum
description: Self-coined as "the first national public museum of the world", the British Museum ironically houses artifacts from across the globe. Once past that irony, tour the institution's showcase of ancient discoveries.

name: Gordos Pizzeria
description: Cozy Dalston pizzeria turning out Neapolitan pies from an open kitchen and tiled wood-fired oven. Natural wine and house chili oil run steady into the night, followed by pistachio tiramisu.

name: Sonora Taquería
description: Narrow Stoke Newington taquería serving Northern Mexican tacos on fresh flour tortillas. Lines spill onto the sidewalk outside the counter-service space, where orders are dressed at a salsa bar and eaten at a few scattered stools.

name: Del74 Tacos
description: High-energy Dalston taqueria running loud and fast with tight tables and a heavy soundtrack. The kitchen slings traditional street tacos alongside steady rounds of mezcal margaritas.

name: Kricket Brixton
description: Busy modern Indian dining room built into two exposed-brick railway arches. The open kitchen turns out sharing plates of Keralan fried chicken and samphire pakoras while trains rumble directly overhead.

name: Rack City Ribs
description: Resident Camden kitchen serving slow-smoked American barbecue with Jamaican roots. Trays of applewood-smoked ribs and loaded brisket fries land on wooden tables alongside pints.

name: Bottle + Rye
description: Intimate Brixton Market wine bar pouring minimal-intervention bottles and seasonal cocktails. Tall counter seating faces a tiny open kitchen where frequent chef residencies serve an ever-changing menu of small plates.

name: Jikoni
description: Homestyle, family food. Self-proclaimed as a "no-borders kitchen". Operating with an instinctive style of cooking, and serving dishes inspired by immigrant cuisines and cultures from South Asia, the Middle East, East Africa, and Britain.

name: OKAN Brixton East
description: Down-to-earth Coldharbour Lane izakaya serving everyday Osakan street food. The spacious, retro-styled dining room runs on savory okonomiyaki, fried noodles, and cold highballs.

name: Black Bear Burger - Restaurant Brixton
description: Sit-down burger joint in the covered lanes of Brixton Village. The wood-paneled room runs loud and busy on weekends, serving dry-aged beef patties and house-made sides at raw timber tables.

name: Ghost Whale
description: Brixton bottle shop and bar lined with fridges holding hundreds of craft beers. A central communal table and a small back garden run steady with pre-gig pints from rotating taps and cold cans pulled straight off the shelves.

name: Supercute Brewhouse
description: Spacious Brixton taproom running out of a former grain mill by the train tracks. House beers pour right next to the brewing tanks, with pints, focaccia sandwiches, and free popcorn landing on tables surrounded by sofas and board games.

name: Maureen's Brixton Kitchen
description: Traditional Jamaican takeaway operating out of a residential Brixton backyard. Jerk pans smoke in the open air, turning out heavy foil containers packed with curry goat, oxtail, and mac and cheese.

name: The Wolseley Piccadilly
description: Sprawling Piccadilly grand café running with a constant, energetic hum from morning through dinner. Waiters carry plates of Wiener schnitzel and steak tartare across black-and-white marble floors under soaring domed ceilings.

name: Bistro Freddie
description: Old-school Shoreditch corner bistro pairing hearty British-French cooking with an all-French wine list. Candles burn in empty bottles around a wood-paneled dining room serving shared pies and large cuts of fire-cooked meat.

name: Casse-Croûte
description: Tiny Bermondsey corner bistro with 20 seats, red gingham tablecloths, and tables pushed close together. The daily blackboard menu sticks to three classic French starters, mains, and desserts paired with an all-French wine list.

name: Alain Ducasse at The Dorchester
description: Bright Dorchester dining room serving contemporary French haute cuisine. Multi-course tasting menus stretch past the three-hour mark, turning dinner into a formal procession of seasonal plates, heavy silver, and serious wine pairings.

name: Caviar House Piccadilly
description: Airy Piccadilly dining room and seafood bar serving high-grade caviar and Balik smoked salmon alongside chilled vodka. Decadent seafood dinners and champagne fill marble tables and oat banquettes under Art Deco lights.

name: Crisp W1
description: Buzzing basement pizzeria beneath a restored Mayfair pub turning out thin-crust New York-style pies. Lines form early for the tight tables, signature garlic dip, and proper pints of Guinness pouring steadily upstairs.

name: The Drapers Arms
description: Neighborhood gastropub offering shabby-chic styling with a courtyard garden. Ample beer and wine selections. The reason to visit, though, is the Sunday roast dinner - here, reviews of the British classic are consistently high.

name: Battersea
description: A London neighborhood on the rise - perhaps having flown under the radar due to its previous lack of a tube station. Wander the southern banks of the Thames, visit the New Covent Garden Flower Market, and note the art deco power station.

name: A Bar with Shapes for a Name
description: A bar without bottles and with shapes for a name. The reimagining of a modern cocktail lounge, "Shapes" serves pre-batched drinks in non-descript bottles within a functional-minimalist environment. Highly celebrated.

name: Jolene Redchurch Street
description: Tiny Shoreditch corner bakery serving heritage-grain sourdough and daily pastries through a large open sash window. Filter coffee and warm sausage rolls go straight to the sidewalk benches until the daily bake sells out.

name: Bilmonte
description: Compact Soho gelateria serving traditional Italian ice cream and gelato-stuffed brioche buns. Flavors are ordered from a wall menu instead of a display case, and usually taken to go with a chocolate-filled mini cone on top.

name: Merton Abbey Mills
description: Historic riverside textile mills turned open-air village of independent pubs, eateries, and craft workshops. Live music and outdoor drinking fill the brick pathways around a working Victorian water wheel.

name: The Jackalope
description: Historic Marylebone mews pub pouring independent craft beer alongside fiery Sichuan street food. A basement kitchen slings spicy Chongqing noodles, handing out pagers that buzz when bowls are ready to take up to the wood-paneled snugs.

name: Black Radish Restaurant
description: Twelve-seat dining room operating out of a historic riverside mill. The chef-owner cooks a fixed Anglo-French tasting menu just steps from the wooden tables, running the room with the intimacy of a private dinner party.

name: Cafe Seek
description: Tiny Canary Wharf patisserie pairing French technique with Japanese flavors. The eight-seat corner room runs mostly on takeaway, serving ceremonial matcha and mentaiko baguettes until the morning bake sells out.

name: Mori Homemade London
description: Quiet Japanese cafe pouring traditionally whisked matcha and slicing homemade Basque cheesecakes. A notebook on the counter collects song requests, and the daily batch of pretzel buns sells out by late afternoon.

name: Dishoom King's Cross
description: Proven Indian cuisine in a Bombay-style setting. Alongside its King's Cross restaurant, Dishoom has locations throughout London. A place to order in bulk and share amongst friends. Open morning till night.

name: Katsute100 Covent Garden
description: Minimalist Japanese teahouse tucked into a second-floor corner of the Covent Garden Uniqlo. The small, timber-slatted room and outdoor terrace stay busy pouring premium matcha and slicing handmade crepe cakes.

name: Uzbek Corner Queensway
description: Tiny, hard-to-find dining room in Queensway Market serving hearty plates of traditional plov and steamed manti. Uzbek television plays in the background of the snug, family-run space.

name: Ronnie Scott's
description: Historic Soho jazz club running nightly live shows in a dimly lit, wood-paneled room. Small dining tables crowd around the stage, keeping the space tight and the attention squarely on the music.

name: Whole Foods Market
description: Sprawling organic supermarket spanning three floors of an Art Deco building on Kensington High Street. Ground-floor hot bars run steady for lunch, with meals weighed out and eaten by the windows or up in the massive food hall.

name: The Zetter Clerkenwell
description: Maximalist Clerkenwell townhouse hotel packed with heavy antiques, rich fabrics, and vintage oddities. Deep-hued bedrooms sit just above a busy ground-floor parlor pouring cocktails late into the night.

name: Night Tales
description: Hybrid Hackney nightlife space built into two former railway arches. A massive heated terrace handles early cocktails and pizza, while the main room pushes house and disco sets through a heavy sound system.

name: Queensway Market
description: Dense indoor warren of independent stalls tucked behind a yellow Bayswater storefront. Narrow aisles run past busy electronics repair counters and tiny kitchens slinging Malaysian and Uzbek street food.

name: Allpress Coffee Roasters Dalston
description: Converted 1930s joinery factory running as a bright, open-plan café and active coffee roastery. The vaulted dining room sits alongside the working roasters behind glass, serving house espresso and toasted banana bread.

name: Chocolatine Bakery
description: Busy Walthamstow bakery turning out 48-hour sourdough and laminated French pastries from an open kitchen. The tiny shop has just two seats and runs as a steady morning takeaway stop for coffee and pistachio palmiers.

name: Five Guys Burgers and Fries Piccadilly Circus
description: Multi-level burger shop running a high-volume lunch operation just off Piccadilly Circus. The open kitchen slings made-to-order burgers and heavy scoops of peanut-oil fries straight into brown paper bags.

name: The Marquee Moon
description: Two-story Dalston pub shifting from early dinners into loud, late-night DJ sets. East Asian pub plates and natural wine take up the ground floor, while a low-lit basement cocktail lounge runs late on a hi-fi sound system.

name: The Snapery East
description: Quiet railway arch bakery off London Fields turning out sourdough and Danish pastries made with regenerative flour. The calm space runs steady through the morning with a heated courtyard, coffee, and fresh loaves cooling on mobile racks.

name: Drake's
description: The Saville Row company rose as a tiemaker, but has since expanded. Drake's now offers a more complete vision of menswear, though they do remain loyal to their handcrafted tie-making process. Timeless elegance is the philosophy here.

name: Dinings
description: Book early for this Japanese venue - 28-seats isn't many, and they fill up fast. Founded by former Nobu chefs, the food is well-honed and comprises fresh European produce. The Wagyu beef and Tar-Tar chips get plenty of attention.

name: Hang-Up Gallery
description: Independent Hoxton gallery on Regent's Canal, dealing in Banksy prints and blue-chip contemporary art. The appointment-only space has five-meter ceilings and bright natural light for quiet, private viewings.

name: Labour and Wait
description: Homeware store with curated items that champion functional design and everyday use. The products - from hardware and stationery, to books and bathroom - are sourced from all over the world. Timeless designs are the ethos here.

name: Old Shades
description: Narrow Victorian pub on Whitehall pouring British ales under a stained-glass cupola. The wood-paneled bar runs steady with casual pints, leading back to a dining room busy with Sunday roasts and long group lunches.

name: Guinness Open Gate Brewery London
description: Massive Covent Garden microbrewery pouring site-exclusive experimental pints alongside the classic stout. The multi-level setup runs from a casual courtyard serving beef cheek pies up to a polished rooftop oyster bar.

name: Brat x Climpson's Arch
description: Lively, marquee-covered courtyard under a London Fields railway arch with a central open-fire kitchen. Wooden tables fill with Basque-style sharing plates like whole grilled turbot, juicy beef ribs, and burnt cheesecake.

name: Dean Street Townhouse
description: Whilst bedrooms at Dean Street Townhouse are Soho House members only, tables in its restaurant are not. A place for sophisticated lunches and dinners - perhaps a negroni at the bar too. Really though, the venue fits most occasions.

name: Ducksoup
description: Soho-based wine bar and restaurant cooking seasonal eats from an everchanging menu. The dishes are diverse and pair well with the venue's selection of wine vintages. Embrace the intimate atmosphere for dinner and drinks.

name: Dumpling Shack
description: Popular market stall serving dumplings, noodles, and soups - all handmade. Quick-serve and vibey; visitors order via a tablet before collecting their goods. Dumpling Shack also has a location at South Quay.

name: Hampstead Heath Ponds
description: When the heat beckons, there are few places in London to take a refreshing dip - hence the popularity of Hampstead Heath's open air ponds. The area makes for a great day out even when the waters are a little too chilly for swimming.

name: The River Café
description: Recognized for its Michelin star and history of notable chefs, this restaurant serves Italian cuisine in a riverside location. Book an outdoor table for an alfresco lunch of fresh pasta - try something sweet afterward, too.

name: Forza Wine Soho
description: High-energy Soho dining room pouring natural wine and serving casual Italian plates. Close tables and loud music keep the room moving fast straight through the night.

name: London Aquatics Centre
description: Designed by the late Zaha Hadid for the 2012 Olympics, the concept of this building is inspired by moving water. The complex offers public swimming access, as well as swimming and diving lessons. There is also a commercial gym onsite.

name: Brasserie Angelica
description: 1920s-inspired Fitzrovia brasserie serving modern European live-fire dishes. Leather banquettes face a frosted glass wall revealing chef silhouettes at work, and a spiral staircase leads down to a basement cocktail bar.

name: Noble Rot Lamb's Conduit
description: Wood-paneled Bloomsbury wine bar pouring rare vintages in fine stemware. The 1701 townhouse splits between a bright front bar for casual glasses and a dark, moody back room serving French-English plates.

name: 2 Willow Road
description: Today, passers-by wouldn't bat an eyelid at this modernist structure. But, back in 1939, Ernö Goldfinger's innovative design was the source of much controversy. Now, his home exists as a national monument, and is open to the public.

name: Dishoom Permit Room Portobello
description: Victorian pub turned Bombay-style restaurant and drinking den on Portobello Road. The lively ground floor runs on cocktails and carrom, while the calmer upstairs dining room serves shared plates of black daal and chicken ruby.

name: Aces Foodcraft
description: Intimate, pale wood Fitzrovia dining room built entirely around a large open kitchen. Chefs pass plates and explain dishes directly across the nine-seat counter, serving an evening tasting menu of British produce and Japanese technique.

name: Tamila Soho
description: Polished Soho dining room serving modern Tamil curries, fresh dosas, and made-to-order roti. Spiced cocktails and shared plates land on marble tables across the ground floor, while a dark plum basement below holds larger groups.

name: Barbican Centre
description: Home to the London Symphony Orchestra, the Barbican is an icon of London arts and culture, comprising a theater, exhibition venues, restaurants, and a library. Plus, the building is a delectable example of Brutalist architecture.

name: Bread & Bean
description: Family-run café offering everything from barista coffees and breakfast croissants to hearty brunches and filling sandwiches. There are lots of vegan or non-dairy options available too. A friendly and relaxed environment.

name: Egg
description: An upmarket boutique snug between the whitewash buildings of Belgravia. With an international customer base, they offer womenswear, linens, home goods, and handcrafted ceramics. Great gifts and incredibly knowledgeable staff.

name: The Waterman's Arms
description: Restored historic pub on the Isle of Dogs, now a smart, split-level space with exposed brick and a fireplace. Elevated British classics come from the kitchen – book ahead for the Sunday roast – and seven boutique rooms are upstairs.

name: Lisboa Patisserie
description: Traditional Portuguese bakery on Golborne Road serving fresh pastel de nata and strong espresso. The simple room and sidewalk tables stay busy from morning until the custard tarts sell out.

name: Maureen Paley
description: Contemporary art gallery set in industrial spaces across Bethnal Green and Shoreditch. Clean, modern rooms show work from major international artists and anchor the East End gallery circuit.

name: Carbon Kopi
description: Light-filled Hammersmith corner cafe pouring New Zealand-style flat whites and pressing thick sourdough toasties. Laptops cover the pale wood tables through the morning until the daily batch of pastries sells out.

name: Algerian Coffee Stores
description: Tiny Soho coffee shop packed with floor-to-ceiling jars and the heavy scent of freshly roasted beans. The original 19th-century wooden counter turns out quick takeaway espresso alongside dozens of global varieties ground to order.

name: Rasputin's
description: Red-lit London Fields bar glowing from small TVs playing spaghetti westerns. Bartenders sling hot dogs, cold beer, and five-olive martinis under hanging bags of potato chips.

name: 107 Wine Bar
description: Natural wine bar built around a single communal table, creating an intimate dinner party feel. Guests pick bottles straight from the shelves – the menu changes constantly with a rotating guest chef.

name: Natura
description: Cozy, wood-lined Hackney Wick dining room serving stone-baked pizzas and fresh pastas to a steady neighborhood crowd. Long tables fill up with locals sharing large plates for casual group dinners and birthdays.

name: Kaffeine
description: Specialty espresso bar and café influenced by Aussie and Kiwi coffee cultures. A rotating menu of pastries, salads, and sandwiches pair well with any artisanal brew. Order a coffee flight for a more refined tasting experience.

name: Rogues.
description: Intimate Hackney Road dining room serving a daily-changing set menu of modern British sharing plates. Bare concrete walls and mismatched wooden tables keep the room relaxed for seasonal cooking and natural wine.

name: The Black Pig
description: Borough Market stall slinging massive ciabatta sandwiches loaded with slow-roasted pork, slaw, and truffle mayonnaise. Fast-moving lines lead to rich, filling lunches eaten standing up in the crowded aisles.

name: Rain Dogs Bar
description: Moody Shoreditch dive bar pouring refined cocktails and pints of Guinness in a dark, rustic room. The space stays loud late into the weekend with live blues, indie playlists, and upgraded snacks like fried chicken scotch eggs.

name: City of London
description: The City of London is where London originally developed within the Roman city walls. It is now one of the world's most important financial centers, and an area where modern skyscrapers wedge in next to medieval churches.

name: Willy's Pies
description: Railway arch kitchen from a St John alum, reviving the traditional British pie with seasonal, high-quality fillings. The deep-filled pies are sold frozen – a restaurant-quality classic meant for the home oven.

name: Henley Royal Regatta
description: A world-famous sporting event, the Henley Royal Regatta features over 300 races across six days of competition. The regatta draws large crowds and boasts a lively atmosphere - dress to impress and enjoy the event's races.

name: Cinder - Belsize Park
description: Warm Belsize Park dining room cooking everything over an open wood fire. The tight space stays loud and busy as charred flatbreads and smoky roasted meats hit close-packed tables.

name: Yuki bar
description: Compact Japanese wine bar pouring low-intervention bottles alongside izakaya-style small plates. Vinyl records spin steadily in the dimly lit room over relaxed evening meals.

name: Malaysian Deli
description: Cozy Brockley dining room serving generous plates of traditional Kelantan cooking. Batik-covered tables fill with slow-cooked rendang and blue nasi kerabu during the BYOB dinner service.

name: St Giles Cripplegate
description: Medieval stone church sitting right in the middle of the concrete Barbican Estate. The restored, light-filled sanctuary pairs quiet daily services with a steady lineup of classical concerts.

name: Portobello Garden Arcade Italian
description: Neapolitan spot tucked away from the Portobello market crowds, serving massive wood-fired pizzas. The open oven is the room's focal point – watch the chefs at work from the simple, honest dining room.

name: The Palomar
description: Family-owned restaurant serving modern Middle Eastern cuisine in Central London. Think harissa chicken, kubaneh bread, and delicate seafood. Make a reservation, as queues for the 16-seat chef's counter are common.

name: Primeur
description: Small plates with robust flavors and quality ingredients, served in a communal setting. The space features an open, airy design with counter and communal table seating.

name: Kristina Records
description: Kristina Records may be an unassuming store in a trendy part of town, but it is most inviting to those who decide to enter. Take your time browsing through the selection of mostly underground dance music - beer or coffee in-hand.

name: House of MoMo
description: Cozy Nepalese spot dishing up traditional Himalayan dumplings and generous platters of goat curry. Expect a queue outside – the entire party must be present before anyone is seated.

name: Sticks'n'Sushi
description: Dimly lit, two-story Covent Garden dining room blending Scandi minimalism with raw walls and oak counters. Large sharing platters pair fresh sushi with hot yakitori sticks from the grill.

name: Elliot's
description: Wood-fired European cuisine served in a shabby-chic aesthetic. Alongside its Borough Market venue, Elliot's has a restaurant in Hackney. Both locations offer impressive wine lists to pair with their seasonal menus.

name: Kruk
description: Bustling Peckham railway arch and gravel courtyard serving unapologetically spicy Thai food. The menu splits straight down the middle, mirroring hand-pounded meat curries with exact plant-based versions alongside draft Singha.

name: BRAT Restaurant
description: Rustic Spanish restaurant with amazing wine recommendations. The kitchen takes influence from Basque-style cooking and prepares dishes over an open wood fire grill. Good food and stellar service in a stylish locale.

name: Skehans
description: Family-run Irish pub on a Nunhead corner pairing steady pints of Guinness with a long-standing Thai kitchen. Live music runs six nights a week, filling the dark-wood front bar and spilling out into the tiered back garden.

name: The Pyrotechnist's Arms
description: Traditional Nunhead pub with a central 1930s island bar, familiar keg beers, and a busy pool table. The single blue room hosts a steady rotation of casual weekend parties, pool games, and laid-back evening pints.

name: Lahore Karahi
description: Bustling Tooting curry house serving rich Pakistani karahi in a bright, no-frills dining room. Grills run hot by the front door while large groups pack the tables with heavy plates of lamb chops and their own bottles of beer.

name: Berenjak Mayfair
description: Polished Persian dining room pairing the communal warmth of a Tehran kabab house with dark woods and ornate tilework. An open kitchen turns out charcoal-grilled meats and fresh tandoor breads for long, shared dinners.

name: Fostok Halab
description: Syrian supermarket in Acton stocking aisles of Middle Eastern pantry staples, fresh produce, and halal meat. A busy counter past the butcher serves fresh shawarma and warm fatayer to go.

name: Templeton Garden
description: Quiet townhouse hotel built around a leafy garden courtyard – a true oasis in Kensington. The rooms are calming retreats with Le Labo toiletries; a neighborhood restaurant and cocktail bar are downstairs.

name: Thenga Cafe
description: Canteen-style cafe inside the Central YMCA serving home-cooked, vegan Bengali food. The daily-changing menu always centers on the thali – a selection of curries and sides served on a metal tray.

name: Burger & Beyond
description: Burger joint built around thick, dry-aged beef patties from native-breed cattle. The rest of the menu is pure American indulgence: bone marrow gravy fries, dirty tots, and boozy milkshakes.

name: Café Deco
description: Bloomsbury-based eatery pairing hearty cuisine with fine wines. Expect modern European cuisine. Open for both lunch and dinner - have a seat outside when the weather allows, or simply enjoy the laidback interior.

name: Carmela's Pizzeria
description: Low-lit Islington pizzeria slinging crispy, foldable New York-style pies. Tables turn fast over tight booking slots as vodka sauce pizzas land alongside hot maple and Calabrian chili ricotta for dunking torn crusts.

name: Its Not Big Dough
description: Neapolitan pizza stall running out of a shipping container on a Walthamstow industrial estate. The kitchen sits right outside the Pretty Decent Beer Co. taproom, pairing cold-fermented pizzas with craft pints at communal tables.

name: Breadstall Clapham
description: Permanent Northcote Road stall slinging crunchy, 72-hour fermented pizza by the quarter-slice or whole pie. Standing tables with checkered cloths sit right on the street for a quick meal with a cold beer and crust dips.

name: Do Not Disturb (DND Bar)
description: Hidden cocktail bar under the Vintry & Mercer hotel serving barrel-aged drinks and small plates. Velvet chairs and leather banquettes fill the dark, 1920s-style room as early happy hours stretch into quiet date nights.

name: Bravi Ragazzi
description: Small corner pizzeria in Streatham baking wood-fired Neapolitan sourdough pies. The tight dining room stays warm from the oven, sending out blistered Margheritas, fried calzones, and potato croquettes.

name: The Pilgrm Hotel Paddington
description: Restored Victorian townhouse hotel skipping the traditional lobby for a ground-floor coffee counter. A grand original staircase connects the all-day lounge to pared-back rooms finished with reclaimed wood and Marshall speakers.

name: Forza Wine Peckham
description: Rooftop bar pouring natural wine and serving Italian small plates high above Rye Lane. The open terrace runs busy through the evening for sunset skyline views and steady drinking.

name: Poppies Fish & Chips
description: Retro fish and chip shop serving massive portions of battered cod and thick-cut chips. Vintage jukeboxes and 1950s memorabilia fill the busy dining room, while a separate counter handles a steady stream of to-go orders.

name: Ottolenghi Spitalfields
description: Lively Middle Eastern dining room near Old Spitalfields Market serving vibrant, vegetable-forward shared plates. Signature cakes line the entrance counter while walk-ins settle at the cocktail bar.

name: Mahali Bakery by Mahali and Co
description: Compact Battersea bakery making pastries with Southeast Asian ingredients like pandan, sambal, and miso. Seating is tight, so weekend takeaway boxes and matcha lattes head straight for the grass in nearby Battersea Park.

name: Dover Street Counter
description: Glossy Mayfair diner pairing elevated American comfort food with a heavy 90s R&B soundtrack. The long stainless steel counter faces an open kitchen turning out cheeseburgers, disco fries, and cold margaritas under warm amber lamps.

name: The Tavern on the Hill
description: Spacious Walthamstow pub pouring local East London pints alongside hand-pressed burgers and Jamaican plates. Huge outdoor seating wraps around the old brick building, running steady through live music nights and weekend roasts.

name: Hoover Building
description: Originally the UK headquarters for The Hoover Company, the Hoover Building is now one of the finest art deco landmarks in London. Since ceasing operations, the building has served as a supermarket and an apartment complex.

name: Fischer's
description: A Viennese restaurant on Marylebone High Street. With a menu and interior design to evoke a traditional Austrian ambiance - chopped liver, kasespatzle, and wiener schnitzel headline the classic dishes.

name: Osteria Vibrato
description: Old-school Soho Italian dining room with red leather banquettes and white tablecloths. Waiters in cream linen suits work the loud, busy floor, serving daily-rolled pasta and pouring from a deep organic wine list.

name: Cambridge Folk Festival
description: One of the longest-running folk festivals in the world, having been founded in 1965. Music is the primary focus, but the event also brings together an eclectic mix of artists and creatives. Food and drink options throughout.

name: Finsbury Park
description: Quietly trendy neighborhood in North London. With its offering of green space and music festivals, the titular Finsbury Park is the area's primary allure. Though a mix of tree-lined streets and fresh eateries also draws ample foot traffic.

name: Bethnal Green
description: Bethnal Green strikes that perfect balance between gritty East End neighborhood and almost-but-not-quite-yet trendy hot spot. Its multicultural make-up gives it a warm, welcoming vibe that you won't find in the city center.

name: BFI London Film Festival
description: The country's largest film festival, the BFI event spans two weeks in October and showcases hundreds of works from filmmakers all over the world. While the event is heavily attended by industry professionals, it is also open to the public.

name: EQUAL PARTS
description: Low-lit Hackney Road cocktail bar pouring equal-measure drinks to a steady vinyl soundtrack. The intimate, wood-paneled room runs on European amaros, agave spirits, and savory martinis mixed behind a bronze mirrored bar.

name: Below Stone Nest
description: Raw, candlelit Soho basement bar pouring highballs and classic cocktails under a former chapel. Loud, live jazz and soul sessions regularly pack the bare concrete, walk-in-only room.

name: Scarfes Bar
description: Plush hotel cocktail bar built around a roaring fireplace, velvet armchairs, and shelves of antique books. Live jazz plays nightly while bartenders mix inventive cocktails under marble walls covered in bold caricatures.

name: Brixton
description: Day or night, Brixton is spirited and colourful - a microcosm of London. The setting of cultural diversity and historical riots. The inspiration behind songs and artists. Go for the vibrant night life and live events.

name: Rogue Sarnies
description: Bethnal Green sandwich shop serving rich, messy fillings on house-baked, wood-fired rolls. Orders run through a self-service kiosk, with a few standing tables and outdoor seats available before the daily specials sell out.

name: Kricket Soho
description: Lively modern Indian restaurant serving seasonal sharing plates from a busy open kitchen. Pink stools sit at the ground-floor counter facing the chefs, with Keralan fried chicken and samphire pakoras coming out to soul and funk music.

name: Kung Fu Mama
description: Tiny Covent Garden noodle bar serving quick bowls of Taiwanese sun-dried noodles and bao. The nine-seat room stays packed, running on fast walk-in turnover rather than lingering dinners.

name: Molly Mc's
description: Lively Irish pub under Waterloo railway arches with live trad music playing through the weekend. Pints of Guinness and Irish spice bags cover the tables in the main room, while vintage-styled snugs double as private karaoke spaces.

name: Fitzrovia
description: Central district where cobblestone side streets separate Victorian-brick buildings. Flush with galleries, old-school pubs, and creative agencies. The bohemian borough is one of London's safest, and offers easy access to the West End.

name: Paddy Wok
description: Deptford food counter slinging massive portions of Irish-Chinese takeaway classics. Heaping salt and chilli spice bags and curry-drenched 3-in-1s land on tables across a shared Creekside space with a pool table in the back.

name: Grocery Post - West Hampstead
description: Modern neighborhood grocery stocking daily provisions alongside premium pantry goods from producers like Neal's Yard and Ottolenghi. The espresso counter serves Ozone coffee and fresh pastries to tables out on the sidewalk.

name: The Parakeet Pub
description: Restored Victorian pub in Kentish Town split between a wood-paneled front bar and a busy back dining room. The open kitchen cooks seasonal dishes over a live fire grill, serving steaks and whole fish alongside pints and biodynamic wines.

name: Hampstead Heath
description: Where sports, recreation, and nature meet - the largest area of common land in the capital. The park that inspired C.S. Lewis to write The Chronicles of Narnia, and a the subject of many of Constable's finest paintings.

name: Camden Town
description: At the forefront of London's counterculture movement. True alternative sights might be few nowadays, but Camden Town still attacks the senses. Shadowed music venues, market stalls, vintage shops, street food courtyards - its heart on.

name: GAIL's Bakery High Street Kensington
description: Bright, two-story bakery serving handmade sourdough, fresh morning pastries, and espresso. The fast-moving counter handles quick takeaway for nearby Holland Park, while a quiet lower level has tables for casual breakfasts.

name: Honey & Co. | Lamb's Conduit Street
description: Light-filled Middle Eastern dining room on a pedestrian corner with wide windows, Moorish floor tiles, and terrace tables. The kitchen turns out slow-cooked lamb, fresh mezze, and feta and honey cheesecake on a kadaif base.

name: Bar Kroketa
description: Loud, fast-paced Spanish bar serving a rotating blackboard menu of croquetas. The narrow room runs on counter seating, tight tables, and steady pours of vermouth and sherry.

name: Blueprint Coffee Tooting
description: Compact Tooting coffee shop pulling specialty espresso and pouring matcha alongside slices of carrot cake. Baristas memorize morning orders while neighborhood dogs wait by the counter.

name: Gagosian
description: Vast contemporary art gallery in Mayfair staging museum-scale solo exhibitions from major international artists. Four interconnected, double-height rooms with fumed oak floors hold monumental works in a quiet, spacious layout.

name: All Nations Vegan House
description: Family-run Dalston takeaway counter serving generous portions of plant-based Caribbean stews and grains. The hot menu shifts daily, with massive Around the World bowls packing in a sample of everything for the road.

name: Jerk Shepherd
description: Peckham Caribbean takeout counter running a traditional jerk pan for 24-hour marinated chicken and lamb. Fresh curry goat and massive stuffed dumplings go straight into heavy to-go boxes.

name: Umana Yana
description: Tiny Guyanese takeaway in Herne Hill wrapping hot curries in fresh, handmade rotis. Parcels of slow-cooked goat, oxtail, or pumpkin dhal puri cross the small counter, bound straight for nearby Brockwell Park.

name: The Serpentine
description: Curving 40-acre lake in the middle of Hyde Park, surrounded by flat walking paths, picnic spots, and waterfront cafes. Sunny afternoons bring long lines for pedal boats, while open-water swimmers stick to the summer lido.

name: Simpson's in the Strand
description: Grand, wood-paneled dining room with leather banquettes and crystal chandeliers. Staff wheel antique silver trolleys across the floor, carving aged Scottish roast beef and serving Yorkshire puddings right at the table.

name: Jay Dee's Catering
description: No-frills Caribbean takeaway in North Kensington with the smell of jerk chicken drifting into the street. The family-run, cash-only spot has zero seating, handing massive portions of oxtail and goat curry over the counter to go.

name: Victoria Miro
description: Victoria Miro is a British contemporary art gallery run by its namesake director. The space represents a variety of established and emerging artists. Be warned, the entrance of the gallery can be easily mistaken for an apartment.

name: Today Bread
description: Bright Walthamstow bakery and cafe serving slow-fermented sourdough, cardamom buns, and daily brunch plates. Open laptops and coffee cups cover the indoor tables while fresh loaves line the front counter.

name: Scarlett Green
description: Bright, art-covered Soho dining room running a high-energy Australian breakfast service. Marble tables fill fast with heavy plates of shakshouka, bacon rolls, and bottles of prosecco left right on the table.

name: Broadway Market
description: Market with more than 120 traders selling their wares, from freshly baked goods, to flowers and vintage gems. Grab a Saturday morning breakfast here, or at any one of the cafes that line the market street.

name: Supernova
description: Purist smash burger spot serving a deliberately short menu of two burgers, fries, and a sundae. Service is fast and the open kitchen is loud; expect a queue at peak times.

name: Tiny Wine Bar & Shop
description: Compact Fitzrovia wine bar pouring small-producer bottles alongside fresh Peruvian ceviche. The tight, glass-fronted room serves citrus-cured seafood and shared tostadas to match the drinks.

name: Half Cut Market
description: Neighborhood wine bar and bottle shop pouring low-intervention labels alongside charcoal-grilled small plates. Shelves of retail wine line the cozy dining room, ready to open at the table or take home.

name: Bonne Route
description: Cosy, dimly lit neighborhood wine bar and bottle shop keeping things strictly walk-in. The small room fills up fast for glasses of orange wine and Puglian Primitivo alongside cheese boards and sliced charcuterie.

name: Authentique - Epicerie & Bar
description: Tufnell Park wine bar and deli pouring regional French bottles alongside charcuterie boards and rotating hot plates. The cozy dining room handles evening drinks and Thursday jazz, opening into a covered rear garden.

name: E5 Bakehouse
description: Community-centric bakery that specializes in artisanal bread, cakes, and organic lunches. Spacious within, and with a sunny patio out the back, this spot is great for a sit-down coffee or light lunch. Expect queues, but they move fast.

name: Hauser & Wirth
description: Mayfair contemporary art gallery operating from a 1922 banking hall. Rich timber paneling lines two massive, column-free rooms holding large-scale modern installations, with an art bookshop leading into the south gallery.

name: Choosing Keeping
description: Wood-paneled Seven Dials stationery shop dealing in rare Japanese paper, glass pens, and Italian scissors. Artisanal desk tools fill the antique cabinets, with weekend queues regularly spilling out the Victorian storefront.

name: Hayward Gallery
description: A gallery 🖼️ known for its contemporary art shows, exhibitions, and brutalist architecture. It has featured work by legendary textile artist Louise Bourgeois 🕷️, Igshaan Adams 🇿🇦, and the LGBTQIA+ 🏳️‍🌈 community and its artists.

name: Borough Market
description: If visiting a market in the city, make it this one. With a history dating back to 1756, Borough Market has long thrived at the center of the London community. One of the city's best locales for fresh produce and multicultural street food.

name: COYA Mayfair
description: Jewel-toned Mayfair dining room serving modern Peruvian plates alongside Pisco infusions and loud music. Meals start with tableside guacamole and fresh ceviche before DJs turn the space into a heavy party late into the night.

name: The New Craftsmen
description: A furniture store that sells contemporary objects representing a community of skilled artisans. The showroom offers regular events to give interested visitors the chance to learn first-hand from makers.

name: Dal Fiorentino Hoxton
description: Fast-paced Florentine sandwich shop running steady through the lunch rush with made-to-order schiacciata. Fresh-baked Tuscan flatbreads are loaded at the counter with sliced mortadella, whole burrata, and pistachio pesto.

name: Dal Fiorentino Fitzrovia
description: Fitzrovia sandwich counter serving fresh-baked Florentine schiacciata. Staff slice the crisp, salty flatbreads to order, stacking them with mortadella, whole burrata, and pistachio pesto for a fast lunch.

name: Wapping
description: A former docks area that has undergone extensive redevelopment post-WWII. What used to be a neighborhood known for pirates and executions now offers coffee shops, Thames trails, and historic pubs.

name: Saatchi Yates
description: Massive, bright contemporary art gallery running large-scale exhibitions across two floors in St. James's. The open ground level shows emerging talent, while the lower floor holds established blue-chip works.

name: WatchHouse Millennium Bridge
description: Spacious specialty coffee shop sitting just off the Millennium Bridge. Sculptural interiors hold quiet corners for catching up over flat whites and filter coffee away from the riverside rush.

name: Kettner's
description: Historic Georgian townhouse hotel with quiet, 1920s-inspired rooms and a classic French restaurant. Downstairs, the Champagne Bar channels the building's past with low lighting and a discreet buzz.

name: Bottarga
description: Intimate King’s Road bistro serving modern Greek sharing plates. Narrow tables crowd with spicy feta, orzo, and whole grilled fish under low candlelight.

name: Kervan Sofrasi - Wood Green
description: Massive Turkish grill house running full-tilt across two floors. The open kitchen churns out charcoal-fired platters of lamb ribs and chicken shish that barely fit on the tables.

name: Charco Charco Yakiniku
description: Glossy Holborn dining room mixing sushi with tabletop BBQ. Inset charcoal grills sear premium Wagyu and seafood right at the table – a smoky, interactive meal that stays lively late into the evening.

name: Beigel Bake Brick Lane Bakery
description: Brick Lane institution. Generously-filled bagels available at all hours of the day - breakfast, lunch break, or post-night out. The salted beef takes center stage but the salmon and cream cheese is also a popular choice. Takeaway only.

name: Shoreditch
description: Shoreditch is one of London's most lively neighborhoods - known for its hipsters, young creatives, and multicultural community. There is no shortage of interest here: from its vintage stores to the curry houses of Brick Lane and beyond.

name: Victoria Park
description: The largest park in Tower Hamlets, the green space comprises a lake, playgrounds, sports facilities, flowerbeds, and two cafes. The popular park is also used as a concert venue and hosts many festivals each year.

name: South Kensington-Chelsea
description: Known for its museums but also for its variety of restaurants that appeal to any tastebud. Highlights include the Natural History Museum and Royal Albert Hall. One of the most affluent and densely populated boroughs in London.

name: Tarantella
description: Rustic Chiswick trattoria run by a husband-and-wife team from Puglia. An open kitchen anchors the split-level room, turning out regional pastas, pizzas, and giant tiramisu.

name: Sông Quê - Phở Bar
description: Commercial Street sibling to the Kingsland Road legend, pairing family-recipe phở with a serious cocktail bar. Deep bowls of rare beef broth sit next to Pandan Negronis across two polished floors.

name: JUNK MARYLEBONE
description: Stark, stainless steel joint in St Christopher’s Place serving French-founded smash burgers. The short menu sticks to stacked patties on brioche and thick Puffy cookies.

name: Bun & Sum
description: Industrial estate kitchen in Bow slinging LA-style smash burgers on imported potato rolls. Outdoor benches and parked cars serve as the primary dining room for the messy, jus-dipped stacks.

name: Jupiter Burger
description: Space-age shack in Netil Market serving California-style smash burgers on Martin’s Potato Rolls. The menu stays tight with beef or veg patties and twice-cooked fries, served at a few counter stools or to go.

name: Monster Burger BBQ & Grill House London
description: Narrow, high-energy Whitechapel spot slinging massive portions of halal American grill staples. Tables turn over quickly as crowds tackle 28-day aged rump steaks and Angus burgers spiked with house Naga sauce.

name: Simply Smashed - Quality Smash Burgers
description: Halal smash burger joint in Stepney Green stacking crispy Wagyu patties and heavy trays of loaded fries. Fast service and a boxing arcade machine keep the energy high.

name: The Hart - Marylebone
description: Classic corner pub with a proper bar on the ground floor and candlelit dining rooms upstairs. The open kitchen serves seasonal British fare – from classic pork pies to lamb chops and steak.

name: The Culpeper
description: Drink at the ground-floor pub, dine in the first-floor restaurant, stay on the second floor, and spend some time in the rooftop garden. A quadruple-threat location with everything needed for an enjoyable stay in London's East End.

name: Soho
description: The heart of London's entertainment industry, from the world-famous West End to an abundance of nightclubs and bars. Carnaby Street is another of the neighborhood's highlights - a pedestrianized street known for its boutiques and eateries.

name: Mount St. Restaurant
description: Gallery-grade dining room sitting above a Mayfair pub, paved with a commissioned mosaic and hung with genuine Warhols. Rich British classics like lobster pie land on the tables.

name: The Monocle Café
description: Café space serving barista-style coffees and international dishes - think Scandinavian pastries, classic sandwiches, and udon bowls. The space offers cozy seating as well as as the latest Monocle magazine.

name: Peter Harrington
description: Rare book dealer of first editions and manuscripts where browsing is genuinely encouraged. Quiet, gallery-style rooms hold immaculate literary history behind glass, from medieval works to signed modern classics.

name: Stir Coffee Brixton
description: Brixton Hill spot rotating through guest beans in a bright, high-ceilinged space. Locals and laptop workers pack the brick-lined back for Reubens and thick slices of banana bread.

name: The Thin White Duke
description: Moody Soho bar channeling Bowie’s Berlin era with industrial brick and low lights. Creative cocktails pair with baskets of dim sum, while a members-only recording studio hides downstairs.

name: Huxley-Parlour
description: Mayfair gallery spread across two spaces with a heavy emphasis on 20th-century photography. Shows mix archival giants like Vivian Maier with new painting and sculpture.

name: Reubens Deli & Restaurant
description: West End kosher staple piles salt beef high on rye. A street-level counter covers takeaway, while the retro downstairs dining room handles heavy plates of schnitzel and latkes.

name: SeeWoo
description: Chinatown supermarket spanning four storefronts of narrow, stacked aisles. Stairs lead to a basement wet market with fresh butchery counters and tanks of live crab and lobster.

name: BLACK CACTUS BBQ
description: Texas-style barbecue kitchen inside the Burnt Faith Brandy House. Offset smokers turn out brisket and burnt ends until sold out, with tables set in view of the large copper stills.

name: Wing Yip Superstore Cricklewood
description: Cavernous warehouse for pan-Asian groceries and live seafood sits under a green-tiled pagoda roof. Grocery runs often end at the busy on-site dim sum restaurant or the canteen slinging roast duck.

name: Prince Alfred
description: Grand Victorian pub anchored by a rare 1898 peninsula bar. Timber and etched glass "snob screens" radiate outward, creating five intimate compartments for ales and Sunday roasts.

name: Timothy Taylor
description: Five-story Georgian townhouse showing post-war and contemporary art across light-filled rooms. The roster leans heavily on expressive painting and major historical surveys.

name: Samaia Georgian Restaurant
description: Compact family-run dining room in Barnes serving handmade Georgian plates. The intimate space gets loud as tables crowd with cheese-stuffed khachapuri and meat-filled dumplings.

name: Prince of Peckham Pub
description: Lively corner pub pairing a traditional tiled bar with Caribbean cooking. Trays of jerk chicken and oxtail crowd the tables before the floor clears for DJs and rum punch.

name: 2210 by NattyCanCook
description: High-energy Herne Hill dining room blending fine-dining precision with Pan-Caribbean heat. An open kitchen sends out refined jerk chicken and ackee spring rolls against a loud backdrop of R&B and Afrobeats.

name: Dulwich Tandoori
description: Lordship Lane fixture serving traditional Indian and Pakistani staples since 1982. Large birthday groups and locals sticking to regular orders fill the cozy dining room.

name: Hyde Park
description: Perhaps London's most famous park. There is much to see and do: from browsing the Serpentine Gallery and Pavillion to swimming and boating. Relax throughout and allow plenty of time to explore all 350 acres.

name: Cafe Jumo
description: Quaint neighborhood cafe good for both a relaxed coffee or a social brunch. All food and drinks served are of high quality. There are a few outdoor tables and the indoor aesthetic is picture-worthy. Under-the-radar, for now.

name: Connie's Pizza
description: Peckham pizzeria serving "Bri-talian" pies that pair light, fermented dough with seasonal British produce. A marble sharing table fills the brick-lined room, facing an open kitchen turning out crispy, blistered bases.

name: Tokyo Bagel
description: Japanese bakery and café in Waterloo with a rose-lined interior. Shokupan and katsu bagel sandos fill the counter by day, while the evening shift flips the room into a sake cocktail and tapas bar.

name: Chishuru
description: Intimate Fitzrovia dining room serving a set tasting menu of modern West African cuisine. Bold, inventive courses arrive in a warm room of rough plaster and wood.

name: Bang Bang Oriental Foodhall
description: Massive Colindale food hall with the noise and density of an Asian hawker market. Two dozen kiosks line the walls, serving roast duck and bubble tea to packed communal tables.

name: Tian Tian Market - Kings Cross
