description: Modern, light-filled supermarket stocking East and Southeast Asian pantry staples. Wooden shelves line deep aisles neatly stacked with regional sauces, frozen dumplings, and imported snacks.

name: Cristea Roberts Gallery
description: Pall Mall gallery focused on contemporary prints and works on paper. Calm, considered rooms give editions by artists like Bridget Riley and Josef Albers room to breathe.

name: Mother Mash Carnaby
description: Modern pie and mash shop serving customizable heaps of sausages and potatoes off Carnaby Street. The menu runs on a simple three-step choice of mash style, main, and gravy to cover it all.

name: Claridge's
description: A London institution housed within an art deco building with brass-detailed doors and fully-attired doorman. Join a long line of esteemed guests, from Winston Churchill to Audrey Hepburn. Claridge's service is of great renown.

name: Dough Hands East
description: Kitchen residency at The Spurstowe Arms turning out thin, crispy pizzas with a serious snap. The pub gets raucous by early evening, with rounds of hot honey and ’nduja pies landing on crowded tables.

name: Smoking Goat Shoreditch
description: Industrial Shoreditch canteen serving Northern Thai drinking food with serious heat. Smoke pours from the open kitchen as tables fill with charcoal-grilled meat and cold lager.

name: Forty Dean Street
description: Buzzing family-run Italian spot sourcing bread and coffee from historic neighbors. The tight room squeezes marble tables against velvet banquettes for homemade lobster ravioli and seafood linguine.

name: 40 Maltby Street
description: Multi-functional space next to the Maltby Street Market. Foremost a restaurant and bar, the venue also sells hearty sandwiches, artisanal foodstuffs, organic produce, and wine. A true neighborhood hotspot.

name: NOPI
description: From starters and mains, to sharing plates - NOPI serves a celebrated menu of seasonal flavors. Eat in the conventional dining room, or in the basement - a space comprising sharing tables that sit in view of the open kitchen.

name: Bentley's Oyster Bar & Grill
description: Mayfair seafood institution split between a bustling ground-floor oyster bar and a formal upstairs dining room. Shuckers work fast at the marble counter, while the heated terrace stays full year-round.

name: Nipotina
description: Polished Mayfair dining room mimics a contemporary Italian residence with soft plaster walls and green velvet. Comforting family recipes join theatrical touches like clay-pot Negronis and a rolling dessert trolley.

name: Cucina London
description: Low-key Italian dining room at the St Giles Hotel serving handmade pasta and oven-cooked pizza. Quiet tables sit within walking distance of West End theaters.

name: Tom Brown at The Capital
description: Intimate 28-seat dining room serving sophisticated, sustainable seafood in Knightsbridge. The open kitchen turns out creative plates like lobster toast and cuttlefish cacio e pepe.

name: AngloThai
description: Intimate Marylebone dining room serving a fixed tasting menu of Thai flavors built from the British larder. The space is tight and energetic, with chili and charcoal smoke drifting from the open kitchen over packed tables.

name: La Petite Maison (LPM) London
description: Airy French dining room tucked in a Mayfair mews with white linens and a zinc bar. Tables come set with fresh tomatoes and a lemon for slicing alongside sharing plates of Niçoise classics.

name: Bella Italia - Wellington Street
description: Casual Italian chain outpost handling the pre-theatre rush near the Lyceum. Familiar pizza and pasta plates arrive fast in a dining room built for volume and families.

name: Noble Rot
description: From the founders of the "Noble Rot" food and wine magazine, this restaurant and wine bar offers seasonal French-British fare. Both this restaurant and its sibling venue, located in Soho, have won awards for their wine lists.

name: 081 Pizzeria Shoreditch
description: Neapolitan pizzeria serving pies with high, air-filled crusts and soft centers. The setup is stripped back and casual, keeping the focus on the dough and traditional toppings.

name: DakaDaka
description: Modern Georgian dining room in Mayfair built around open-fire cooking. Counter seats line the pass as chefs fold khinkali and grill meats; the wine list runs deep on natural bottles.

name: ALTA Kingly Court
description: Northern Spanish grill spanning two floors of Kingly Court. A wood-fired open kitchen dominates the ground level, while the upstairs dining room serves sharing plates and wines on tap.

name: Bagan Vibe Pan Asian Restaurant
description: Cozy dining room hung with puppets and parasols. The kitchen covers broad Pan-Asian ground, but the Burmese menu dominates the tables with authentic tea leaf salads and heavy noodle bowls.

name: SUSHINOEN
description: Bright, plant-filled Japanese dining room occupying a grand Victorian clergy house. Bubbling sukiyaki pots and generous sushi platters crowd raw wood tables near the open kitchen.

name: Chez Lui
description: Intimate Notting Hill bistro serving roast chicken and steak au poivre in a candlelit dining room. Downstairs, a jewel-toned bar pours late cocktails on velvet banquettes.

name: Spring Street Pizza
description: Packed railway arch slinging eighteen-inch New York pies with thin, foldable crusts. The massive rounds are built for sharing, with most tables splitting toppings half-and-half.

name: Lahpet West End
description: Polished, split-level dining room serving a modern introduction to Burmese cuisine. Groups fill the warm interior and terrace to share bowls of mohinga and the signature pickled tea leaf salad.

name: Arponnar
description: Homestyle Burmese kitchen in Willesden Green lined with teak carvings. The room smells of shrimp paste and plays Burmese radio as tables share tea leaf salads and bowls of mohinga.

name: Tatar Bunar
description: Warm Ukrainian dining room filled with Carpathian oak and vintage rugs. The open kitchen cooks sharing plates and dumplings over live fire to go with house vodka infusions.

name: XIX Nineteen
description: Stratford dining room serving massive portions of Ukrainian comfort food like borscht and varenyky. The cozy, lounge-like space fills up on weekends for long group dinners and occasional live music.

name: Disfrutar
description: Touted as one of the world's finest restaurants, Disfrutar's dining experience is one of the best in the city. The chefs are consistently creative with the combinations of flavour, texture, and of course, the presentation of their dishes.

name: Panico
description: Cozy Poblenou pizzeria filled with the heavy scent of baking dough. The kitchen turns out traditional Neapolitan pies, pulling blistered, 48-hour fermented crusts loaded with imported Italian cheese straight from a central oven.

name: Arcano Restaurant
description: Hidden 17th-century stable turned intimate El Born dining room. Candlelight warms the stone arches while the kitchen sends out tasting menus and charcoal-grilled Mediterranean cuts.

name: Arcano
description: Restored 17th-century stone stables in El Born repurposed into an intimate, cave-like dining room. Leisurely Mediterranean dinners center on grilled meats and tasting menus under low-lit arches.

name: Palau Dalmases
description: Baroque 17th-century palace in El Born staging intimate, nightly flamenco performances. Hour-long sets of live guitar, singing, and traditional dance play out in a candlelit, 50-seat stone room with natural acoustics.

name: Perros Mediterráneos
description: Two-story Sant Antoni record shop and bar pouring natural wine alongside bins of vinyl. Floor cushions fill up early for tapas and cocktails while DJs play funk and electronic at a volume built for conversation.

name: La Font del Gat
description: Historic park pavilion and terraced garden set high on Montjuïc hill. The sprawling outdoor terrace fills with long tables for shared Catalan tapas, wood-fired skewers, and pitchers of cava sangria alongside live music.

name: Sunseabar
description: Open-air beach bar sitting right on the sand at Platja del Fòrum. Casual afternoon drinks turn into sunset dance parties, bringing house and techno DJs straight to the shoreline.

name: Calma Yoga Studio
description: Intimate Sarrià yoga studio capping classes at ten mats for close, hands-on instruction. The quiet space runs a steady schedule of active Vinyasa flows and deep, guided Nidra rest.

name: Centre Cívic Can Deu
description: Restored 19th-century mansion operating as an active neighborhood cultural center in Les Corts. The vintage café opens onto a quiet garden terrace hosting a steady schedule of community workshops, live concerts, and afternoon drinks.

name: Candy Darling
description: Vibrant queer bar with plush lounge seating, eclectic art, and a steady rotation of drag and burlesque shows. Early evenings run on cocktails and toasted sandwiches before late-night dancing takes over the pocket-sized disco.

name: Freedonia
description: Grassroots cultural space and intimate underground club in El Raval. The two-room layout splits a relaxed front lounge from a small, notoriously sweaty dancefloor running live bands and late-night DJ sets.

name: Gats
description: Chic bar located in the Carrer d'en Xuclà neighborhood of Barcelona. Gats pairs cocktails with a highly popular tapas menu. Visit for casual drinks and conversation on the venue's stylish terrace, or go with more serious dining in mind.

name: Berbena
description: Intimate 24-seat Gràcia dining room built around an open kitchen. Chefs run the floor themselves, serving seasonal Mediterranean half-portions, fresh bread, and natural wine.

name: Bodega La Puntual
description: Traditional Catalan bodega stretching deep into a medieval El Born building. Barrel tables up front handle quick rounds of house vermouth, while the stone-walled back room serves full dinners of classic tapas and seasonal plates.

name: Origo
description: Artisan bakery outposts turning out slow-fermented organic sourdough and handmade pastries. The takeaway counter slings specialty espresso, daily cardamom twists, and dark chocolate cookies.

name: Vereda Bar
description: Olive-green corner restaurant in Eixample Esquerra with large street-facing windows. An open kitchen sits at the center of the small dining room, serving seasonal sharing plates and natural wine for slow, lingering dinners.

name: La Pubilla
description: Bustling Gràcia dining room across from the Mercat de la Llibertat, serving hearty Catalan dishes sourced from the daily market haul. Tables fill fast as staff translate seasonal specials from a menu printed strictly in Catalan.

name: Queviures Múrria
description: Restored 1898 Catalan grocery running as an intimate restaurant lined with wooden shelves of wine and artisanal cheese. Small high-top tables and a pine counter fill with modern Catalan plates, Iberico ham, and local wines.

name: La Cova Fumada
description: Unmarked Barceloneta tapas bar hidden behind a steady line out the door. The loud, cramped room runs fast and chaotic, slinging deep-fried potato bombas and grilled seafood across a crowded bar and seven marble tables.

name: Casa Costa
description: Barceloneta beachfront restaurant serving Josper-grilled seafood and shared tapas right on the sand. Seating splits between a busy ground-floor terrace and an upstairs dining room looking straight out over the water.

name: Curated By.
description: Minimalist design shop on Carrer d'Enric Granados stocking small-batch homewares, furniture, and apparel. The natural-toned space carries locally made, limited-edition pieces, from glass pitchers to side tables.

name: Tiberi Bar
description: Airy Poble-sec bar and dining room pouring natural wine alongside modern Catalan shared plates. Exposed stone and candlelight wrap around tables covered in chicken focaccia, Iberian pork, and mezcal cocktails.

name: Colmado Wilmot
description: Bright neighborhood deli and wine bar serving elevated Catalan tapas and half-portions. Cured meats and pantry staples line the walls around tight tables filled with potato tortillas, rich beef stews, and cold vermouth.

name: La Camila
description: Retro neighborhood bar in Gràcia filled with antique furniture and vintage crockery. The cozy space runs from morning specialty coffee into afternoon natural wine, house vermouth, and classic slices of tortilla de patatas.

name: Besta
description: Seafood-driven Eixample neo-bistro combining Galician and Catalan traditions. Chefs plate market-fresh tasting menus right across a black marble counter, pouring small-production regional wines to match.

name: Teòric Taverna Gastronòmica
description: Intimate dining room serving a set Catalan tasting menu built around seasonal sea and mountain ingredients. The kitchen runs through ten or thirteen courses paired with natural wines, with staff explaining the origin of every plate.

name: Bar Salvatge
description: Lively, intimate Gràcia natural wine bar pouring a rotating lineup of low-intervention vintages on tap. Generous glasses sit alongside shared plates of XXL Gildas, duck tacos, and local cheeses.

name: Working In The Redwoods
description: Miriam Cernuda carefully handcrafts each piece for sale in this ceramic store, taking cues from the Mediterranean Sea and the nature of the Costa Brava. Cernuda's simple yet elegant wares feature natural hues perfect for any room.

name: Casa Bonay
description: This converted 1869 townhouse has just the right amount of original neoclassical elements alongside modern, local design. The hotel comprises four restaurant and bar spaces, which include rooftop tapas and a coffee-cocktail bar.

name: Noak Roam
description: A locally owned and operated furniture store that sells both new and vintage pieces from Scandinavia. The owners are proud of the pieces they have curated for their store. Also featuring the work of local artists and artisans.

name: BistroNou
description: Relaxed Poblenou bistro pouring natural wine alongside modern tapas and small plates. Meals center on strong vegetarian dishes and updated Spanish staples like patatas bravas and churros.

name: Hotel Pulitzer
description: The Pulitzer is notorious for attracting a suave crowd - recline in the spacious for a dose of people watching. The recently redone rooms are tastefully designed, and the leafy rooftop bar is ideal for alfresco evenings spent relaxing.

name: Wittmore Hotel
description: The Wittmore Hotel is all class with just the right amount of quirk. This adult-only hotel provides stunning vistas of the sea, and the city's ornate rooftops. It's the ideal spot from which to explore Barcelona's bustling creative hub.

name: Bar La Plata
description: A 17th-century tapas restaurant in Barcelona's Gothic Quarter. The menu offers four classic dishes - a salad of tomato, onion, and Arbequina olives; botifarra; fresh anchovies; and deep-fried sardines.

name: Les Filles Cafè
description: Contemporary-modern venue serving tapas and health-conscious meals. Come the weekend, Les Filles Café serves serves a popular brunch menu that is best accompanied by a selection of handcrafted cocktails.

name: Two Schmucks
description: Self-described as a "five-star dive bar", Two Schmucks is a relaxed spot that also delivers excellent drinks. Located in hipster El Raval, they also offer a happy hour with beer, shots, and snacks. Great late night as well.

name: Mercat dels Encants de Barcelona
description: Sprawling open-air flea market under a massive mirrored canopy. Sloping ramps wind past hundreds of stalls piled with antiques, vintage clothes, and hardware, running steady from early morning auctions to mid-afternoon.

name: Platja d'Ocata
description: Expansive stretch of coarse golden sand a short train ride north of central Barcelona. Volleyball games and lively beach bars run along the wide shore, sitting right beside deep water and light Mediterranean surf.

name: La Dama
description: A popular dining venue for Barcelona's well-to-do. La Dama, set within a Gaudi-style building, serves a refined Mediterranean menu with additional French influences. Think roast pigeon and soft-lit anniversary dinners.

name: Soho House Barcelona
description: Everything to be expected from a Soho House establishment. Book a room here for immediate access to the many amenities - such as a restaurant, bar, health club and spa, pool, and rooftop terrace.

name: Love Vintage
description: Clean, owner-run vintage shop in central Barcelona stocking highly wearable clothing over costume pieces. The knowledgeable owner keeps racks filled with classic designer labels and unbranded finds in excellent condition.

name: Dr. Stravinsky
description: Experimental El Born cocktail bar styled as an old apothecary, packed with illuminated jars and working stills. Bartenders work the busy main counter, mixing house-distilled spirits and complex ferments ordered from a flavor map.

name: Tacos 99
description: Compact, busy taqueria on Avinguda del Paral·lel serving traditional street-style tacos and cold margaritas. The kitchen sticks to the classics, turning out slow-cooked carnitas, fresh guacamole, and house-made tres leches.

name: Vermut i a la Gàbia
description: Lively tapas and vermouth bar spilling onto a terrace in Plaça d'Osca. Glasses of red vermouth, beef-stuffed bombas, and patatas bravas run steady from the half-open kitchen to crowded tables on the square.

name: El Passadís del Pep
description: Long, unmarked corridor opening into a bustling, windowless dining room. Waiters skip the menus entirely, pouring cava and dropping plates of fresh market seafood onto white tablecloths.

name: La Petite Parade
description: Weekend vintage market tucked into a hidden El Born alleyway. Racks of curated 90s and Y2K clothing line the stone-arched showroom, mixing second-hand streetwear with upcycled pieces from local designers.

name: Sala Apolo
description: Classic Art Deco theatre running as a multi-room live music venue and late-night club. The main floor shifts from evening gigs to late DJ sets under high stucco ceilings, with a red-velvet mezzanine looking down at the stage.

name: Il Giardinetto
description: Classic 1974 dining room styled like a lush indoor forest with rich green tones and split-level seating. The kitchen serves a mix of Italian and Catalan plates alongside classic cocktails and live piano music.

name: Flash Flash
description: Preserved 1970s pop-art dining room serving over 50 varieties of Spanish tortillas and classic burgers. Closely packed tables and white leather sofas stay loud and busy with continuous service from midday through late night.

name: La Nova Premsa
description: Renovated Catalan farmhouse pouring local Penedès wine alongside globally influenced sharing plates. Weekly chalkboard specials drive the menu, mixing regional tapas and Asian flavors across a busy dining room and outdoor terrace.

name: Chula Vista
description: High-energy restaurant serving Californian-Mexican food on a Raval plaza. The raw, neon-lit space runs loud with music and strong margaritas, with tables spilling onto a tree-shaded terrace for LA-style burritos.

name: Forno Bomba
description: Neighborhood bakery in Sants turning out sourdough, Roman pizza, and cardamom buns from an open kitchen. The compact front room handles steady takeout orders, while a hidden back patio has quiet tables for coffee and focaccia.

name: Bistro Levante
description: This little leafy enclave in the Gothic Quarter serves up Mediterranean fare that is generous in flavour, yet simple and light. Whatever dish of choice, enjoy it with hummus and any one of their soft breads.

name: Els Encants
description: One of Europe's oldest flea markets. Over 500 vendors sell everything from furnishings, to clothes and music - some vintage, some second-hand. Browse and bargain hunt beneath Els Encants' iconic mirror canopy.

name: Entrepanes Díaz
description: Flavorful restaurant serving creative, gourmet sandwiches, tapas, and drinks. Be sure to try the Antxón sandwich, made with chistorra (cured sausage), an egg, and crispy potatoes. Book ahead for the best tables.

name: Bar del Pla
description: An intimate wine bar and restaurant that exudes a familial warmth. Expect proper Catalan tapas, like squid ink croquettes, fried egg with sausages, and, of course, patatas bravas.

name: Granja Dulcinea
description: All things sweet alongside classic, old-world charm - a chocolate shop that has been standing since 1941. Go for the churros - they're served with thick, Swiss hot chocolate.

name: Libreria Sant Jordi
description: One of the oldest bookshops in Barcelona, Llibreria Sant Jordi harbors a diverse collection (some 6000 books) on design, photography, and art. In fact, "poor taste" is the only thing they do not stock - direct from the owner's mouth.

name: Cripta de la Colònia Güell
description: Unfinished subterranean church in a quiet industrial village outside Barcelona. Leaning basalt columns and irregular stained glass fill the intimate space – a crowd-free testing ground for the Sagrada Família.

name: Origo Bakery
description: Warm sourdough bakery turning out slow-fermented loaves and Scandinavian pastries from an open kitchen. Specialty coffee and fresh cardamom twists move fast during the morning rush, with the daily bake often selling out early.

name: Els Pescadors
description: Els Pescadors is set beneath three magnificent ancient ombu trees in the fishermen village of El Poblenou. It's the perfect setting for a leisurely lunch of fresh Mediterranean and seafood dishes.

name: Basilica of the Sagrada Familia
description: Massive, unfinished Gaudí basilica with towering spires and heavily carved stone facades. Branching columns rise through the vast nave, catching shifting light from the surrounding stained-glass windows.

name: ALNORTE Bar
description: Neighborhood bar focused on the food and drink of Northern Spain: Asturian cider, Galician empanadas, and artisanal cheeses. The small kitchen has no deep fryer, serving a simple menu of plates that changes weekly based on available product

name: paloma wool
description: Womenswear label with an artistic sensibility, housed in a spacious converted garage. Display pieces are brought to fitting rooms by staff; mirrors inside feature adjustable dimmers to simulate day and evening light.

name: Teatre Tívoli
description: Grand Eixample theater staging major musicals, classical ballets, and large-scale plays. Red velvet and gold moldings run through the 1,600-seat auditorium, matching the traditional scale of the performances.

name: Right Side Coffee Bar
description: Compact coffee bar tucked down a Gothic Quarter alley pouring house-roasted espresso and flat whites. Large windows catch the sun, filling the high-ceilinged room with bright morning light.

name: Salts - Terrassa Bar Montjuïc
description: Open-air terrace bar sitting right above the 1992 Olympic diving pool on Montjuïc hill. The busy counter hands off cold beers and sangria to crowded tables waiting for the sun to drop over the Barcelona skyline.

name: Carnal Steak House
description: Warm Eixample steakhouse serving heavily dry-aged beef and strong cocktails. Sizzling cuts arrive alongside hot stones for a final sear, filling the room with the heavy scent of wood smoke and roasting meat.

name: MIKAN
description: Warm Eixample Esquerra dining room serving Northeast Asian small plates and natural wine. Tables load up with Iberian pork katsu and cherry tomato bombs while staff pour tasting splashes from open bottles.

name: Los Tortíllez | Eixample
description: Tight, 80s-style Eixample dining room built around the Spanish potato omelet. The busy kitchen sends out traditional tapas alongside over fifteen variations of individual, made-to-order tortillas.

name: Scobies Irish Pub
description: Traditional Irish pub near Plaça de Catalunya pouring proper pints of Guinness alongside a deep whiskey list. The wood-paneled room gets loud and lively during major rugby and football matches, with steady rounds and bags of Tayto crisps.

name: Pobail Nua
description: Warm Irish pub in Sant Martí pouring proper pints of Guinness and Murphy’s stout. Live football matches play on overhead screens, and tabs close with a complimentary Baby Murphy shot.

name: Pigment Gallery
description: Luminous contemporary gallery near the Arc de Triomf hanging both modern figurative pieces and pure abstraction. The founder frequently walks the floor, talking through the current exhibitions and the artists behind them.

name: Sita Murt Mallorca
description: Barcelona-based women's boutique founded by designer Sita Murt - renowned for her unique fabrics crafted from yarn. A knitting master, her brand continues to showcase timeless, high-quality women's fashion, honoring her legacy.

name: Bel y Cía 1842
description: Classic Passeig de Gràcia tailor running a two-floor workshop for bespoke shirts and handmade Teba jackets. The back room holds bolts of cloth and thick swatch books for made-to-measure fittings.

name: Arenas de Barcelona
description: A commercial shopping, sports and music complex located in Placa España that previously served as a bullfighting arena. Come for the shops, stay for the 360-degree view of the city from its rooftop.

name: Bodega Bonay
description: Buzzy ground-floor dining room in Casa Bonay pouring natural wine alongside pan-Mediterranean sharing plates. Bar stools face an open kitchen sending out dishes like sea-urchin royale and braised pork jowl.

name: Hotel Alma
description: A self-described oasis in the heart of the city, Hotel Alma's sleek industrial-feel décor beautifully contrasts its lush garden courtyard. The modern aesthetic flows through all 72 rooms, and the hotel's spa is worthy of note too.

name: Margot House
description: Located across from Poma de la Discòrdia, Margot House offers a mix of suave boutique hotel and warm, homely atmosphere. Guests of the nine rooms are free to enjoy the hotel's gorgeous lounge, dining room and library.

name: Paradiso
description: Consistently on a few "World's Best Bars" lists, it does make sense how hyped Paradiso is. The cocktails are outstanding, the staff is friendly, and the vibe is very speakeasy. Arrive early unless you're ready to queue for a while.

name: Fino Bar
description: Neighborhood bodega where seasonal tapas and charcuterie are sliced and plated along a long marble bar. The wine list is heavy on sherries and natural bottles; book ahead for a seat at the counter.

name: H10 Art Gallery
description: Modern Eixample hotel doubling as an art gallery, with original Miró works in the lobby and artist-themed guest rooms. Welcome cava is poured by the rooftop plunge pool or down in the courtyard next to a century-old olive tree.

name: Sips
description: The closest thing to alcohol theatre you'll ever experience, Sips earns its place amongst the best bars in the world. With the bar in the centre of the room, watch as your drink is expertly prepared by the friendly mixologists.

name: The Green Spot
description: With its minimalist interiors, this is one of the slickest cafes in a city filled with slick cafes 😍. As the name suggests, The Green Spot does vegetarian and vegan dishes.

name: Can Travi Nou
description: Absolutely gorgeous restaurant set in a 1600s farmhouse with a shaded terrace perfect for outdoor summer nights. Food highlights include excellent calcotadas, paella, black rice, and codfish. Worth visiting just for the experience.

name: Santa Caterina Market
description: Fresh food market with a photogenic roof - though the mosaic is best seen from above, visitors can appreciate the wave-like structure from the ground. Enter for local produce, artisan goods, and tasty eateries.

name: Mont Bar
description: The deliciously modern concept of bar fine dining is achieved exceedingly well by chef Domonic Ungaro. He dreams up sharing plates using imaginative ingredients and techniques. Highlights include oysters, wagyu, and sobrassada.

name: Lomo Alto
description: Sip wine and listen to one of Lomo Alto's waiters wax lyrical about meat breeds and cuts before indulging in one of the best steaks that Barcelona has to offer. From veal to ox, Lomo Alto's dedication to artisanal quality is absolute.

name: Mediamanga
description: With its open kitchen concept, dining at Mediamanga is a true sensory experience - watch, smell, and then taste. Fresh, locally-sourced ingredients further ensure a raw gastronomic journey through the Mediterranean cuisine.

name: Gresca
description: Bag a stool by Gresca's open kitchen to watch their team passionately prepare a variety of Catalan tapas dishes. Trust your meal to well-paired with a wine from the restaurant's selection of over 400 new bottles per month.

name: Montseny
description: A rural municipality set between Barcelona and Girona - and part of the Catalan Pre-Coastal Range. Best known for the eponymous Montseny Massif and Natural Park, designated as a UNESCO reserve in 1978.

name: Balius
description: Located in what used to be a pharmacy, Balius now serves up a medicine of a different kind: cocktails and vermouth 🍹. It's a warm, cozy spot made more so with the friendly service. Enjoy a live jazz band once a week 🎷.

name: Casa Bloc
description: Perhaps unremarkable today, Casa Bloc was revolutionary upon its construction in the 1930s. The S-shaped complex prompted a new direction of social housing, and is now one of the best examples of 20th century rationalist architecture.

name: La Sagrada Familia
description: Barcelona's most famous attraction, it's a testament to Gaudi's style and truly unlike any other church in the world. Still under construction ~140 years later, it's easy to understand why with the intricate level of detail present.

name: CREC
description: Spacious and well-kept co-working facility in the heart of Barcelona - an excellent place to do business. Offers plenty of room for meetings and phone calls in some of the smaller areas. A friendly community.

name: Girona
description: Girona is a small city at the confluence of the Ter and Onyar rivers renowned for both its well-preserved Jewish Quarter and medieval old town. Pop culture fans will even recognize some sights from Game of Thrones. Also a cycling hub.

name: BD Barcelona Design
description: Functioning as a shop, showroom and studio, BD Barcelona is more like a gallery, exhibiting the very best in interior design, from lighting fixtures to furniture pieces. Their catalogue includes original designs by Dali and Gaudi.

name: Satan's Coffee Corner
description: Contrary to the name, the coffee here may very well be from the Gods. Here for the city's misfits, Satan's prides itself on pouring a damn good brew. The in-house pastry chef will also sweeten the deal, as will the Japanese-slant menu.

name: Paco Meralgo
description: Tapas bar with a buzzy vibe and modern stool seating, serving seafood plates, croquettes, and a few kinds of tartare. Each dish is exceedingly fresh and it's hard to go wrong.

name: Leona General Store
description: Intimate neighborhood boutique stocked with a varied mix of clothing, home decor, and original gifts. The owner runs the shop and makes the artisan jewelry by hand.

name: Jaç Hi-fi Cafe
description: Walnut-lined coffee shop and vinyl listening bar running without Wi-Fi to keep focus on the music. Custom speakers built into the counter play records while the bar serves in-house roasts, direct-source matcha, and sourdough toast.

name: Pasteleria Hofmann
description: Sweet tooth or not, this is a must. Bestsellers include filled croissants - mascarpone, chocolate, raspberry.

name: Mercer Hotel
description: Each room at the Mercer is its own experience, replete with original Roman-era walls and 14th-century pointed archways. Take full advantage and dine at the in-house restaurant - one of the finest in this Gothic Quarter.

name: Xemei
description: Venetian cuisine focused on seafood by brothers Stefano and Max Colombo. Cozy restaurant with a rustic feel to it that meshes nicely with the beautiful plating.

name: La Barceloneta
description: La Barceloneta is a big part of what defines the city as a whole - young, cool, always moving. Catch a tan or a surf on Sant Sebastià; wine and dine in the ocean air; or simply enjoy a walk through the narrow streets or on the promenade.

name: Bar Bodega Quimet
description: Traditional tapas and wine bar frequented by locals for good food and drinks - expect very reasonable prices too. Bar Bodega Quiment's extensive drinks list includes wine straight from the barrel.

name: Can Maño
description: No bells and whistles, just good 'ol Catalan fresh fish. Arrive hungry as the portions are sizable, and the prices are low. It's a local favorite, so there may be a wait, but the grilled calamari will make it all worthwhile.

name: Casa Comalat
description: Gaudi's influence is clear in this Modernista apartment block designed by Salvador Valeri i Pupurull. The building stands out on a corner of Avinguda Diagonal due to its ornate and fantastical details.

name: Casa Batlló
description: Part architectural landmark, part fantastical creation, Gaudi's Casa Batlló is a gem of the Modernism architectural movement. It constitutes part of the iconic Block of Discord, a row of buildings by noted Modernista architects.

name: Benevola Pastelería
description: Calm, plant-based patisserie serving refined, low-sugar vegan desserts. Seasonal chocolate pecan cakes and citrus tarts sit alongside specialty coffee and natural wine.

name: Bodega Solera
description: Gràcia bodega pairing classic Andalusian tavern style with a massive natural wine cellar. Plates of hand-carved Iberian ham and slow-cooked fricandó hit the marble counter alongside steady pours of sherry and biodynamic bottles.

name: ESPECIARIUM BAR | Barcelona
description: Intimate El Born cocktail bar mixing global spices into complex drinks. Bartenders shake heavily infused spirits like curry rum, passing drinks and small tapas across a warmly lit counter.

name: La Vinya del Senyor
description: Compact El Born wine bar pouring a rotating by-the-glass list alongside plates of cured meats and artisanal cheeses. Tables line the cobblestone plaza directly facing the Gothic facade of the Santa Maria del Mar basilica.

name: Quirat
description: Michelin-starred dining room attached to the InterContinental hotel with an independent street entrance. The kitchen runs multi-course tasting menus built around regional Catalan ingredients in a lively, conversational space.

name: Brabo | Restaurante Gracia
description: Modern Gràcia asador centered on an open kitchen and glowing Holm oak embers. Tables fill with house-cured charcuterie, thick ribeyes, and three-day fermented bread pulled directly from the grill.

name: franca
description: Warm Eixample dining room with arched brick ceilings and acoustics quiet enough for real conversation. Dinner runs on inventive Catalan small plates, warm olives, and local natural wine.

name: Caravelle
description: This vibey café gets its name from the founders having parked a caravan in the city - and the rest, as they say, is history. On top of excellent brunch meals, they also brew their own beer. No reservations so go early or plan to wait.

name: Elsa y Fred
description: Gastrobar inspired by a wealth of flavours, Elsa y Fred has become a favored eatery and watering hole. Popular throughout the day, but most alive during lunch hours. Don't leave without trying the humble but mighty patatas bravas.

name: Carretera de les Aigües
description: A respite from the city's buzz, Carretera de les Aigües is a mostly flat walking and cycling path around the Collserola mountain, just eight kilometers from the city centre. Make a day of it and pack a picnic basket.

name: Estimar
description: At Estimar, it's hard to know if the diners are eating in the kitchen, or if the kitchen is in the dining room. What is known though, is the quality of the menu. Fresh, local seafood arrives everyday and is prepared in a variety of ways.

name: Carrer de Blai
description: A regular jaunt for locals, this street is filled with little cafés for alfresco dining. By dining we mean tapas and pintxos without the touristy price tags. Go for the festive night time vibe no matter the time of year.

name: Espai Joliu
description: An eclectic, industrial coffee shop with well-made coffees and breakfast. While waiting for coffee, be sure to take a look at the various magazines, plants, and other home-goods for sale.

name: Aire de Barcelona
description: A 17th century warehouse converted into arguably Barcelona's most lavish retreat. Aire offers an Arabic spa experience within a subterranean setting - from couples experiences, to athletes massages and wedding specials.

name: Sitges
description: Southwest of Barcelona, Sitges is a coastal town in Catalonia backed by the mountains of Parc Natural del Garraf. Beautiful beaches, restaurants, shopping and queer nightlife make it a hotspot for visitors.

name: El Corte Inglés
description: Sprawling department store on Plaça de Catalunya with nine floors of fashion, electronics, and home goods. A basement supermarket stocks daily groceries while the top-floor food hall serves meals with panoramic city views.

name: Sant Martí
description: Sant Martí is a district in Barcelona situated along the Mediterranean Coast. It has restaurants, music festivals, street art, and more. Platja del Bogatell is a popular beach with snack bars, volleyball courts, and funky sculptures.

name: Bardeni El Meatbar
description: Chef-driven meatbar with a vintage butcher shop aesthetic, serving high-end cuts as creative small plates. The counter is the best seat for the house signatures: hand-cut steak tartar and rich oxtail cannelloni.

name: Bellesguard
description: Take a tour of one of Gaudi's lesser known buildings. It stands on historical land that, in the 15th century, held the summer residence of Martin of Aragon; information that inspired Gaudi to create the house seen today.

name: Juice Dudes
description: Headlined by its juices, Juice Dudes also serves a popular array of health foods and coffee. Grab a smoothie on the go, or stop in for an acai bowl and caffeine boost.

name: Mies van der Rohe Pavilion
description: The Barcelona Pavilion was designed by Mies van der Rohe for the 1929 Barcelona International Exposition. The Pavilion's bold design has since become a monument for modern architects, and a exhibition space for contemporary artists.

name: Hotel Elena de Cobre
description: Restored 19th-century mansion in downtown León capped by a brutalist copper addition. The central patio serves smoked Mexican plates, while rooms balance colonial stone and modern concrete.

name: Spotify Camp Nou
description: FC Barcelona’s colossal stadium is in the middle of a major renovation. The complex centers on an interactive museum and three-story megastore while the pitch is closed.

name: Sant Andreu
description: This neighborhood in Barcelona is scarcely trafficked by tourists but well worth a visit, especially for the food. The Bacallanera Perelló specializes in salt cod, and Rabassada is a family-run restaurant with a lovely terrace.

name: Santa Eulalia
description: Santa Eulalia is a family-owned boutique that has been around since 1843. Stocking many high-end brands that you won't be able to find elsewhere in Barcelona, it is frequented by chic locals and luxury travelers alike.

name: Iriarte Iriarte
description: Barcelona's Iriarte Iriarte combines old-world craftsmanship with eco-friendly techniques and materials. Their pieces have high-quality finishes, solid brass fittings, and novel reinterpretations of classic designs.

name: Raspall
description: Gràcia bar serving a free, selectable tapa with every drink. Crowds squeeze into the tight interior to pick from the daily chalkboard menu or spill out onto the plaza terrace.

name: Razzmatazz
description: Colossal industrial complex in Poblenou running five distinct clubs under one roof. The labyrinthine layout shifts from live indie gigs to heavy techno sets without leaving the building.

name: Frizzant | Barcelona
description: Social wellness center pairing a yoga studio with a health-focused kitchen and workspace. English-friendly movement classes spill directly into the lounge for post-workout meals and remote work.

name: La Pubilla del Taulat
description: Historic Poblenou bodega split between a tapas bar and a bulk wine shop. The counter serves house vermouth and classic Catalan plates like bombas and bravas under original wooden beams.

name: Masa Vins Barcelona
description: Tiny natural wine bar in Poble Nou with the energy of a packed living room. Vinyl spins over Eastern European bottles and creative small plates like kimchi grilled cheese.

name: Vila Viniteca
description: Vila Viniteca is a foodie paradise. With some of the best cheese, charcuterie, wine, and dry goods in Spain, it is the perfect place in the city to shop for a picnic. They also regularly offer wine tastings, which can be booked online.

name: La Taverna del Clínic
description: A small gastronomic enclave, comprising two dining spaces, in the heart of Barcelona. Alongside its Mediterranean food, La Taverna del Clínic has a carefully curated wine cellar.

name: El Nacional
description: El Nacional offers four different dining experiences under the same roof - a meat restaurant, a fish restaurant, a tapas eatery, and a fast-paced deli. A multi-culinary dining experience for every taste. There are four bars within too.

name: Fleischerei Haroun
description: Second-generation Halal butcher in Wedding prepping fresh daily cuts and house-made sausages. Multilingual staff wrap up batches of family-recipe merguez, spiced köfte, and herb-marinated chicken thighs.

name: Otto
description: Seasonal small plates and natural wines are served in an intimate venue with a leafy terrace. The menu features locally sourced ingredients, including great for sharing dishes like smoked brook trout and koji butter.

name: Ma-Makan
description: Homestyle kopitiam on a car-free Kreuzberg square cooking scratch-made Malaysian and Singaporean recipes. The kitchen shifts from kaya toast breakfasts to spicy bowls of laksa and nasi lemak later in the day.

name: Feed Back
description: Contemporary Chinese restaurant serving elevated takes on classic dishes. With a menu full of recognizable dishes - from Peking duck to wasabi king prawns - Feed Back prides itself on using only the best ingredients.

name: Marktlokal
description: Fashionable restaurant focusing on regional cuisine made from seasonal produce. Visit on Saturdays for their highly-popular fish and chips special - book ahead to be safe. Also offers a large range of wines and beer.

name: UUU
description: Upscale private dining space serving contemporary Chinese cuisine. Accommodating just nine people, the restaurant offers a tasting menu crafted from locally sourced produce with traditional tea pairings.

name: Torbar
description: Steak, caviar, oysters, cigars. A relative newcomer to Mitte, Torbar has quickly turned into a Torstraße scene with prices to match. Plentiful outdoor seating at this French corner haunt.

name: Enzo Sushi Bar
description: Landlocked Berlin doesn't seem like it should be a sushi haven, yet somehow new spots serving immensely high quality fish worth trying keep popping up. Enzo is definitely one of them. Food is impeccable. Setting has a sultry vibe.

name: The Berlin Art Market by the Zeughaus
description: Open-air stalls line the Spree promenade every weekend with original prints, jewelry, and paintings. Artists sell their own work under rows of umbrellas, chatting with crowds crossing Museum Island.

name: Café Drop
description: Calm Mitte cafe serving massive Turkish breakfast platters and copper pans of menemen. The room runs steady during the week with open laptops and matcha lattes, shifting to heavy brunch service on weekends.

name: Kesselhaus in der Kulturbrauerei
description: Industrial brewery boiler house running a steady rotation of live gigs, club nights, and festivals. High ceilings and exposed brick wrap around the mid-sized standing floor, keeping shows loud and close to the stage.

name: Galerie im Turm
description: Single-room contemporary art gallery sitting at the base of a monumental 1950s tower on Karl-Marx-Allee. The compact space cycles through free exhibitions highlighting Berlin-based artists.

name: PLÖTTJES
description: Intimate Kreuzberg ceramics studio running beginner-friendly wheel-throwing and hand-building workshops. Potter's wheels and spacious work tables sit alongside shelves of handcrafted clay pieces for sale.

name: Klinke
description: Casual and modern restaurant in Kreuzberg that reimagines German childhood dishes in a tapas-style format. Bring a group of friends and order from all corners of the menu. Also, enjoy a solid selection of drinks.

name: Atelier Culinário - Sabine Hueck
description: Colorful Schöneberg cooking studio arranged like an eclectic private home. Sabine Hueck leads hands-on Brazilian workshops at the central island before the room settles into a shared dinner.

name: float Berlin Mitte Wellness
description: Private rooms hold open saltwater basins for weightless floating, spacious enough for solo guests or couples. The focus is deep sensory deprivation, often followed by a massage.

name: Prince
description: Berlin likes Asian fusion? It's not a great thing because it's really hard to do right. Prince does a good job though. Alluring vibe with excellent cocktails makes for a solid date spot.

name: Vietnamese Restaurant Anjoy
description: Vietnamese restaurant where traditional meets modern. Expect classic Asian flavors with some added flair - look no further than the "Flying Noodles" special. Occupies a prime position on a leafy street corner.

name: Betahaus
description: Fantastic place to be productive. Plenty of power, space, and wifi. It doubles as a cafe so you can grab a cup of coffee and some food while you catch up on emails, work on a project, or do whatever it is you need to do 💪.

name: Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin
description: Massive historic library running on strict scholarly quiet and a busy ground-floor locker system. Students trade bags for provided baskets before claiming workstations under the natural light of the central glass cube.

name: Oday Deli (Ở Đây Deli)
description: Warm, wood-paneled cafe beside Weinbergspark serving a Vietnamese spin on all-day breakfast. Wide sidewalk tables fill quickly on sunny mornings for black sesame French toast and sweet coconut coffee.

name: Merz b. Schwanen
description: Warm Mitte clothing shop selling heavy-duty, seamless basics made on century-old machines. Racks of thick loopwheeled t-shirts and henleys sit among vintage industrial furniture and natural wood.

name: Bravo Bravko
description: Probably the best cheesecakes in Kreuzberg. Quaint, cozy, and warm on cold days with outdoor seating available during the summers. Vegan options and coffee are of course available... it's still in Berlin after all.

name: Boros Collection
description: Art gallery located in a repurposed bunker (once Berlin's first techno club!) that exhibits modern architecture and contemporary artwork.

name: Pool und Cigars
description: Of a few popular billiard halls, Pool und Cigars is on the nicer end. Tucked into the Kulturbrauerei, the building itself is something to see and they often have live sports going on a project. Rare for Berlin!

name: Stadion An der Alten Försterei
description: It's virtually impossible to get tickets to a FC Union game, but if for some reason the opportunity arises, Alte Försterei is a soccer environment that's hard to match anywhere in Europe.

name: The Lir
description: About as close to an Irish ☘️ pub as you can get in Berlin. Wonderful fish and chips along with a great Guinness pour. Solid place to come catch a game 🏉 as well.

name: Grünfisch
description: Intimate Graefekiez dining room running as a true one-man show. The owner handles the whole space himself, cooking and serving modern Sicilian dishes with subtle Asian touches alongside regional wines.

name: Daluma
description: Daluma is a vegan's delight, serving up smoothies, vibrant bowls, and great coffee. The flavors will excite the omnivores amongst us too - it's that good. Their avocado and toast is out of this world 🥑.

name: Café Schöngrau
description: Beautiful café offering imaginative brunch dishes with a twist, complemented by robust coffee. Notable for its fresh ingredients and distinct bagel pairings. Inviting space accented by artful floral displays.

name: MOII Cafe
description: Tiny Charlottenburg cafe serving Hong Kong milk tea and airy chiffon roll cakes. Handmade ceramics and crochet goods line the compact room, leaving just a few tables that fill fast.

name: Hebbel am Ufer (HAU)
description: Grand Art Nouveau theater from 1908, now a key stage for contemporary international dance and performance. The program is avant-garde and globally sourced – most productions include English surtitles.

name: Wiener Brot
description: Small Mitte storefront baking thick-crusted Austrian sourdoughs and traditional pastries. Heavy wood-fired loaves, apple strudels, and savory rolls go straight from the takeaway counter to the sidewalk benches outside.

name: Thelonius Bar
description: Thelonius is renowned not just for the great cocktails, but for the super friendly bartenders who mix them up against a backdrop of jazzy vibes.

name: Bar Neiro
description: Immersive listening bar tucked away for a sensory adventure. Offers a meticulously selected vinyl collection and a focused cocktail menu, wrapped in a cozy, intentional setting.

name: etwas. kleines
description: Tiny Friedrichshain bakery pulling espresso and boxing handcrafted croissants for takeaway. Morning lines form early on the busy sidewalk for classic, savory, and miso-caramel flavors handed over a brown-tiled counter.

name: Fine Bagels
description: Don't let the name fool you... these bagels are much more than just fine 😍🥯. This cafe doubles as a bookshop so don't be shy grabbing a book and sitting a spell. Not a bad place to spend an afternoon.

name: Black Light Mini Golf
description: Entertaining spot for a rainy day or a unique date night. Have a little friendly competition on the glow-in-the-dark mini-golf course. They sell drinks and 3D glasses if you're looking to add a little challenge to your game ⛳️.

name: Du Bonheur
description: A little piece of Paris in Berlin 🍮. While you can grab light meals here, be warned that the gorgeously presented French pastries are absolutely out of this world. You'd be challenged to pick just one, but go for the millefeuile.

name: Breathe
description: Minimalist beauty boutique stocking small-batch skincare and natural cosmetics. The quiet space smells of botanical oils and runs at a slow, deliberate pace.

name: Kuchen von Gaia
description: Busy Kreuzberg market counter serving traditional Italian sweets. Crisp Sicilian cannoli shells are piped to order with sweet ricotta and pistachio while the owner hands out fresh samples.

name: Museum Island
description: Unique museum complex on Spreeinsel in the heart of Berlin. The island comprises five museums, and the landmark Berlin Cathedral. It's connected to Brandenburg Tor by a metro, where there are many other sights to explore.

name: Wochenmarkt Boxhagener Platz
description: On Saturdays it's a farmers market with fresh produce, meat, baked good, and flowers 💐. On Sundays it's a flea market. Busy area with wonderful bars, cafes, and restaurants nearby.

name: Museum of Musical Instruments
description: Sunlit, terraced galleries at the Kulturforum hold five centuries of European musical history. The collection spans from Prussian court flutes to a massive 1929 Wurlitzer organ played during regular live demos.

name: EIGEN+ART Lab
description: Experimental project space tucked into a courtyard off Torstraße. The small white room sits behind a buzzer, cycling through installations and video work by emerging artists.

name: Berlin University of the Arts
description: Major arts university serving as a public venue for concerts and exhibitions. The 1950s concert hall stages symphony and jazz, while student degree shows fill the Neo-Baroque main building.

name: BARRED
description: Unpretentious bar serving classic cocktails and natural wines with the familiarity of a friend's living room. Free popcorn is a given, and smoking is allowed inside.

name: ZOLA - Paul-Lincke-Ufer - Kreuzberg
description: Neapolitan pizzeria on Paul-Lincke-Ufer turning out blistered, wood-fired pies. Crowds pack the tight interior or spill onto the sidewalk for wine and sunsets by the canal.

name: fa:me Gastrobar
description: Warm Neukölln dining room serving ten-course Mediterranean tasting menus from an open kitchen. The owners run the floor, pouring wine and delivering shared plates over long, relaxed dinners.

name: Viniculture
description: Spacious Charlottenburg bottle shop stocking low-intervention and biodynamic European wines. Staff pull rare orange vintages and Pet-Nats from the shelves, talking through tasting notes and pouring samples on Saturdays.

name: Sunyoga
description: Hot yoga venue holding a variety of classes and courses. Welcoming to all, the friendly studio introduces patrons to the practice of Bikram Yoga. Studio temperatures are regulated and range between 35°C and 40°C.

name: Long March Canteen
description: Creative interpretations of traditional Cantonese dishes offered in both pre-fix and à la carte. Low-lit, sultry interior in industrial-chic setting that's equally suits dates and bigger groups.

name: Berliner Ensemble
description: Historic riverside theater staging Bertolt Brecht classics and contemporary plays. The ornate, red-seated main hall runs German-language performances with English subtitles.

name: Olympiastadion Berlin
description: Stadium built for the 1936 Olympic Games in Berlin. They still host matches and concerts here as well as allow visitors on non-game days. Bring good shoes for a lot of walking. Nice spot for history and sports buffs.

name: C/O Berlin
description: Contemporary museum for photography and visual media 🎨. If you are a photographer or just a fan of photography 📷 C/O is a must.

name: Calli. the coffee club
description: Stylish newcomer pouring specialty coffee and matcha. The cozy, well-furnished room is dog-friendly, with fresh pastries on the counter.

name: tigertörtchen
description: Compact Nikolaiviertel patisserie serving custom-roasted coffee alongside handmade, miniature cupcakes. The bite-sized scale means picking three or four different flavors at once and eating them outside under the trees.

name: Sword Master Noodle
description: Snug Prenzlauer Berg dining room serving chewy Korean knife-cut noodles. The chef slices fresh dough behind a glass partition while massive bowls of spicy broth and giant dumplings land on the tight tables.

name: Bar La Gioia
description: Italian day bar in Mitte running from morning espresso to evening aperitivo. The terrace and modern dining room fill with fresh vodka pasta and rounds of Negronis.

name: P61 Gallery
description: Dark, industrial Schöneberg gallery showing digital and new media art. Large LED screens play computer-generated visuals set to electronic soundscapes, while drinks from the bar are carried freely through the blacked-out rooms.

name: Literary Colloquium Berlin
description: Red brick lakeside villa hosting residencies, workshops, and events for writers and readers. Public readings, summer publishing festivals, and silent reading sessions fill the waterfront grounds and garden.

name: Volume One Gastro Bar
description: Neukölln gastro bar pairing precise cocktails with a kitchen running until midnight. Walk-ins crowd the tables for shared rounds of lamb tacos and crispy potatoes.

name: Alain Snack
description: Historic window counter serving the Ketwurst, a GDR-era hot dog. Soft buns get toasted on a metal spike and stuffed with sausage and secret ketchup for a quick standing lunch.

name: Holzmarkt
description: The ultimate Berlin style beer garden. Perched right on the Spree and the little neighbor to superclub Kater Blau, Holzmarkt has borrowed some of Kater's style and charm to create a one-of-a-kind spot.

name: Tiergarten Park
description: Big park that's home to The Berlin Zoo 🦍. Lots of walking paths, rivers, and spots to sit. Stop at the lakeside beer garden Café am Neuen See for a beer, then head south for some small artsy shops and museums.

name: Mr. Noodle Chen
description: Casual spot for Lanzhou-style hand-pulled noodles, made to order in a glass-walled kitchen. The main event is the beef noodle soup – choose your noodle width at the counter and ask for a free refill.

name: Kitten Deli
description: Wonderful Israeli restaurant with a stunningly designed interior in a former bakery. Comfortable seating both inside and out, and a menu that deviates from the norm in a pleasant way.

name: café gentil
description: French cafe and gallery hybrid on a quiet Prenzlauer Berg street. Deep sofas and art-filled walls create a living room vibe for laptop sessions or lingering over lemon meringue tarts.

name: Katie's Blue Cat
description: Contemporary coffee shop with an open layout and outdoor seating. They offer an excellent selection of home-baked cakes and pastries alongside their proven lineup of coffee and savory snacks. A good spot in Reuterkiez to recharge.

name: Zabriskie Bookstore
description: Kreuzberg specialist stocking a distinct mix of natural history and counterculture. The single room packs in English and German titles on ecology, fungi, and underground music alongside rare zines.

name: Galerie erstererster
description: Glass-fronted project space in Prenzlauer Berg cycling through design pop-ups and art shows. Floor-to-ceiling windows leave the high-ceilinged interior fully exposed to the street.

name: Viktoriapark
description: For when you need a quick retreat from the city lights. Especially gorgeous when the streams are full and the waterfall is flowing, it's a popular sunset picnic spot, and offers the perfect vantage point for epic views of the city.

name: Annelies
description: Sunny, cosy breakfast and lunch spot across from Görlitzer Park with wonderful fresh dishes daily.

name: Hotel Orania Berlin
description: Historic 1912 building on Oranienplatz filled with warm wood and live music. The open ground floor pairs jazz concerts on a Steinway grand with a kitchen roasting Peking-style duck.

name: Precy Delish
description: Intimate Wilmersdorf dining room serving big plates of traditional Nigerian food. The stylish twenty-seat space stays busy on weekends with slow-cooked bowls of Egusi, hot Jollof rice, and spicy pepper soup.

name: CAMERA WORK
description: Two-story Charlottenburg gallery showing exclusively photographic art. Exhibitions hang vintage prints from legends like Helmut Newton alongside modern fashion and portrait work.

name: Bottega Seppel
description: Lively Charlottenburg neighborhood spot pairing a deep wine list with seasonal European plates like beef tartare and whipped ricotta. Vinyl plays over candlelit, tightly packed tables meant for lingering.

name: Didi Pa
description: Small Neukölln dining room serving traditional Ghanaian stews, jollof rice, and fufu. The cash-only space runs busy on weekends with bowls of spicy peanut soup and fried plantains.

name: Pastis
description: Intimate French brasserie on a quiet residential square, run by a husband-and-wife team. The Michelin Bib Gourmand spot serves a surprise tasting menu – book well in advance.

name: Fes
description: Berlin Turkish BBQ at its peak. Phenomenal. Reservation necessary. Worth a visit for meat eaters.

name: Prater Biergarten
description: Between here and Cafe am Neuen See you have your idyllic Hollywood painting of a classic southern German style beer garden covered. It's a nice spot that fits the vibe (vibe!!) of Prenzlauer Berg, but also a bit on the pricey side.

name: Saunafloß MS Aufguss
description: Wood-fired sauna raft on the Rummelsburger Bucht for private sessions. The panoramic hot room fuels a cycle of deep sweating and immediate plunges into the Spree.

name: Haubentaucher
description: A scene. Pools with a party atmosphere are hard to come by in the summer, so among the slim pickings you're either trying to go here, Badeschiff, or if you know someone, the Soho House. The line can be very long - try and book ahead.

name: Mogg
description: Famous for their pastrami sandwich and New York-style cheesecake. It's good, it's good! But it's definitely not New York. Try and grab a table outside for some Auguststraße people watching.

name: SoFi
description: Phenomenal bakery in a hidden Mitte courtyard. From fresh pastries to homemade focaccia, everything is worth trying at least once. Coffee available as well.

name: OST Hafen Berlin
description: Massive riverside power plant hosting heavy techno nights, live gigs, and open-air food festivals. The multi-room industrial layout opens directly onto the banks of the Spree for long outdoor parties.

name: Unfold Studio
description: Light-filled yoga and Pilates studio tucked into a Kreuzberg courtyard. Small group classes run in the minimalist main room, alongside a cozy couch area for lingering over fresh tea before or after a session.

name: Barra
description: Cozy restaurant with food that could be worth a Michelin Star. Small plates and healthy whole ingredients with wonderful seafood. Prices aren't too bad and the natural wine is excellent.

name: Crackers
description: Initially founded as a club, this easy-to-miss space now does food, drinks, and music all at once. If you're there just for drinks, the cocktails 🍸 are excellent. Trendy location, where the later the night goes, the more lively it gets.

name: Yoga On The Move
description: Bright, wood-filled Schöneberg yoga studio running daily Vinyasa and breathwork classes. Sandy walls and indoor swings sit next to a large lounge area used for post-class tea.

name: Nutts Thai Kitchen
description: Small Friedrichshain dining room run by three siblings cooking traditional Northern Thai food with serious heat. The kitchen skips takeout entirely, sending rich bowls of Khao Soi and spicy papaya salads straight to small tables.

name: One More Chapter
description: Book-lined Friedrichshain cafe serving a South African-inspired menu next door to its partner bookshop. Plates of bunny chow and spicy peri-peri rice bowls share table space with open paperbacks and afternoon coffee.

name: Katz Orange
description: It's been years yet somehow Katz Orange is still hyped as if they were a new restaurant? Comes with both positives and negatives. Food is excellent though a bit on the pricey side. Beautiful location, professional staff, solid drinks.

name: Paolo Pinkel
description: Unique restaurant concept with Peruvian, Korean, Italian, and Cypriot food stands, serviced by a full bar with an upbeat lounge area. Great place to start before a night out in Neukölln.

name: Brasserie Chez Manu
description: Classic French brasserie serving onion soup and steak tartare on the edge of Halensee. Live piano plays in a warm dining room opening onto a waterfront terrace.

name: Blaue Stunde
description: Open-air bar running out of a red-and-white tiled signal building on the edge of Tempelhofer Feld. Cobalt blue chairs spread across the grass for afternoon spritzes and draft beer as the sun sets over the old airfield.

name: Haus Ungarn
description: Former East Berlin cultural center running as a sprawling venue for club nights and parties near Alexanderplatz. Original 1970s wood paneling sits alongside raw concrete floors, with an outdoor terrace facing the TV Tower.

name: Kunsthaus Dahlem
description: Monumental brick exhibition space on the edge of the Grunewald forest showing German post-war modern art. Massive windows bring light into the high-ceilinged former studio, which opens out to a quiet sculpture garden and cafe.

name: Brücke Museum
description: Low-slung modernist museum on the edge of the Grunewald forest showing vivid German Expressionist art. Floor-to-ceiling windows connect the quiet viewing rooms directly to the pine trees outside.

name: BUNA Café
description: Quiet Charlottenburg cafe pouring standard espresso alongside traditional Ethiopian coffee. Daily flat whites run through a La Marzocco machine, while clay pots and wooden mortars handle the slow, ceremonial brewing.

name: Dieselhaus
description: Relatively new Mitte brewery with plenty of outdoor seating and a scenic view of the New Synagogue. Wide variety of beers on tap with a friendly and knowledgeable staff available to answer questions.

name: Sonntags-Club
description: Historic LGBTQ+ center and bar anchoring the neighborhood since the GDR era. Readings, support groups, and casual drinks fill a space built for conversation rather than dancing.

name: Villa Rixdorf
description: Excellent beer garden in Rixdorf to come and enjoy a beer in the sun. Food options in include German staples, though aren't as recommendable.

name: Museum of Decorative Arts
description: Imposing concrete halls at the Kulturforum hold a massive timeline of European design. Quiet floors move from medieval gold and Renaissance furniture to modern industrial pieces and high fashion.

name: Zimt & Mehl
description: Wonderful canal side cafe that serves an excellent brunch (both German and Turkish!) alongside a variety of coffee options. Great for outdoor people watching.

name: Berlin Zoo and Tierpark
description: Enormous zoo featuring pandas, elephants, lions, and more. Good spot to bring kids and have a walk.

name: Space Meduza
description: Relatively new to the Kreuzberg bar scene, Space Meduza is full of friendly faces that haven't seem to have yet bent to the usual saltiness that comes with Berlin nightlife. Alien space themed decorations and a few solid beers on tap.

name: Wannsee
description: The perfect fairytale-like vistas make this well worth the trip, even for an overnight or weekend stay. Think lush forests, gleaming lakes, and neoclassical architecture.

name: The Ritz-Carlton, Berlin
description: Your classic Ritz-Carlton style property. Close to Potsdamer Platz, the Tiergarten, and other Berlin sightseeing.

name: Wellenwerk
description: Compound with a beer garden and surf school (artificial waves!). You may not have come to Berlin to surf, but that doesn't mean you can't catch some waves 🏄🏼.

name: Landwehr Canal
description: Tree-shaded canal running through central Berlin with continuous paths and wide grassy banks. The water's edge works as an active linear park, busy with daily cyclists, bustling markets, and groups sharing drinks in the grass.

name: Berliner Republik
description: Riverside bar and restaurant that prides itself on Berlin specialties, with a wide range of draft beers on tap. Bit of a Mitte tourist spot, so skip the food, but perfectly fine to grab a drink by the river.

name: Friedrichshain
description: Pre-reunification, Friedrichshain was a largely blue-collar district with strongly left politics (which still hold today). Recent gentrification over the past 20 years has pushed many of the squats out, slowly changing the cultural fabric.

name: Generator Berlin Mitte
description: Stylish hostel offering dorms with free Wi-Fi and shared bathrooms with lockers. Also included are a cafe and bar with an industrial design, a lounge with 24-hour access, and laundry facilities. Budget stay but centrally located.

name: Zum Schwalbenschwanz
description: An absolute locals spot and just a generally great place for a weekday drink. Wonderful sours (whiskey, pisco, etc) to go with a more extensive cocktail and beer menu. They do the occasional comedy or trivia night as well.

name: Night Kitchen
description: Tucked into a cute little brick building in the Heckmann Höfe, Night Kitchen is easy to miss but wonderful if you can find it. Would recommend going with the pre-fix menu/wine pairing, as the staff is super friendly and go above and beyond.

name: Tiefwerder Wiesen
description: Unbelievable stretch of wilderness right by the city. Go here for hikes, walks, and just general zen vibes.

name: Dussmann Bookshop
description: Take their word: "Berlin is culture. And culture is Dussmann das KulturKaufhaus." A treasure trove - three floors of books, records, films. You may never want to leave.

name: Princess Cheesecake
description: Reliable eatery where the range of options seems endless, but the classic cheesecake is always the winner. Don't be afraid to venture into the great sweet unknown though!

name: Lokal
description: About as farm to table a feel of a restaurant as you can find. Has a bit of that Mitte bourgeois feel to it, but in the summer sitting outside on Linienstraße with some fresh dressed up ingredients and a drink in hand is hard to beat.

name: Brlo Brwhouse
description: Modern "American style" brewery. They have a range of IPAs, some decent BBQ options, and plenty of space to have fun and relax.

name: Konnopke's Imbiss
description: Tucked underneath the U2 train line closed to Eberswalder Strasse, Konnopke's is arguably Berlin's best place for a currywurst. Open odd hours, so check in advance.

name: Reichstag
description: Tourist heavy destination but very historically relevant and interesting, so it's definitely worth the trip and the cost of a tour. The modern glass dome contrasts with the historical building in a very Berlin way.

name: Chicha
description: Super high quality fish with a frequently changing menu based on what's fresh. Nice outdoor seating - great for some pisco sours in the summer heat. A little on the pricey side.

name: Babylon Kino
description: First built in the late 1920s, this incredible cinema can be found right in the middle of Berlin's Rosa Luxemburg Platz. Silent films are accompanied by live orchestral music for an old-timey experience that should not be missed.

name: Berlin Design Week
description: Design Week is a time for creatives to come together and discuss current trends, but it's also a time to think about future design and sustainability. Happens annually in May.

name: Katerschmaus
description: The sister restaurant of super-club Kater Blau and beer garden Holzmarkt 25, Katerschmaus is a waterfront hidden gem that's great for lunch in the sun or a weekend pre-night out dinner. Fresh and local ingredients.

name: Chicago Williams BBQ
description: American home style barbeque, with a focus on carefully prepared and smoked meat 🥩 and German craft beer 🍻.

name: Badeschiff
description: Perfect place for a tan and a cocktail in the summer. A beach bar and a fine-sand beach in a city. 🏖️ Swimming? Take a dip in their outdoor floating pool in the Spree River. Right next to CDV and a few other clubs.

name: Kuchi Kant
description: Typically Asian fusion restaurants come bearing a red flag, but Kuchi knows how to not overextend itself and does simple dishes with high quality ingredients very well. Two locations, one on Kuchi Kant and Kuchi Mitte.

name: Kumpelnest 3000
description: Originally opened in 1987 as an exhibition space, Kumplnest has seen many lives and is hard to label as "just" a bar. Very LGBTQ+ friendly, expect fun music, exciting drinks, and a riot of an ambiance.

name: Petit Bijou
description: Wonderful little cozy cafe right by the Spree with a phenomenal view of the Bode Museum and Museum Island. While the food and drinks are good, it's definitely best to come here for the outdoor seating on a sunny day.

name: Kiez Sauna
description: Cozy sauna in the heart of Friedrichshain offering two saunas, one steam room, and a well-stocked bar. Known for being clean, boasting a friendly atmosphere, and being one of the city's quieter spa facilities.

name: Hamam
description: Women’s Turkish sauna in the heart of Kreuzberg with a Hamam bath and private treatments - the facilities are designed to cleanse the skin and leave visitors feeling rejuvenated. Bookings can be made online.

name: India Club Berlin
description: Elegant, mahogany-paneled dining room in the Adlon Palais serving high-end North Indian cuisine. The kitchen runs traditional clay tandoor ovens, turning out farm-sourced lamb and rich curries for multi-course evening dates.

name: Clärchens Ballhaus
description: Wonderful beer garden that makes for a charming date night. Have some German-Italian food, enjoy the live music, and take to the ballroom dance floor. If you have two left feet, no worries – they offer dance classes 💃💃💃.

name: Birgit
description: Beer garden during the day, bar at night, club in the early morning. Somewhat self-branded as a "magical playground for adults", with three dance floors playing techno to house to everything but, it's basically true.

name: Bierhof Rüdersdorf
description: Unique location not because of where it is, but because of what it's next to (Berghain). If you're there anytime on Saturday or Sunday the soundtrack you'll be listening to is techno. Three levels with some good sunny spots to be found.

name: Neues Museum
description: The "New Museum" houses some of the oldest art in Berlin with a vast collection of Egyptian art and prehistoric archeology. Completed in 1855, it was heavily damaged in World War II and restored by David Chipperfield in recent decades.

name: Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe
description: Profoundly moving outdoor memorial park made up of 2,700 concrete pillars in memory of the Jewish people who perished during the Holocaust.

name: Hotel Oderberger Berlin
description: Restored 19th-century public bathhouse operating as a boutique hotel in Prenzlauer Berg. The original vaulted swimming hall holds a 20-meter pool, running alongside a multi-level boiler house restaurant and fireplace bar.

name: Onette
description: Corner luncheonette with the feel of a German pub, serving diner staples and local comfort food. The signature hash brown special is a neighborhood ritual – it often sells out before noon.

name: Victoria Bar
description: Plush interiors in a way that feels like you're on the set of a movie. They pride themselves on the pleasure of drinking, and it shows. Cocktails are mixed to perfection and made to suit your personal preferences.

name: Father Carpenter
description: Trendy cafe well-known for its inventive brunch and speciality coffees. Tucked into a charming "alt-bau" courtyard that is worth the visit to see as well.

name: The Tree
description: Asian fusion rice bowls and noodle soups with Szechuan influence. The menu also includes small plates - a great option for exploring different flavors. The space itself boasts a minimalist yet cozy concept.

name: Biererei
description: Beer bar with a huge selection of taps (even IPAs!) on Oranienstrasse. Friendly and knowledgeable owner with additional curbside seating.

name: Minigolf am Insulaner Park - Berlin Schöneberg
description: Shaded 18-hole minigolf course tucked under a dense canopy of old trees in Schöneberg. Retro 1960s lanes wrap around a blue wooden kiosk slinging cold beers and snacks for birthday parties and casual afternoon rounds.

name: Prinzipal Kreuzberg
description: Live burlesque shows most nights. Friendly bartenders, excellent cocktails, fresh ingredients.

name: Kink Bar & Restaurant
description: Loungey bar and restaurant with an outdoor patio highlighting imaginative cocktails and small plates, plus seasonal farm-to-table fare. Great for an outdoor drink in the summer, or cozy cocktail in the winter.

name: Mamecha
description: Japanese matcha café serving a mix of savory and sweet fare. Not exclusive to its green tea theme, patrons can enjoy onigiri and bento boxes before indulging in mochi and cheesecake. Also offers the usual roster of coffees and tea.

name: Weißensee Kunsthochschule Berlin
description: Working art school spanning a former 1930s chocolate factory and midcentury Bauhaus extensions. Bright studios and nineteen practical workshops fill with materials and student projects, opening up for the annual summer open house.

name: Coffee Drink Your Monkey
description: Jarring name aside, this cafe serves a stellar line-up of specialty coffee, baked goods, breakfast bowls, and light lunches. Boasts an airy interior but the best seats in the house are on the front terrace - weather permitting.

name: Early Bird Gelato
description: Compact Prenzlauer Berg cafe serving traditional Italian gelato layered with a spatula. Steady lines spill out the door on warm afternoons for fresh pistachio, Basque cheesecake, and rich espresso poured over cold gelato.

name: Tribeca Ice Cream Prenzlauer Berg
description: Plant-based Prenzlauer Berg scoop shop serving raw, soy-free ice cream made from nut milks and natural sweeteners. Pastel benches line the sidewalk for eating scoops of hazelnut baobab and blue coconut.

name: America Memorial Library
description: Large modernist library in Kreuzberg running as a daily neighborhood hub for reading, studying, and Sunday coffee. Light-filled open floors hold dense book stacks alongside vinyl listening stations and borrowable original art.

name: Chipi Chipi Bombón
description: Small Friedrichshain ice cream shop serving traditional Argentine dulce de leche and inventive flavors like lime, coriander, and chili. Space is tight, leaving just two sidewalk benches for late-night scoops and tasting bowls.

name: Literature Forum at the Brecht House
description: Intimate literary venue operating from Bertolt Brecht’s former home. Writers and critics gather for evening readings, book launches, and sharp political discussions.

name: Basalt
description: Botanical cocktail bar with green-tiled walls and plants suspended from the ceiling. The seasonal menu focuses on proprietary drinks. Arrive early on weekends to secure a seat.

name: Bode Museum
description: This beautiful building is at the very tip of Museum Island, with a great view of the river. Inside, there's a wide range of statues and artifacts from the Byzantine Era. Some of the most beautiful in Berlin.

name: Berliner Unterwelten
description: Museum that is perfect for a rainy day because it's all underground. Visit the former WWII bunkers and learn about the city's history during the war. The guides are professional and knowledgeable.

name: Ankerklause
description: Popular canalside bar with a terrace and lively vibe. This small bar has a ship interior design and is a canal-side favorite for both Kreuzberg locals and tourists alike.

name: Karl-Marx-Allee
description: In Berlin's Friedrichshain and Mitte, Karl-Marx-Allee is a monumental socialist boulevard built by the German Democratic Republic. It runs from Alexanderplatz to the Frankfurter Tor. Today, the boulevard is named after Karl Marx.

name: Die Apotheken Bar
description: Cocktail bar housed within, as its name suggests, a former apothecary. Dimly lit and with vintage decor, the bar delivers an intimate ambiance. Drinks are creative, and their cost reflects the quality.

name: Benedict
description: An upscale breakfast place that specializes in boozy brunches. Popular choices include the shakshuka, avocado bagel, and pancakes. Be sure to make a reservation in advance, as it can get busy.

name: Panke Culture
