description: From the outside, this grungy bar / nightclub may just look like an old brick factory covered in street art, but stop inside for a drink, some music, and a cool vibe. You can even come for lunch and sit in their garden out back.

name: Henne
description: Iconic restaurant which first opened its doors in 1908. Well-known for its 1/2 roasted chicken, which is traditionally served alongside potato salad, sauerkraut, and a slice of bread.

name: Brandenburger Tor
description: Iconic gate that, while interesting historically, serves as a bit of a tourist trap for people looking for Instagram shots. It's best seen walking through on your way to the Tiergarten and a beer at Cafe am Neuen See.

name: 44 Brekkie
description: Breakfast and brunch staple of the stylish district of Rykestraße specializing in egg drop sandwiches - from bacon and garlic to salmon and avocado. Minimal interior and exterior seating areas promote calm social gatherings over food.

name: Aachen
description: Historical city where the borders of Germany, Belgium, and the Netherlands meet. First developed as a natural bathing town in Roman times, Aachen's fame now extends to its UNESCO cathedral, heritage buildings, and young vibe.

name: Botanical Garden and Botanical Museum
description: Expansive 43-hectare botanical park with wooded paths and outdoor gardens that take hours to walk. Towering Art Nouveau glasshouses anchor the grounds, filled with humid tropical heat, giant bamboo, and rare water lilies.

name: Curry 36
description: From a wooden wagon to a Berlin institution. Curry 36 is one of the city's most frequented snack bars, providing patrons with hearty and affordable eats into the early hours. Currywurst and chips aplenty.

name: ACUD Theater
description: Small arts venue staging theater performances and showing niche indie films. Cozy inside and with an eclectic outdoor courtyard. Patrons can socialize pre and post-show at the informal bar. Something for everyone.

name: Kinderbauernhof Görlitzer Park
description: Children’s petting zoo located in Görlitzer Park. Ideal for animal lovers of all ages, the farm houses a wide range of animals and feeding stations - from ducks and chickens to pigs and even miniature horses. Also features playgrounds.

name: Maru
description: A bit of an under-the-radar Korean spot compared to many of the mainstays, but Maru is a nice alternative. Excellent kimchi, wonderful bibimbap, and many vegetarian options. You might miss the k-bbq though.

name: Treptow-Köpenick
description: The city's largest borough, charming Treptow-Köpenick is known for its old town, castle, and many lakes and forests. Make sure to visit Treptower Park and the Soviet War Memorial.

name: Tempelhof Airport
description: Decommissioned 1930s airport turned vast public park and cultural venue. Long walking tours navigate the monumental limestone terminal, passing through old check-in halls, underground bunkers, and abandoned US military spaces.

name: WILLIAM FAN
description: Dual-concept flagship split between a street-facing gift shop and a hidden courtyard boutique. Gender-fluid garments hang among modular steel fixtures in the back, while the front room stocks signature fortune cookie bags.

name: Eins44
description: Inventive plates with familiar ingredients and textures presented in a contemporary manner. Located in a modernized former distillery.

name: Strandbad Plötzensee
description: Historic 1920s lido on a glacial lake with a sandy beach, wooden pier, and open-water swimming. Towels and volleyball games pack the shore on hot afternoons, while evenings bring DJs, cold drinks, and dancing by the water.

name: Apló Greek Kitchen & Foods
description: Cozy, fast-casual Mitte kitchen turning out hearty plates of traditional Greek street food. Warm, fluffy corn pitas come loaded with lamb souvlaki or chicken gyros alongside hand-cut herb fries and thick tzatziki.

name: Ristorante Osteria Centrale
description: Cozy, unpretentious Charlottenburg dining room serving straightforward Tuscan plates and high-end Italian wine. The tight, cash-only restaurant runs a steady dinner service with the owners working the floor.

name: Café Augusta
description: Bustling Neukölln cafe serving large plates of Eggs Benedict and croissant French toast alongside specialty coffee. The cozy space runs loud and crowded during weekend brunch, while weekday mornings leave open tables for laptops.

name: Hotel Augusta Berlin
description: Historic Berlin hotel sitting on a quiet side street just off the busy Kurfürstendamm. A quirky layout leads across a covered inner courtyard to high-ceilinged rooms, some with private saunas or street-facing balconies.

name: Salumeria da Pino
description: Classic Italian deli and enoteca running as a cozy Charlottenburg dining room. Dinners come straight from the glass counter, pairing fresh antipasti and cured meats with bottles pulled from the massive wine selection.

name: El Borriquito
description: Old-school Spanish restaurant pouring sangria and serving generous plates of tapas and paella until the early morning. The cramped room stays loud and tightly packed, reaching full volume when the live guitar starts around nine.

name: NAUMANNS Biergarten
description: Open-air Schöneberg beer garden set in a multi-use commercial park. Long tables fill with neighborhood locals and nearby workers splitting cold beer and Roman-style pinsa.

name: FAT HENRY Berlin
description: Intimate Mitte seafood spot running with the energy of a Japanese bar. Chefs work in full view, passing fresh crudo, hand rolls, and oysters straight across the counter.

name: Cevicheria
description: Nice little spot for a daily changing assortment of fresh ceviche and pisco sours. Dresdener Strasse is a hidden gem in Kreuzberg with plentiful after dinner drink spots to visit as well (Würgeengel, Ottorink Weinbar, Trödler).

name: Der kleine August
description: Intimate Mitte wine bar pouring artisan French bottles in a warm, low-lit room. Staff in blue worker jackets slice charcuterie to order behind the counter, serving small plates of cheese and pâté alongside natural pours.

name: Puffer-Imbiss
description: Busy Hermannplatz kiosk frying massive, crispy potato pancakes. Hot Kartoffelpuffer come out fast on real plates, paired with sweet apple sauce or savory herb quark for a hearty lunch right on the square.

name: Two Planets
description: Minimalist Neukölln cafe pouring specialty coffee and serving thick, loaded toasts. The quiet, plant-filled room stays relaxed through the morning, running a tight menu of simple breakfast bowls and cold brew.

name: MS Hoppetosse
description: Moored ship on the Spree River running minimal house and techno sets through a heavy sound system. Low ceilings keep the bass tight on the compact dance floor, leaving the open top deck for fresh air and early morning sunrises.

name: WEIN BUNNY
description: Intimate Friedrichshain bottle shop pouring natural and organic wines near Boxhagener Platz. Shelves of takeaway bottles surround a ten-seat wooden tasting counter, while a sun terrace sits out front for wine and light snacks.

name: Sound Metaphors
description: Kreuzberg record shop and label hub heavily stocked with well-sorted new and used electronic vinyl. Bins of house, techno, and Italo carry detailed staff notes for deep digging before testing tracks at the listening stations.

name: Richard Bistro
description: Landmarked dining room where modern art hangs beneath high wood ceilings and gothic stained-glass windows. The menu is similarly composed, serving market-fresh Mediterranean dishes like Fines de Claire oysters and saddle of venison.

name: Gemäldegalerie
description: The Gemäldegalerie is among the most significant collections of pre-modern European painting and sculpture, with a vast array of German, Dutch, and Italian masterpieces. An audio guide is recommended to streamline your visit.

name: MS Tapete • Winterpause bis 16.01. • Fine Art Wallpaper
description: Working studio and showroom where fine art wallpaper is designed and printed on-site. The high-resolution patterns are produced as individual sheets – not rolls – and the artist is often present to consult on application.

name: Cafe Ribo
description: Weekday lunch spot serving traditional Swabian comfort food from a tiny kitchen. The focused menu sticks to the classics – homemade Maultaschen and Käsespätzle with fried onions.

name: Chapters Bookshop
description: English-language bookshop curating its shelves by theme – "Power & Resistance" sits next to "Romance & Ruinous." Out back, a quiet secret garden offers a place for reading.

name: Cielo Weinbar
description: Chef-driven wine bar serving Spanish-Italian sharing plates like lamb tonnato and grilled artichokes. A single blue neon cloud glows on the wall of the cozy, stylish room, setting a relaxed fine-dining vibe.

name: Amazingy
description: Natural beauty boutique offering organic body products and skincare. Founded in the Netherlands, this brand has a passion for the good stuff – only stocking cruelty-free products that are gentle on the skin.

name: Isla Coffee
description: Modern and minimalist coffee shop serving fresh roasts to a hip young crowd. Find baked goods and brunch plates alongside the speciality brews. Grab a seat inside when there is space, or outside if the weather permits.

name: Kadó
description: Candy store specializing in the confectionary art of licorice - from sweet to savory. The first of its kind in Kreuzberg, this spot stocks goods from ten countries. Lovers of the candy's acquired taste will struggle to leave empty-handed.

name: Nandi
description: Concept store offering textiles and accessories from 15 different countries. A great place to pick up a gift, customers can find Tuscan ceramics, Peruvian blankets, handcrafted Cypriot jewelry, and Indonesian robes.

name: Sing Blackbird Vintage
description: Vintage clothes store in Neukölln also containing a hip coffeeshop. Known for its well-curated collection, this spot stocks a mix of designer and high-street brands. Refuel and refresh after browsing.

name: Arkonaplatz Market
description: Bi-weekly market on Arkonaplatz where Sundays are for second-hand goods and other knick-knacks, while Fridays are for organic food and drink vendors. Quaint and cosy.

name: Nauta
description: Prenzlauer Berg's go-to Peruvian spot... with the price to match. The food is good and it's presented beautifully, but you'll feel like you were out in NYC instead of in Berlin. Nice ambiance and great bartender.

name: Cafe Anna Blume
description: Upscale cafe with a love for breakfast, coffee, and freshly baked cakes and tarts 🍰. Quaint yet also a Prenzlauer Berg weekend brunch scene, especially when the Kollwitzmarkt is happening.

name: MYKITA Berlin Mitte
description: All-white eyewear flagship displaying handmade Berlin frames across a massive, backlit steel wall. In-house optometrists run exams and fit lenses while staff pull inventory from repurposed airline trolleys.

name: Cafe Luzia
description: A non-smoker bar in Berlin? Can't believe it but it's true. Eclectically laid out with a main center bar that hip 20-somethings huddle around trying to get a drink, it's a good spot to go to start a night.

name: Tylko Space Berlin
description: Physical showroom for the online furniture brand, set up as a series of interconnected rooms. Material swatches sit out for testing while in-house design advisors configure made-to-order shelving and storage.

name: tak Theater Aufbau Kreuzberg
description: Intimate, collectively run performance space tucked in the courtyard of Kreuzberg’s Aufbau Haus. Experimental dance, political plays, and film installations fill a small room set with scattered floor mats and informal seating.

name: Stetson Store Berlin
description: Traditional hatter shop in Mitte carrying a full lineup of fedoras, flat caps, and Western styles. Expert staff pull options from the shelves and handle the sizing to find an exact fit.

name: Pluto
description: Convivial wine bar pouring low-intervention European bottles and simple, rustic plates for sharing. The space is walk-in-only: three dimly lit rooms with a long zinc bar and a large communal table.

name: Synthesizer Museum Berlin
description: Vast private collection of vintage synthesizers where every instrument is meant to be played. The rooms are arranged by decade, with recording stations set up for hands-on experimentation.

name: Verwalterhaus
description: Contemporary art gallery housed in a former cemetery administrator's residence on quiet, historic grounds. Exhibitions, mostly photography, are staged in the empty rooms, using the building's scarred walls as part of the installation.

name: Pickleball.Collective
description: Social pickleball sessions hosted on courts across the city, designed for all skill levels. Equipment is always provided – just book a spot online for beginner lessons or competitive open play.

name: Witty Stories
description: Historic half-timbered cottage set inside a quiet park, serving coffee and cake from a small, bright room. Most seating is outside on a sunny terrace surrounded by rose bushes.

name: Pastiche
description: Specialty coffee shop and curated record store built around a custom hi-fi sound system. By night, the record racks are replaced with tatami mats for immersive listening events.

name: Palast Kiosk
description: Mint-green historic kiosk on Steinplatz functioning as a public platform for local art. Open-air film screenings and workshops fill the plaza, fueled by natural wine and Ethiopian coffee with popcorn.

name: Clash
description: Grimey, but in a good way. It's the kind of bar people come to Berlin for - punk rock vibes where the music is loud and the beer is cheap and plenty 🍻. Nice beer garden patio open outside in the summers. Can be smokey. Foosball tables.

name: Dschungel Bar
description: A living jungle (dschungel!), this is maybe the only place you can come in Berlin during the winter to feel any sort of heat or humidity. Fun little spot that pulls a good crowd and has a friendly bartender. They have fish tanks.

name: Trattoria Breda
description: Orange-drenched Kreuzberg trattoria serving Northern Italian share plates along the Landwehrkanal. Evenings start with canal-side wine and sea bass crudo before the loud, polished dining room turns into a late-night bar scene.

name: barlevain
description: Minimalist Schöneberg corner tavern pairing unfussy German pub food with classic and natural wines. Handmade pork terrines and grilled meats come straight from the open kitchen into a tight room with creaking floorboards.

name: Blomeyers Käse aus Deutschland
description: Spacious Charlottenburg delicatessen selling only artisanal German raw milk cheese. The large central counter holds dozens of wedges from small farm dairies, ready to pair with regional wines and fresh sourdough.

name: Original Feelings
description: Kreuzberg yoga studio running daily movement and meditation classes named after specific emotions. Hempcrete surfaces and painted textiles divide the fluid space into calm, tactile zones for practice and lingering.

name: Talea - Italienisches Botanisches Bistro und Restaurant
description: Italian restaurant and plant shop tucked under the Schöneberg train station. Plates of Venetian cicchetti and squid ink pasta arrive on vintage school desks surrounded by hanging vines and potted plants available to buy.

name: Fabelei
description: Among the many cocktail bar options in Schöneberg, Fabelei might be the best of them. Although it's still flying a bit under the radar, the menu is well thought through and the drinks are excellent. Cute setting with a date night feel.

name: Kaffee 9
description: Coffeehouse and roastery, serving up great coffee as well as beer, wine, and light cocktails. Modernizing the way people view coffee shops, this super popular location offers a reliable meeting spot till late in the evening.

name: Klunkerkranich
description: Overrun by tourists but a view is a view and this one is hard to beat so it's worth the wait. Uniquely Berlin in that it's great to bring kids to during the day, but... you can also party here until 4 am.

name: Zeit für Brot
description: Zeit für Brot, or, "time for bread," is a warm and friendly bakery that welcomes customers to watch as they go about their work. Besides bread, try the raspberry and white chocolate bun, along with the cinnamon and chocolate rolls 🍞🥖.

name: P & T - Paper & Tea - tea shop Berlin
description: Wood-lined specialty tea shop built around open tasting stations. Staff pour impromptu samples over the counter, while shelves hold whole-leaf teas, handmade ceramics, and paper goods.

name: Denizen
description: A hub for community and creativity. Modeled on the idea of a "neighborhood living room", patrons can network and create in a comfortable yet stimulating space. Day passes and monthly memberships are available.

name: David Hasselhoff Museum
description: An acquired taste but undeniably one of Berlin's many unique experiences. Less of a full museum experience and more of a shrine dedicated to the actor. Visit with an open mind and a sense of humor.

name: Alte Milch
description: Specialty cheese counter in Markthalle Neun with a glass-walled cave aging wheels of raw milk cheese. The tight selection is sourced directly from small European farms – staff offer expert advice on everything from Comté to Tuscan Pecorino.

name: Orville’s
description: Bar and café in the former US Air Force casino of Tempelhof Airport, styled like a 1960s airline lounge. The room fills up for Italian aperitivo, classic cocktails, and its popular live jazz nights.

name: Five Elephant Kollwitz
description: Specialty coffee roaster pouring single-origin filter and espresso in a minimalist Prenzlauer Berg space. The house-made cheesecake is the main draw – often paired with a newspaper at one of the outdoor tables.

name: Garten Mitte
description: Minimalist Mitte cafe pouring specialty coffee under original ballroom frescoes. Seating fills a wild, sunny utility garden with raised produce beds, keeping the space quiet for working or lingering over marbled banana bread.

name: German Historical Museum
description: Arguably the most comprehensive archive of German history in the city. Self-described as a place of "enlightenment and understanding of the shared history of Germans and Europeans." Features a new, modern extension.

name: Stilbruch Kaffee
description: Cute cafe with generous portions, perfect for remote work vibes or leisurely brunch. Avocado toast and uniquely flavored beans are favorites.

name: Anna Hirsch Bar
description: Dark-wood bar lit by candles and a mirrored disco ball above the counter. Vinyl records spin behind the bar while cocktails mix with a haze of indoor smoke.

name: Food Technique Berlin
description: Ghost kitchen specializing in take-home ramen kits with light, clear "chintan" broths. Orders are lowered to the street from a second-floor window in a red bucket; occasional pop-ups are the only chance to have it served hot.

name: Kame Bakery
description: Cafe focused on Japanese baked goods, treats, and drinks. Simple in both design and concept, Kame is wonderful to visit for either a quick matcha or for a longer hangout. Very friendly and polite staff.

name: Galerie Deschler
description: Early fixture of Mitte’s post-reunification art scene, showing figurative works from the 'Neue Wilde' movement. The intimate, multi-level space exhibits both established German painters and new international talent.

name: Parfums Lubner - Fragrance Library
description: Curated library of niche perfumes from small, artistic houses, deliberately avoiding major designer brands. Each scent has its own story card – pencils and paper strips are laid out for taking notes.

name: Mischke - Fleischerei & Catering
description: Longstanding Pankow butcher shop running a steady hot lunch counter alongside its fresh meat cases. House-made sausages and hot midday plates move fast, while the main deli cuts regional meats to order.

name: Tekbir Döner
description: Tiny Kreuzberg kebab counter serving traditional Turkish street food since 1979. Hand-stacked slices of beef and lamb fat are shaved straight from the spit into warm bread for fast, cash-only lunches.

name: Manon Brasserie Nouvelle
description: Polished Charlottenburg brasserie serving modern French plates of steak frites, grilled bone marrow, and oysters. Marble floors and wood paneling run past an open kitchen straight into a Mediterranean-style courtyard.

name: Pavillon am Ufer
description: Little drinks and food stand along the Landwehr Canal in Kreuzberg. Perfect for an outdoor summer morning coffee, afternoon aperitif, or evening drink. In the winter, it's one of the best Glühwein-to-go spots along the water.

name: Berlin Botanical Garden
description: The worlds second largest botanical garden 🪴. Beautiful outside and inside the glasshouses 🌴. Stunning light display around Christmas 🎄.

name: Minimal Bar
description: Iconic Friedrichshain establishment on (in)famous Rigaer Strasse. Equal parts mellow and energetic with a very fun little dance floor DJ'd with electronic music until late late late. They also have a ping pong table and beer on tap.

name: Kaffeebar
description: Café and coffee shop serving healthy options in a bright, airy environment. Sustainability-focused, Kaffeebar pours freshly ground coffee alongside a menu containing plenty of vegan and gluten-free options.

name: Burgermeister
description: The best smashburger 🍔 in Berlin. Not quite In-N-Out, but gets close in a pinch. Several locations, but the one built into the old Schlesisches Tor 🚇 public restroom is the original. Great anytime of day but also open late.

name: Berlin Festival of Lights
description: Spectacular event that transforms landmarks across the city through illuminations, projections, and even 3D mapping. October is when the cold starts to bite, but it's well worth walking around for a few hours to take in the lights ✨🏮.

name: Taco Tales
description: Berlin struggles with Mexican food in... every way. Taco Tales is one of ~three places that might tithe you over until you're back in the Americas. There is a nice little market in front where pozole, chiles, and other staples are sold.

name: Macke Prinz
description: Wonderful little kiez bar overlooking Zionskirchplatz ⛪️🌿. It's hard to find a more picturesque spot to sit outside during the summer. In the winters it transforms into a perfect (low-lit and smoky) place to huddle up away from the cold.

name: Osmans Töchter
description: Excellent Turkish style tapas in a cute setting. Very Instagrammable but the food is also absolutely excellent and they've gone out of their way to create a modern, light menu. Great cocktails as well. Good to make a reservation ahead.

name: Kater Blau
description: The ying to Berghain's yang. Colorful outfits, lively music, open, and outdoors with a beautiful location right on the Spree.

name: City Chicken
description: There are more hyped half-chicken places in Berlin, but ask any taxi driver and they will tell you "City Chicken auf der Sonnenallee" can't be beat. Open late and the perfect post-bar food.

name: Neni Berlin
description: Neni has violated one significant tourist trap guideline, namely, it has an incredible view. The food is good, but nothing special, so just worth coming here for the ambiance and 1-2 punch with Monkey Bar across the way.

name: Gotxa
description: Brick-walled bar serving Spanish tapas like croquetas, squid empanadas, and weekend paella from a tight rotating menu. Estrella Galicia pours from the tap while Basque cheesecake chills behind the counter.

name: 893 Ryōtei
description: Serving some of the freshest fish available in Berlin, 893 blends Peruvian and Japanese cuisines to create what is probably Germany's best competitor to Nobu. Unassuming and graffiti clad exterior contrasts with dark and swanky interior.

name: Michelberger Hotel
description: By perfect accident, the Michelberger became the de-facto lodging for musicians operating in East Berlin. Though it's a popular place to end off debaucherous jaunts in the city, the hotel's homely vibe is perfectly suited to families too.

name: Tischendorf
description: There's no shortage of great coffee in Berlin, but Tischendorf is a staple. Both quality and cute, you can taste the love in their freshly baked goods and color-wonder lunch bowls.

name: SongSong Chicken
description: Tiny Bergmannkiez shop frying up double-fried Korean chicken in sticky soy-garlic or chili glazes. Seating is tight, so most orders leave in takeaway boxes.

name: heimlichTreu
description: Berlin is already a green city, but this bar/restaurant/beer garden is an oasis in the hinterhof of an altbau that is so nice it almost hurts. Great food and amazing drinks.

name: Magic John's
description: Berlin did Neopolitan pizzas and Neopolitan pizzas only until recently. Now... Magic John's mixes in some New York and Detroit style 🍕. Both are good but the Detroit style feels like a bit more closer to truth.

name: Cocolo Ramen
description: Traditional Japanese ramen bowls. Arguably the best in Berlin. The intimate space can only take so many guests, so there's always a queue, plus they don't take reservations. Two locations (Mitte and Kreuzberg).

name: Lerchen und Eulen
description: Open so late you can end up here even after striking out at a few clubs, it's hard to not have a great night among the flowers at Lerchen. It's also a great spot to sit outside during the day for a coffee, Aperol, people-watching, etc.

name: A Never Ever Ending Love Story
description: Not necessarily the most comfortable place to go as the indoor seating is cramped, so probably best served coming here and sitting outside in the summer. Lots of French style scrambled eggs, avocado toast, and pancakes.

name: HALO Bagels
description: Small Mitte bakery turning out hand-rolled, slow-fermented sourdough bagels from an open kitchen. The room runs on fast turnover, slinging loaded pastrami and smoked salmon sandwiches for takeout or a quick bite on a stool.

name: Judin GmbH
description: Contemporary art gallery operating out of a former newspaper printing plant on Potsdamer Straße. Sunlit, nine-meter-high halls hold large-scale paintings and sculptures alongside a deep selection of specialized art books.

name: Albatross Bakery
description: Wonderful sourdough, babka, and other baked goods. Excellent coffee and a nice little selection of delicatessen as well. One bench of outdoor seating.

name: Galerie Thomas Schulte
description: Contemporary gallery in Mitte showing international conceptual art under nine-meter ceilings. Large-scale installations take over the corner room, visible straight from the sidewalk through a massive historic display window.

name: Borchardt
description: Berlin institution. Frequented by tourists, politicians, and celebrities, it's often a scene. The menu is ever-changing, but the schnitzel is a safe bet.

name: Admiralbrücke
description: Unique and amazing outdoor Berlin spot 🌉 often featuring live musicians. Go around sunset with a few beers and some friends and just take in the atmosphere.

name: An einem Sonntag im August
description: Trendy cafe that can be a little hipster at times. There's often a live DJ and it's a nice spot for a cocktail. They do serve food and coffees that are pretty good too. Indoor and outdoor seating.

name: Ick bin Berliner
description: Small specialty shop in the Nikolaiviertel selling only food and drink from Berlin producers. Shelves are packed with local gins, craft beers, and jars of Currywurst ready to take home.

name: Topography of Terror
description: Somber indoor-outdoor museum detailing the history of repression under the Nazis. Located on the site of the former Gestapo headquarters and contains one of the longest remaining stretches of the Berlin Wall.

name: Supermarque
description: Menswear concept store in a gallery-like concrete space, anchored by a black Le Corbusier sofa that hosts monthly talks. The selection mixes its own line of premium cotton shirts with curated books, spirits, and leather goods.

name: Deutsches Technikmuseum
description: Go explore artifacts across the full spectrum of technology, from transport to telecommunications, with a focus on rail and industrial technology. Always an enlightening trip through global technological history.

name: Buck and Breck
description: A member of the "Worlds 50 Best Bars" list, Buck and Breck is easy to miss with a blinking ‘Closed’ sign greeting visitors from the street. Sleek, swanky, and only seating 14 guests, the low-lit space favors strong, icy drinks.

name: La Maison
description: Relatively new to the neighborhood but probably won't be going anywhere soon. Great outdoor patio allows for fun people watching along Paul-Linke-Ufer. Amazing French baked goods.

name: Golden Phoenix
description: French-Chinese 🇫🇷🇨🇳 dishes and a sensational 4-course prix fixe menu. Delicious food and a menu that's just a little bit spicy.

name: Cafe le buns
description: Prenzlauer Berg cafe serving sweet and savory buns made from flaky croissant dough. Books and art fill the apartment-style interior, while the sidewalk terrace catches the sun through most of the day.

name: Mae Charoen Thai-Imbiss
description: Tiny Thai spot on Sonnenallee offers hefty portions of Pad Thai, Tom Kha soup, and Massaman curry. Fast-paced, no-frills vibe with limited seating; bring a container for takeout.

name: Doyum
description: Turkish grill house that is consistently solid (and open late!). Go for the Adana kebab or a hearty lentil soup if it's chilly out, and finish it off with Kunefe for dessert.

name: Buchmann Galerie
description: Contemporary art gallery operating two adjacent spaces near Checkpoint Charlie. The setup pairs major solo shows by established international sculptors and painters with smaller, focused exhibitions in the neighboring project box.

name: House of Burgerz
description: Relaxed Mitte burger joint doubling as a gaming lounge full of screens and consoles. The kitchen serves halal American-style patties, vegan options, and curly fries with handmade sauces.

name: Dong Xuan Center
description: Dong Xuan Center is a bargain-hunter's paradise. More than 400 vendors make up this massive site, trading close to anything you can think of. Don't leave without some Vietnamese street food.

name: Nathanja & Heinrich
description: Definitely a date bar, but also just... nice? It's not too smokey in here and the furniture and layout are cozy. Cocktails are solid and they also do beer, wine, and some light snacks.

name: Frühstück 3000
description: A hip spot for breakfast that offers upscale renditions of traditional dishes as well as seasonal specialities, drinks 🍷🍺🍸🍹, and coffee ☕🍵 .

name: CoffeinCentrale
description: Great little eco cafe where the beans are roasted on-site each morning (you can also buy a bag to go!). Nice selection of fresh baked goods as well.

name: Dachkammer
description: Casual, cosy spot to have a few drinks 🍺. Go for the chilled-out atmosphere, which is brought together by the friendly staff, interesting guests, and unique decor.

name: Pergamon Museum
description: Stepping into this museum feels a bit like stepping into a different time period in another part of the world. They have an impressive amount of archaeological findings from the second century BC. If you go, don't miss the Pergamon Altar.

name: Five Elephant
description: A pioneer of Berlin's specialty coffee movement – a great space to sit, socialize, and recharge. Close to Paul-Lincke-Ufer and features arguably the best cheesecake in Berlin. Now with three locations throughout the city.

name: Jüdisches Museum Berlin
description: Striking modern building housing exhibits that trace the history of German-Jewish culture. Home to the Holocaust memorial.

name: Ä Bar
description: About as stereotypically Berlin as a bar can get. Darkly-lit, serving cheap beer and generous wine pours, and with a separate area for non-smokers, Ä is a rare find in Berlin.

name: Kissabo - contemporary tea bar
description: Quiet Prenzlauer Berg tea bar pouring high-grade Japanese teas at a slow, deliberate pace. Freshly whisked matcha and roasted hojicha fill handcrafted bowls, served alongside warm homemade mochi and complex non-alcoholic drinks.

name: Weinerei Forum
description: Cosy little wine spot that stands out for self-service pours 🍷. Popular with locals and tourists alike. Close to Kastanianallee and Zionskirchplatz.

name: Treptower Park
description: One of the most picturesque parks in the city, Treptower offers lush greenery perfect for leisurely strolls alongside the river front. It's also home to the breathtaking Soviet War Memorial, the biggest of its kind outside Russia.

name: Peace Out Paradise
description: Bright Kreuzberg studio dedicated to ceramics, with rows of pottery wheels and long tables for hand-building. One-off classes are popular with beginners; memberships give experienced potters independent access to the space.

name: GlogauAir
description: Artist-in-residence program housed in a landmark former school building in Kreuzberg. The ground-floor project space showcases work from artists living upstairs, with open studios that often spill out into the quiet garden.

name: Kreuzberg
description: If you're in your late 20's / early 30's ideally Kreuzberg is where you want to set yourself up. While previously home to a large mix of leftist punks, anarchists, LGBTQ+, creative artists and Turkish immigrants, it's rapidly gentrified.

name: Rosengarten Kulturpavillon
description: Outdoor pavilion nestled in a park, offering a peaceful retreat for evening drinks and live DJ sets. The spot caters to those seeking a laid-back atmosphere with music.

name: Columbiahalle
description: The perfect size for concert venues: not too big, nor too small, it's just right. Cheap drinks and great shows – good acoustics too for the music nerds. Definitely one of the best places to see a show in Berlin.

name: D.Eli Berlin
description: Vegetarian café in Mitte serving Mediterranean-style salads, roasted vegetables, and house-baked pastries. Sunlit tables and a compact grocery shelf fill the corner space just off Torstraße.

name: 3 Schwestern
description: Unique restaurant hidden inside Künstlerhaus Bethanien, a former 1846 hospital. The refined, airy dining room offering seasonal South German-Austrian cuisine.

name: Molecule Man
description: Massive 30-meter-tall human sculpture in the river Spree at the intersection of the Fredrichshain, Kreuzberg, and Treptow. Covered in holes, they're thought to represent human molecules coming together to create existence.

name: Potsdam
description: A city full of palaces 🏰. Super historic area with beautiful architecture around every bend. Many Italian and English garden styles surrounded by water.

name: Modular
description: Art supply store at Moritzplatz that lives up to the exceptionally high German standard for stationary goods. Come for anything from niche architecture model parts to unusual paints and hard-to-find lead pencils.

name: Home Bar
description: Solid little Friedrichshain living room bar that also might lay claim to serving the best pint of Guinness in Berlin. Plenty of British memorabilia, snacks, and drinks around. Very friendly bartenders.

name: Gorki Apartments
description: Perched above the Weinbergsweg close to Rosenthaler Platz, Gorki is an excellent jumping off point to explore the city. Tastefully designed to feel warm and welcoming, there are 30 apartments of differing sizes and styles.

name: Pfaueninsel
description: Idyllic island that feels like something out of a story book. Big castle-looking buildings and tons of peacocks wandering around. Good for a picnic or a walk on a sunny day. Take the ferry over for four euros.

name: Mädchenitaliener
description: Great Mitte spot for lunch with a focus on freshly made pasta. Can't really go wrong with the burrata either. Recently added a nice outdoor backyard for the summers!

name: Berliner Philharmonie
description: It really doesn't matter where your seat is, the view and music is jaw dropping at every angle. Built in the 1960s, the inside is surprisingly modern and beautiful. Book any ticket and you're sure to have a nice time.

name: Papaya Kantstraße
description: Relaxed Thai restaurant offering a traditional menu that's perfect for a quick lunch bite. Easily amendable to accommodating vegetarian only requests. Watch out, when they say "medium spicy", they mean it.

name: Beach61
description: This is a great place to meet people. Well-kept beach volleyball 🏐 courts that you can rent out or just hang around. Get some drinks and food and sit at the picnic tables. Bring sunglasses and a hat 😎🧢.

name: Misfit Bar
description: Punk bar inspired by the band of the same name. A staple of the local rock scene, come for fresh beer on tap, cheap cocktails, and some light bites. Can get crowded on the weekends but there's also a cozy beer garden out front.

name: Bouleplatz am Landwehrkanal
description: "Boules", or "bocce", or "bowls" is a game that's been embraced across most Berliner neighborhoods. This specific one along the Landwehrkanal is especially beautiful - offering a great view of the river and surrounded by trees.

name: Checkpoint Charlie
description: Cold War border crossing marked by a replica guardhouse and the “You are leaving the American sector” sign. Informational panels and a preserved Berlin Wall segment line the busy stretch of Friedrichstraße.

name: Circus Hostel
description: Bang for your buck doesn't get much better this. Sure, it's a hostel, but the superb service and slick interiors will have you fooled. It's also perfectly situated, surrounded by eateries, bars, cafes, and public transport.

name: Gendarmenmarkt
description: Public square built in 1688 distinguished by its surrounding buildings, including the Deutscher Dom and Französischer Dom which both feature eye-catching architectural features. Often hosts events such as a Christmas market and concerts.

name: Möbel-Olfe
description: Gay bar in Kreuzberg popular with a diverse crowd and welcoming to all. Known for turning the volume up and offering a place to dance, this place often gets so busy that customers sprawl into the Kotti alleyways to drink.

name: 25hours Hotel Bikini Berlin
description: While it's primarily a hotel, 25Hours is also a hotspot for locals who come for drinks and live music at the rooftop Monkey Bar, or for Moroccan food at Neni. The rooms themselves are bright and have views of either the city or Berlin zoo.

name: Volkspark Friedrichshain
description: Massive public park mixing dense woods, wide lawns, and steep hills built over wartime rubble. Winding paths connect active skateparks and sports courts to open fields packed with weekend barbecues and sprawling picnics.

name: KaDeWe - Kaufhaus des Westens
description: Eight-story luxury department store on Tauentzienstraße. Designer fashion fills the lower levels, leading up to a sprawling sixth-floor food hall packed with dining counters, wine bars, and specialty groceries.

name: KaDeWe - Die Sechste
description: Sprawling sixth-floor food hall packed with high-end deli counters, specialized kitchens, and wine bars. The loud, energetic floor runs steady with orders for fresh oysters, posh currywurst, and glasses of champagne.

name: Domberger Brot-Werk - Tegel
description: Craft bakery running out of a converted shipping container in a quiet corner of Tegel. Heavy sourdough loaves, fresh pretzels, and cinnamon buns are baked right in the open space, filling the street with the smell of warm bread.

name: Dudu31
description: Dudu is one of the higher end Asian fusion places 🍱🍜🥢. A little sleek, a little sterile. Does everything well, but nothing *great*. Good for lunch.

name: ACID P-Berg
description: Minimalist corner cafe serving specialty coffee and fresh cardamom buns across a solid granite counter. Raw concrete walls kill cell reception, so the busy room runs strictly on sharp espresso and a heavy sound system.

name: Dresden
description: Nearly completely leveled by bombs during World War II, Dresden was rebuilt from the ground up, imitating Baroque architecture from the past. Some who miss the "old" Berlin now see Dresden as cooler, younger, hipper.

name: Mein Haus am See
description: The tourist trap of all tourist traps but it is central, open 24/7, and has free WiFi so you might, maybe, potentially, could, possibly, inevitably find yourself here. Upstairs theater style seating with a downstairs dance floor.

name: Cafe Sets
description: Trendy cafe with friendly service that will have you feeling right at home. Can't go wrong with one of their sandwiches 🥪 and a fresh juice. Get there early before the people flood in.

name: Goldies
description: One of many fries-focused options in Berlin, Goldies also does fried chicken sandwiches and at their second location, smashburgers. It's all fine in a pinch but some might like other similar spots better. Still good.

name: Crackbuns
description: The Japanese-inspired fuwa-fuwa buns are little balls of soft, fluffy goodness, and the Mochi fries are unlike any other with their doughy texture.

name: Biergarten Am Kleinen Tiergarten
description: Outdoor beer garden located in Berlin's Moabit district, offering a selection of beers and casual dining options. Features a relaxed atmosphere with ample seating under trees, ideal for enjoying drinks and light meals.

name: Bärbucha Kombucha
description: Schöneberg taproom and fermentery pouring tasting flights of raw, house-made kombucha. Jars of SCOBYs and salted lemons sit behind the counter, sharing shelf space with takeaway bottles, beet kvass, and homebrew starter kits.

name: Cafe Fleuery
description: Lovely little French cafe with gluten-free and vegetarian options so everyone can enjoy a delicious cup of coffee ☕ and a Pain au Chocolat 🥐. Try to grab a table outside for people watching along the Weinbergsweg.

name: Barbara Thumm Gallery
description: Contemporary Kreuzberg gallery tucked up a slightly hidden ramp. Exhibitions highlight conceptual, multimedia, and political work from a largely female roster.

name: Berlinische Galerie
description: Compact modern art museum. All of the artists are associated with Berlin in some way, giving it a historian feel as well. Mainly paintings, but there are a few sculptures too.

name: Soho House Berlin
description: About what you would expect from a Soho House with the added benefit of one of the best views of Berlin from the rooftop pool. Three separate bars, along with Cecconi's downstairs. Nice spa and workout area.

name: Boese Buben Bar
description: Coffee shop meets book store meets bar. Go for a breakfast and get a coffee and a cake. Feel free to stick around all day and see how it transforms into one of Mitte's more tucked away watering holes.

name: Bryk Bar
description: The cocktails here are the epitome of "trust the process". You may find yourself making a face at a chocolate and horseradish drink... but don't knock it 'til you try it 🍹. Take a seat inside or outside and enjoy.

name: Bonanza Coffee Roasters
description: Kreuzberg coffee shop with a modern aesthetic serving great pastries. No wi-fi, bring a book 📚.

name: rocket + basil
description: Homey little cafe from a celebrated sister duo serving an excellent brunch with a Persian twist. The mascarpone pancakes or poached eggs are sure bets - but you can't miss with anything. Also great for their lunchtime sandwiches.

name: Café am Neuen See
description: A Bavarian style beer garden serving good food & beer in a rustic-chic space with a lake-view. Definitely one of the more posh Berlin beer gardens, but well worth a trip at least once.

name: The Castle Berlin Mitte
description: Pub that hosts events like trivia and game nights. Huge selection of craft beers which is nice to mix in with the usual beer garden pilsners. There's an outdoor section and music as well when the weather's nice.

name: Bully’s Bakery
description: Trendy cafe serving high-quality coffees, classic baked goods, and light sandwiches. Bully's cheesecakes, in particular, have built a reputation for themselves. An aesthetic setting with good food and drinks.

name: Botanical Affairs
description: If you're a gin drinker with an affinity for a niche brand, look here first ☝️. Cozy bar with a seemingly infinite range of liquors. Tastings can last upwards of three hours, or you can just grab a quick drink with a friend.

name: Monbijoupark
description: Not a huge park, but somehow tons of unique spots are hidden around every corner. Between being across from Museum Island, having both an outdoor gym and basketball court, and being barbecue friendly makes this one of the Berlin favorites.

name: Orient Falafel
description: Compact neighborhood counter serving daily-made falafel and marinated chicken shawarma. Fast, straightforward service loads heavy platters and tight wraps with fresh tabbouleh, hummus, and a standout peanut sauce.

name: Secret Garden | Vegan Sushi
description: Dimly lit vegan sushi spot tucked upstairs from a Friedrichshain supermarket. The plant-draped room serves large shared boards of elaborate tempura rolls, hot dumplings, and cocktails across glass-topped moss tables.

name: Ming Dynastie West Berlin
description: Sprawling West Berlin dining room serving traditional Sichuan cooking and family-style banquets. Shared dinners happen around big circular tables, with spinning lazy Susans loaded with carved Peking duck and fiery chili broth.

name: Oslo Kaffeebar
description: Coffee bar with an edge, serving home-roasted coffee alongside good music and local art. Clad in natural wood, this hipster hangout plays a mix of relaxing tunes while also offering home-baked cookies and cakes.

name: Volksbühne am Rosa-Luxemburg-Platz
description: Pillar-fronted Mitte theater staging experimental plays, contemporary dance, and live music. Radical productions fill the 800-seat main auditorium, while the relaxed Roter Salon pours drinks before and after shows.

name: ROOTS Pizzeria Kreuzberg
description: Sleek Kreuzberg pizzeria firing Neapolitan sourdough from an open kitchen on Kottbusser Damm. The loud, modern dining room runs on electronic music and cocktails, with tables sharing burrata starter pizzas and blistered pies.

name: Hamburger Bahnhof
description: Contemporary art museum set within a preserved 19th-century railway station. Its vast, industrial train shed now serves as the main hall, a dramatic space for monumental installations and ambitious temporary shows.

name: Paska.L Choux P-Berg
description: Stylish Prenzlauer Berg patisserie serving crisp, cream-filled choux and specialty coffee. Decorative boxes of pistachio and salted caramel pastries stack up for takeaway, while the outdoor terrace fills up on warm afternoons.

name: Flakturm Humboldthain
description: Wonderful opportunity for enthusiasts of World War II to see a well-preserved German defensive installation. Although it's a bit of a hike up, the stairs and paths are in good condition, and the view (by Berlin standards), is impressive.

name: Hackesche Höfe
description: Eight interconnected courtyards with hidden nooks, alleys, and shops welcome visitors with a peaceful embrace amongst the hustle of Mitte. Though some visit for the facades alone, locals also come here for a movie, dinner, or show.

name: Fleischerei Domke
description: Family-run East German butcher shop pulling double duty as a fast, counter-service lunch spot. Glass cases hold fresh cuts and thick sausages, while the kitchen dishes out massive plates of schnitzel and pork knuckle.

name: Freya Fuchs
description: Wedding bar featuring exposed concrete, brick walls, and vintage furniture. Dark, smokey, and candlelit, it's great for both cocktails and beers (from the tap). Keep an eye out for the foosball table as well. Open late.

name: Hotel Adlon
description: At the top tier of posh regarding Berlin lodging, the Adlon is about as centrally located from a tourist standpoint as you can get. Try and get a room that faces the Brandenburg Gate. Has an amazing breakfast buffet as well.

name: Promenaden Eck
description: Owned by the same people who run Birgit and Minimal Bar, Promenaden Eck has a similar relaxed vibe that also somehow carries through until the early morning, basically... every morning. Good sound system with a fun dance floor.

name: Berlin Wall Memorial
description: While the East Side Gallery shows the postwar beauty of what the wall can be, the Berlin Wall Memorial is a nice monument frozen in time. Worth seeing both.

name: Booze Bar Berlin
description: Hopefully you're not the type to check the menu in advance, because there isn't one. The bartender will ask you what you're in the mood for, then create a special cocktail just for you 🍹. Excellent service and experience.

name: Berlin International Film Festival
description: Held every February, the "Berlinale" is the world's largest publicly attended annual film festival with events spread out among Berlin's varied film venues. Los Angeles gives out Oscars, we give out the Golden Bear.

name: Kaia Bar
description: One of your many "kiez" bars in and around Simon-Dach-Strasse, but endearing nonetheless. Known for its Guinness just as much as its cocktails, with a live DJ on weekends to boot.

name: Tata Christiane
description: Independent fashion label transforming forgotten textiles into theatrical, wearable art. All pieces are handmade in a Berlin atelier, mixing bold patchwork with deconstructed silhouettes.

name: KVOST
description: Art association in a heritage-listed GDR building showcasing contemporary artists with ties to Eastern Europe. Its exhibitions of photography and sculpture directly engage with the surrounding architecture and the region's complex histories

name: Co Co Banh Mi Deli
description: Great for a quick lunch banh mi sandwich at fair prices. Fresh ingredients that you can eat there or as take-out. If it's too busy, head to Banh Mi Stable nearby.

name: Optimistic Runners
description: Cozy Torstrasse shop selling its own line of minimalist, technical running apparel. Glossy ripstop jackets and perforated tees hang next to independent print magazines, and the storefront doubles as a base for Saturday group runs.

name: Herrlich Berlin
description: All-day Neukölln cafe turning out massive Turkish breakfast platters and hot pans of menemen. Generous spreads of fresh salads, cheeses, and hot tea take over the tables during busy, group-heavy mornings.

name: Golda delux
description: Tiny Kreuzberg corner counter slinging elevated Israeli street food and elaborate desserts. With just four indoor seats, most steam-baked Sabich pitas and brioche French toast go straight to the nearby park for lunch.

name: Zwiebelfisch
description: Classic West Berlin neighborhood pub pouring draft beer and serving hot onion soup well past midnight. Dense layers of old posters, postcards, and international banknotes plaster the walls of the unpretentious space.

name: Lamour Creperie
description: Warm Prenzlauer Berg café run by French siblings serving traditional buckwheat galettes and sweet crêpes. French music plays overhead while the neighborhood drops in for specialty coffee and casual lunches.

name: DR BURGER NEUKÖLLN
description: Tiny Neukölln burger joint slinging halal smash burgers and loaded fries. A solo operator works the grill and counter, passing over messy double-patty orders with wet wipes to make up for the lack of a sink.

name: Villa Elisabeth
description: Grand 1907 parish hall hosting a steady lineup of classical chamber music and contemporary sound art. Evening performances fill a two-story gallery space lined with stucco columns and original herringbone parquet.

name: ick koof mir Dave Lombardo wenn ick reich bin
description: While at one point this might have been a metal bar (Google: Dave Lombardo), it's definitely a bit quieter nowadays. Great to stop by for a pint of Rollberg or to try one of their 50+ gins.

name: Mitte
description: The central district of Berlin and the bougiest. Long gentrified, the clubs picked up and left in the early 2000s and now most bars are either a scene, cocktails, or hidden. It's great for shopping, sights, museums, and restaurants.

name: Formidable
description: It's hard to find good "American style" sandwiches in Berlin. Formidable is about as close as you can get. Friendly spot with a large menu.

name: Meine Bar ICI
description: Jazzy bar that has a great selection of beer and wine to drink next to a cozy fireplace. Walking in feels like you're being transported into a Berlin bar 50 years ago. Smoking friendly – goes with the board games ♣️.

name: Berliner Dom
description: Stunning cathedral for architecture lovers. Walk around the outside first to take it in, then go inside to check out the dome, organ, and intricate artwork. Take the 270 steps to the top for an aerial view of Berlin.

name: Babylon Kreuzberg
description: One of two Berlin Babylon cinemas, most people usually end up at the one in Mitte (also nice, but a different experience). Often chosen as a film festival site, Babylon works hard to put together director showings and other fun surprises.

name: East Side Gallery
description: Ok so this is Berlin's Eiffel Tower or Empire State Building, and the tourists flock accordingly. Worth coming by to see, but don't necessarily go out of your way because you will pass it naturally during the course of a regular day.

name: Hackbarth’s
description: Classic Mitte Kneipe running steady from morning coffee until the early hours. Daytime readers sit along the worn wooden bar with cake before the room fills with a late-night gallery crowd drinking cold tap beer.

name: Nea Pizza 1889
description: Small, unassuming pizzeria serving soft, hand-stretched Neapolitan pies. Tables sit close together in the dining room, with a few extra seats out on the sidewalk during summer.

name: Ökomarkt am Kollwitzplatz
description: Exactly what you would expect from a Prenzlauer Berg farmers' market. Everything is organic, perfectly manicured, very high quality and... priced to match. Great to come to to check out, as it's nestled into a nice area (Kollwitzkiez).

name: OPEN HOUSE
description: Minimalist neighborhood café with a Copenhagen feel, serving simple brunch plates and specialty coffee. Sourdough from Gorilla bakery is topped with cheese from Alte Milch; pastries are from Albatross.

name: Backhaus Projects
description: Flexible hire space in Neukölln that serves as a blank canvas for Berlin’s creative scene. The bright, single room transforms constantly – one week a gallery for a photo show, the next a market for local ceramicists.

name: RARE BERLIN STORE & COLLECTIVE
description: Designer-run collective focused on upcycled fashion, with most pieces crafted from discarded denim and duvet covers. The four creators share shifts on the shop floor, making the space feel more like an open studio than a traditional retail

name: DARK MATTER
description: Seven darkened rooms in a former factory house a permanent collection of immersive light and sound art. Each space is a unique, choreographed world – from pulsing light grids to interactive soundscapes that respond to movement.

name: Weinladen
description: Neighborhood shop for organic and biodynamic European wines: bottles line simple wooden shelves from floor to ceiling. A changing selection is poured by the glass for drinking at small tables out front.

name: Friedrichstadt-Palast
description: Super cool theater to see a show while you're in town. The venue is big and beautiful with some amazing set design. There's also a comedy club in the basement with shows in English on Wednesday nights if you're in the mood for a laugh.

name: panke.gallery
description: Digital art gallery and event space tucked into a graffiti-covered courtyard. Exhibitions focus on net-based art; the program regularly shifts to live music and DJ sets.

name: Delphi Lux
description: A cinema experience. Each of the intimate screening rooms are uniquely designed and you're guaranteed a carefully curated movie selection. With friendly staff and movie snacks sorted, it's the perfect night in/out.

name: Wintergarten Variete
description: Wonderful venue that functions as both a revue theatre and a restaurant (dinner and a show!), the Wintergarten combines glamour and the roaring twenties in a uniquely Berlin way.

name: Mr. Susan
description: Late-night basement bar with a modern speakeasy vibe. A great spot for well-crafted and creative cocktails, Mr. Susan is known for its skilled mixologists and quick service. One more drink is always on the cards.

name: Angry Chicken
description: Small and unassuming Korean fried chicken shop. Good wings, decent fried chicken sandwiches. Varying levels of spice.

name: Monkey Bar
description: A Bohemian style rooftop bar, facing the Gedächtniskirche on one side and the monkey enclosure of the zoo on the other. Upscale for Berlin, be sure to try one of their excellent cocktails.

name: Seebad Friedrichshagen
description: This beach is perfect for a day trip outside of Berlin. Open for e-foiling, lake surfing, platform jumping, and barbecues in the summer ☀️🌊. Also open in the winter for ice skating.

name: Space Shack
description: Sprawling coworking hub with bright, modern architecture and distinct zones for quiet focus or collaboration. Private offices and hot desks share a community kitchen, phone booths, and a large outdoor terrace for work or breaks.

name: SİNEMA TRANSTOPIA
description: Independent cinema and social space in a Wedding industrial courtyard. Curated transnational films play in an intimate 78-seat theater, while the adjoining bar serves drinks and meze for post-show conversations.

name: ONO Spa
description: Luxury spa at the Mandala Hotel offering patrons professional relaxation. With views over the city, ONO delivers shiatsu massages, full facial treatments, and even pregnancy care packages. An upscale wellness experience.

name: Badfish Bar
description: Your classic local Berlin neighborhood bar with a shockingly good pint of Guinness and a solid selection of whiskeys. They also do craft beer and quality cocktails. They serve alcohol, it's nice. Don't think too hard about it.

name: Tori-Katsu Berlin
description: Tight, loud Schöneberg snack bar frying panko-crusted chicken cutlets since 1968. The busy room moves fast, turning out straightforward plates of crispy katsu, rice, and shredded cabbage smothered in rich Japanese curry.

name: machiko sake.shochu.bites
description: Snug Japanese bar in Prenzlauer Berg pouring sake and shochu under a strict drink-first rule. Rotating seafood small plates act as backup to the drinks, landing on compact tables in a tight room built for casual sipping.

name: GASTRONOMIE & DESIGN ATELIER KUMAMI
description: Minimalist Köpenick dining room centered on a single wood counter with under ten seats. A husband-and-wife duo prepares a quiet Washoku tasting menu, sliding a detailed map of seasonal ingredients alongside each dish.

name: Kōji Handroll Bar
description: Minimalist handroll counter in the Kalle Halle food court. Chefs pass warm rice and fresh fish wrapped in nori straight across the bar, serving temaki one by one before the seaweed loses its snap.

name: s h i z u k u .
description: Signless 14-seat Japanese hideout pouring rare sake and shochu just off Hasenheide Park. A long wooden bar takes up most of the quiet room, serving a seasonal omakase menu alongside small sharing plates.

name: OKA Onigiri
description: Streamlined Japanese lunch counter in Mitte shaping fresh onigiri to order in an open kitchen. The pale timber room runs on a simple QR-code system, built for quick lunches at the curved chef's table or easy takeaways.

name: Niko Izakaya
description: Lively Wedding izakaya centered on a busy counter and open kitchen. Daily-changing small plates cross the bar alongside whisky highballs and sake poured into handmade cups picked straight off the shelf.

name: Ishin Mittelstraße
description: No-frills Japanese canteen running a fast, loud lunch service across long communal tables. Free green tea lands next to quick plates of fresh sushi and rice bowls while chefs work the open counter.

name: RAMEN BONES 3
description: Tiny Friedrichshain ramen shop serving massive bowls of heavy, Jiro-style ramen. Intensely rich pork broth comes loaded with thick chewy noodles, pork fat, and towering mounds of garlic and bean sprouts.

name: Japan Plaza Bistro
description: Compact, tucked-away Japanese supermarket in Mitte with narrow aisles of imported groceries and fresh wasabi. An attached casual bistro serves hot bowls of katsu curry and ramen alongside ready-to-eat bento boxes.

name: SO/ Berlin Das Stue
description: What was once the Royal Danish Embassy now stands as an imposing hotel in the diplomatic district of Tiergarten. Enjoy the opulence you'd expect from a luxury hotel (spa, pool, libraries), plus private entrance into the zoo next door.

name: Hotel Orania
description: Right in the middle of Kreuzberg, Hotel Orania is universally reviled by locals due to its elitist status, nestled in among a more down-to-earth part of Berlin. It is a nice hotel though with a good restaurant and solid bar.

name: Toca Rouge
description: Chinese favorites with a fusion spin on them, so your senses are in for a treat. Keep your phone charged for the Insta-worthy dishes and interiors (check the unique bathroom lighting) ✨.

name: Ratzeputz
description: Delicious cocktails mixed with top notch spirits, tasty craft beers (as well as the staples), and a wine list featuring independent vineyards from all over Europe. Cozy at night, and work-friendly during the day. Trivia on Sundays.

name: Astor Film Lounge
description: Think movie theater, but make it fancy. Art Deco-style venue that shows classic films and new releases. Enjoy high-quality beverages and finger foods in front of the big screen. A premium cinema experience.

name: Das Hotel Radio
description: Evolved from live music at Das Hotel bar in Kreuzberg, Das Hotel Radio puts on concerts and live performances showcasing some of Berlin's most creative talents.

name: Azzam
description: No frills kebab joint. If you're not super hungry, grab one dish to share with your friends because the portions are huge. Tea is on the house and the price is super fair for what you get. Some of the best falafel you can get in Berlin.

name: Mugrabi
description: Cozy Israeli cafe by Görlitzer Park perfect for a fresh outdoor brunch. Make sure to try their hummus or hamshuka when you stop by.

name: Zur Glühlampe
description: Rudolfkiez's local corner bar. Relatively relaxed, but a great place to go to catch a soccer game or grab a pitcher of beer (yes, they do pitchers here!). Very friendly owner and bartender, who occasionally arrange music shows as well.

name: Peace Yoga
description: Yoga studio focusing on the practice of Jivamukti - a yogic method that combines physical movement with philosophy and spiritual activism. The facility holds classes in German and English, as well as community-based workshops and retreats.

name: Kino International
description: Kino International first opened its doors in 1963 as a premier venue of the German Democratic Republic. Today, the theater is known for showing both mainstream and indie films in a glamorous midcentury modern space.

name: The Mandala Hotel
description: Sleek, spacious rooms in a great location from which to explore the city. The Mandala is a five-star hotel with an ensemble of premier amenities, including a two-Michelin-star restaurant and a spa. Upscale comfort.

name: R.S.V.P. Papier
description: Paper goods never looked this good. Here you can find a carefully curated selection of gorgeously designed stationary products from around the world. It's a must-visit for one-of-a-kind special gifts 🎁.

name: Kindl - Center for Contemporary Art
description: Established in the 1920s, this former brewery is now home to a large collection of contemporary artwork - and an accompanying café. The building itself is distinctive, and the exhibitions it harbors are of meticulous curation.

name: crazylegz Skate Café & Concept Store
description: Neukölln café and skate shop with smooth floors cleared for indoor roller skating. Skaters roll over a custom ramp connecting a blue room serving homemade cake and coffee to a hot pink back shop stocked with quad skates.

name: Full Node Berlin
description: Blockchain? The blockchain? Blockchains? It's a co-working space for web3 nerds (lovingly!). A little on the pricey side but only because you didn't buy bitcoin when you should have.

name: Berliner Fernsehturm
description: Unless you are going to take the elevator up for the view, the TV tower is what all Berliners use as a navigation tool to stay as far away from Alexanderplatz as possible.

name: Izmir Köfte
description: Finding a good sandwich 🥖 in Berlin can be hard, but this Turkish take served on fresh baguette definitely does the trick. Simple menu but everything is great to grab and go (it's right at Kotti after all).

name: Freiluftkino Kreuzberg
description: Kreuzberg's open air cinema located in the garden of the Künstlerhaus Bethanien. Shows independent movies, documentaries, classics, and the occasional blockbuster. Free to bring your own food and drinks. Comfortable beach chair seating.

name: Freiluftkino Rehberge
description: Huge open-air theater 📽 in a state park surrounded by forests. The Freiluftkino Rehberge screens German-dubbed films. Romantic date spot for film buffs.

name: Villa Neukölln
description: Wonderful Neukölln bar that's cozy in the front and cavernous in the back (with a stage!). Depending on the night artists will jump on to perform or play shows.

name: Zosse
description: Charming little bar and beer garden hidden down an alleyway in the Rixdorf region of Neukölln. Built into a former blacksmith's workshop, Zosse features an extensive menu of drinks in addition to your usual beer-on-tap staples.

name: Markthalle Neun
description: Famous for its "streetfood Thursdays", Markthalle Neun is also a wonderful spot to come pick up fresh produce 🥬 or have a glass of wine 🍷 at during the week. Brunch here on the weekends is also fun with ~50 vendors to poke around at.

name: pars Restaurant + Pralinen
description: Minimalist Charlottenburg dining room centered on a large communal table with clear views into a quiet open kitchen. The seasonal tasting menu draws on Austrian traditions and finishes with a dedicated course of sculptural pralines.

name: Kaffeekirsche
description: Contemporary coffee shop and roastery passionate about specialty brews from around the world. The flagship Böckhstraße location also serves diverse brunch options and baked goods. Ideal for a pitstop or relaxed refuel.

name: Tak Kee
description: Family-run Wilmersdorf dining room serving old-school Hong Kong cuisine. Sizzling clay pots and weekend pork belly hit the tables, while the owner translates daily seafood specials from the Cantonese chalkboards.

name: Kapelle am Urban
description: Repurposed 1890 hospital chapel in Kreuzberg staging a steady rotation of intimate concerts, choir rehearsals, and art shows. Live performances happen upstairs around a historic grand piano on the original tile floors.

name: Café Schroeder
description: Cozy, Scandi-style Mitte cafe pulling specialty espresso and serving thick buttermilk pancakes. Small tables sit close together by large windows, filling up fast on weekends for fresh sourdough and natural wine.

name: Würgeengel
description: Cozy cocktail bar with lovely décor and warm lighting. Can often get quite full on weekends, but has a more relaxed environment during the week. Excellent and friendly bartenders - try a Whiskey Sour or White Negroni.

name: Banh Mi Stable
description: Three options to pick from (pork, tofu, chicken) - all of which are excellent. Not a lot of indoor seating so either take it to go or curb it with a Tiger beer. If the line is too long (can happen), head to Co Co Banh Mi close-by.

name: Allans Breakfast Club
description: A fun brunch spot that will have you feeling like you're on vacation. Super interesting twists on classic breakfast foods like their eggs benedict (would reccomend). Healthy food that won't way you down.

name: ://about blank
description: Unassuming from the outside, but one of the city's best party spots. A nightclub with an industrial design that features two indoor floors and an outdoor garden - expect different music genres in each space.

name: Hallesches Haus
description: Think of this "general store" as more of a concept store. Super earthy vibe and unique items. There's also a beautiful lunchroom with a terrace. Good spot for a meal or just to sit with a coffee and a book 📚.

name: ploetz
description: Original green-and-white tiles line a former butcher shop turned Schöneberg neighborhood cafe. Trays of babka and croissants crowd the counter while the kitchen slings shakshuka and blood sausage sandwiches.

name: Humboldthain Club
description: Built into S-Bahn station Humboldthain, Humboldthain Club is the rare Wedding club and wonderfully unique. Two dance floors playing either harder techno or funk, with plenty of outdoor (stadium) seating surrounding lively ping pong tables.

name: Else
description: Colorful riverfront nightclub that is built mostly out of repurposed shipping containers. Multiple dance floors and a large outdoor patio. Great summer spot.

name: Hoppetosse
description: One of Berlin's more peculiar clubs, Hoppetosse is a permanently moored ship ⛴ that now features an amazing roof deck and small dance floor pumping techno music.

name: Yaam
description: Not your traditional Berlin club with thumping techno music, as Yaam (Young African Artist Market) features more live music, reggae, and other beats. Good spot for a chilled afternoon in the sun ☀️ along the river. Food carts also open.

name: Trabrennbahn Karlshorst
description: Harness racing track anchored by a light-filled 1930s grandstand. Trotters run the circuit on race days, while giant antique markets regularly take over the vast infield.

name: Flowers Marsano GmbH
description: Mitte floral studio mixing wild, loose-form arrangements with vintage furniture and antique glass. Lush displays of rare, locally grown blooms fill a room lined with golden wallpaper.

name: Tier
description: For out-of-the-glass cocktails dreamed up by some of the best bartenders around, paired with an energy that is uniquely theirs. Because of this, it gets quite busy, quite quickly, so best you get there early ⏰.

name: SHA-LA Studios Prenzlauer Berg
description: Light-filled Kastanienallee studio running a daily rotation of yoga, Pilates, and breathwork. The fully equipped space pairs active movement with recovery treatments like sound healing and red light therapy.

name: Aura Berlin - Pilates Studio
description: Cozy movement studio mixing mindful grounding with serious sweat. The schedule spans technical power Pilates and ballet-style barre to high-energy Latin dance.

name: Wentrup GmbH
description: Contemporary gallery occupying a 1920s brick building in Charlottenburg. International exhibitions fill the former post office space, set against original details like the tiled floors.

name: Der Fischladen
description: Hybrid fishmonger and restaurant spanning three storefronts on Schönhauser Allee. The kitchen grills fresh catch straight from the retail display, serving battered fish and chips or classic fish sandwiches.

name: Pinci
description: All-day Italian bar in a converted supermarket, pouring espresso in the morning and natural wines at night. The menu is short and changes daily – expect simple pastas, house-made focaccia, and plates of sliced Mortadella.

name: Dr Maury Wine Bar
description: Intimate wine bar pouring natural and organic bottles from France, Italy, and Spain. Seasonal small plates are made for sharing; the tightly packed room hums with a largely French crowd.

name: Johann Bäckerei
description: Located in Schöneberg, this bakery offers homemade sourdough bread, croissants, pretzels, rolls, and sweet pastries. Patrons can enjoy their treats with coffee by the window or take them home for breakfast.

name: Berlin Victory Column
description: While this monument is nice to look at, it's even better to experience it on the inside. Accessible through underground passages. You can go to the top for stunning views of the Tiergarten - best at sunset.

name: Sisyphos
description: Previously a more under-the-radar club, Sisyphos has jumped into the top tier of Berlin's nightlife options along with Berghain, Kater, and Renate. Several dance floors playing various forms of electronic music await.

name: Café EGGRYTHING
description: Minimalist Korean spot filling thick brioche with fluffy eggs and bulgogi. Sweet croffles and black sesame lattes pair with the savory toast in a quiet, cozy room.

name: Trinkteufel
description: Loosely translated as "drinking devil," Trinkteufel is best loved by those of the hardcore punk and metal persuasion 🤘🏼. The drinks are good, basic, and cheap.

name: YSY
description: Bright, modernist bar on Frankfurter Allee pairing a custom sound system with a deep agave selection. DJs play in the high-ceilinged room while the bar pours mezcal and tequila.

name: Berghain
description: Berlin's techno mecca. Famous venue known as much for its sound system as its long lines.

name: Salon Zur Wilden Renate
description: Spanning multiple floors of an untended "Altbau" in Friedrichshain across the Spree from Treptower Park, Salon Zur Wilden Renate lays claim to Berlin's top local's nightclub.

name: Concierge Coffee
description: A cool little grab-and-go coffee spot tucked near the Landwehr Canal. Here, baristas stand where doormen once stood, serving specialty espresso to a handful of indoor tables and through the hole-in-the-wall service hatch.

name: do you read me?!
description: Small bookstore specializing in art and design titles, with a particular focus on curating independent magazines.

name: KUCHI Mitte
description: Bustling Japanese spot filling communal tables with oversized sushi rolls and fusion bowls. Dining spills into a leafy courtyard garden in summer.

name: Han BBQ
description: Bustling Korean barbecue hall on Kantstraße with tabletop grills for searing marinated beef and pork belly. The strict walk-in policy keeps the room packed and high-energy.

name: Cecconi's Berlin
description: Fresh Italian food in a trendy space on the ground floor of the Soho House. Specialties: Vitello Tonnato, Calamari Fritti, Picante Della Casa, and Cotoletta. A scene to be taken in with an Espresso Martini.

name: KOKIO
description: Lively Prenzlauer Berg spot dedicated to chimaek – the Korean ritual of fried chicken and beer. Halal, double-fried wings arrive sticky with soy garlic or spicy glaze alongside pickled radish and cold drafts.

name: Julius Ernst
description: Sleek counterpart to fine-dining neighbor Ernst using the same pristine produce for casual à la carte dinners. Japanese techniques shape daily small plates served with natural wines in a minimalist, monochrome room.

name: Funky Fisch
description: Colorful seafood restaurant serving high-quality food in a contemporary environment. Dishes take inspiration from different world cuisines, and guests can even choose their catch at the eatery's fish counter.

name: Frieda
description: Cozy all day contemporary hangout spot that features handcrafted bread, market-driven plates, and an extensive wine list.

name: ORA Restaurant & Wine Bar
description: Original medicine cabinets and dark woodwork wrap the bustling dining room of the former Oranien-Apotheke. Dinner service pairs seasonal plates from the restaurant's farm with natural wines.

name: Bergmanns
description: Intimate Kreuzberg dining room with sidewalk tables under mature trees. Inventive, vegetable-forward sharing plates arrive alongside natural wines.

name: Saint Farah
description: Lively Mitte bistro serving modern Levantine sharing plates near Weinbergspark. The open kitchen fires fresh pita in a pizza oven, anchoring a casual room hung with art you can buy off the walls.

name: Tossakan
description: Cozy Thai spot in Berlin serving bold dishes like juicy satay, crispy pork belly, and rich Mama Tom Yam. Authentic flavors shine in spicy papaya salad and green curry ribs, with sweet desserts like mango sticky rice.

name: Orania.Restaurant & Orania.Bar
description: Open-plan Kreuzberg dining room centered on a concert stage and roaring fireplaces. Dinner service revolves around the signature four-course duck menu while live jazz plays from the Steinway.

name: Kimchi Princess
description: Kreuzberg Korean BBQ restaurant, with wooden tables and bench seating, offering dishes to be shared alongside soju.

name: Jolie Bistrot
description: Intimate French bistro lined with dark mahogany and soft light. Seasonal sharing plates and natural wines crowd the compact tables, making for a close-knit dinner near Kollwitzplatz.

name: Tossakan Berlin
description: Cozy Prenzlauer Berg dining room serving Thai home cooking with uncompromising Bangkok heat. Tables book out weeks in advance for holy basil stir-fry and rich Tom Yam soups set to a lo-fi soundtrack.

name: Trattoria del Corso
description: Wholesome Italian restaurant that has become a local favorite. Ideal for alfresco lunches and hearty dinners. Enjoy stone-baked pizzas, generous helpings of handmade pasta, and antipasti dishes. Cash only.

name: Schwiliko
description: Busy, family-run Georgian restaurant with a cozy ambiance. Well-frequented by the local community, this eatery serves traditional dishes such as khachapuri and lobio stew - book the "Supra" set menu for a choreographed experience.

name: Simonetta
description: Bustling Italian trattoria on the Canal de l'Ourcq serving Neapolitan pizza and fresh pasta. Tables sit tightly packed and service runs fast, with blistered pies arriving from the wood-fired oven in minutes.

name: Rôtisserie Segar
description: Takeaway rotisserie on Rue Mouffetard turning out flame-roasted Landes chickens and hot sides. Staff pull whole birds straight from the spit and assemble fresh baguettes stuffed with shredded meat, aged parmesan, and crispy skin chips.

name: 57 Grains
description: Specialty coffee shop on a sloping Montmartre street pouring flat whites and serving Turkish-inspired brunch. Weekend mornings run loud and busy over plates of Turkish eggs, halva brownies, and thick pastrami sandwiches.

name: R. des Martyrs
description: Steep market street climbing from the 9th arrondissement toward Montmartre. Independent cheese shops, bakeries, and cafes pack the slope, drawing a steady crowd for fresh bread and supplies.

name: Salted boy
description: Compact Marais bakery baking fresh batches of buttery, Asian-inspired salt bread every hour. Warm, crispy-bottomed loaves are handed over the stainless counter, ready to be torn and dipped into pandan cream or salted lattes.

name: Yasubé
description: Long-standing Japanese dining room on Rue Sainte-Anne serving yakitori from a smoky charcoal grill. Ground floor counter seats face the open kitchen, while the downstairs tatami room stays quiet for relaxed dinners.

name: Clos d’Astorg
