description: Classic Parisian bistro serving generous, butter-rich French classics on white tablecloths. Hearty stuffed cabbage and sweetbreads are followed by massive portions of chocolate mousse scooped from a large bowl tableside.

name: EchizenSOBA TOGO
description: Compact, no-reservations Japanese canteen near the Tuileries serving hot and cold Echizen soba. Shared wood tables fill the tight room, where meals end by mixing hot sobayu into leftover dipping sauce.

name: Trâmette
description: Tiny, counter-style dining room pouring natural wine alongside shared plates of shiso oysters and lemongrass razor clams. The terracotta-walled space runs as a neighborhood deli by day before shifting into an evening wine bar.

name: Agatto
description: Intimate 11th arrondissement tea room doubling as a Japanese pastry studio. Hands-on workshops break down the steps for rolling and filling mochi daifuku, ending with boxed treats to take home.

name: Rasa Yoga Rive Gauche
description: Secluded yoga studio hidden behind a heavy wooden door in a quiet 5th arrondissement courtyard. Natural light pours through translucent roofs into stone-walled practice rooms during bilingual Vinyasa and Yin classes.

name: Church of Saint-Roch
description: Baroque parish on rue Saint-Honoré holding the tombs of Diderot and Le Nôtre. The deep interior extends well past the altar into a series of theatrical, art-filled chapels.

name: 20th Arrondissement
description: Home to some of the city's most iconic landmarks including the Cemetery of Père Lachaise. Paris' 20th arrondissement is often defined as laidback. World cuisine eateries can be found throughout, as can art galleries and trendy bars.

name: Big Smile Bazaar
description: An enthusiast's record shop that specializes in hard-to-find vinyl gems. Carries a wide range of genres from hip-hop and rock 'n roll, to Brazilian soul and beyond. A cool place to go when in the market for some music.

name: Au Rendez-Vous des Amis
description: Classic Montmartre corner bar running steady from lunch to late night. The dimly lit room has a busy counter and single banquette, while tables spill onto the terrace for shared cheese boards and happy hour cocktails.

name: 18th Arrondissement
description: A high-traffic neighborhood surrounding the Montmartre hilltop. Full of variety, and a haven for bargain hunters. The 18th is home to numerous restaurants, markets, and shops - explore, dine, and even catch a Moulin Rouge showing.

name: Restaurant Anne
description: Intimate library salon off the Place des Vosges with deep velvets, bookshelves, and just eight tables. Modern French tasting menus shift to a secluded, vine-draped courtyard on warm days.

name: Ducasse Baccarat
description: Historic 16th arrondissement townhouse carved into intimate dining salons. Seasonal French tasting menus from Alain Ducasse arrive on heavy Baccarat crystal under massive chandeliers.

name: Medici Fountain
description: Sculpted marble fountain and long water basin tucked into a quiet corner of the Jardin du Luxembourg. Rows of plane trees arch over the water, shading the metal park chairs pulled up to the edge for reading and escaping the sun.

name: Marché Bastille
description: Massive open-air food market running down Boulevard Richard-Lenoir every Thursday and Sunday. Long aisles are packed with seasonal produce and artisanal cheese, alongside stands serving freshly shucked oysters and cold white wine.

name: Quartier Montorgueil
description: Pedestrian market district built around a cobblestone street packed with cheese shops, fishmongers, and historic bakeries. Cafe terraces spill onto the pavement, mixing outdoor dining with the daily rhythm of fresh grocery runs.

name: Sound and Coffee
description: Walnut-lined cafe and listening room tucked down the historic Passage des Panoramas. Baristas pull specialty espresso while warm audio plays from a massive vinyl collection and vintage hi-fi system.

name: Semiose
description: Contemporary gallery set behind a lemon-yellow courtyard entrance in the Marais. Vast, bright rooms display large-scale works alongside a bookstore stocking the gallery's own art editions.

name: Les Pères Populaires
description: Eclectic neighborhood canteen filled with thrifted sofas and mismatched school chairs. It’s a quiet workspace by day before the lights dim for cheap beer, charcuterie, and live jazz.

name: Cave De Vie
description: Casual ground-floor bar and bottle shop set around a large communal table, pouring natural wines and regional French spirits. The room doubles as the entrance to an intimate, farm-to-glass cocktail bar down in the limestone cellar.

name: Buly 1803
description: Offers an array of skin ointments, all-natural perfumes, and dental opiates. The shop is lined with aged apothecary bottles and features marbled countertops – a bit of a step back in time.

name: Casa Pregonda
description: Candlelit Spanish tavern with exposed stone walls, serving Menorcan-inspired shared plates and seafood. The intimate dining room is a popular date spot; the bar pours classic gin Pomadas.

name: Le Canard Sauvage
description: Buzzy, slightly chaotic bistro with jungle-print wallpaper and a low-ceilinged mezzanine. The English chef sends out a daily-changing menu of modern French game dishes and natural wines.

name: A La Renaissance
description: Neighborhood bistro with its original marble bar, spotted mirrors, and wine-red banquettes. The menu is classic French, but the extensive natural wine list and strong house martinis are what fill the room with locals.

name: Prévelle
description: Upstairs dining room with exposed beams and stone, home to chef Romain Meder's personal tasting menus. Modern French dishes arrive in five or seven courses, each built from ingredients sourced directly from French artisans.

name: Les Bouquinistes of Paris
description: Open-air stalls with over 300,000 books on offer, from rare editions by Jules Vernes to old magazines. Stroll along the Seine on a rainy day and take in the sights and sounds of Paris while browsing the city's famous bookstalls.

name: Huitrerie Régis
description: Postage-stamp-sized oyster bar with whitewashed walls and a singular focus on Marennes-Oléron oysters. The menu is strictly shellfish, bread, and wine; the handful of tables are first-come, first-served.

name: Lissit
description: Intimate corner bistro where a solo chef reworks French classics from a tiny open kitchen. The lively room runs on natural wine, with a long list of vermouths to start.

name: L'Arret by The Grey
description: Southern American port city cooking served in a classic Parisian bistro from Savannah chef Mashama Bailey. Dishes like shrimp and grits and chicken country captain land on tables near the vintage marble bar.

name: Brigitte Tanaka
description: Located next to Église Saint-Roch, Brigitte Tanaka is a one-stop shop for French and Japanese fashion accessories, jewelry, and home décor. Filled with stylish items for even the most discerning shopper.

name: Cafe Laurent
description: For years, this beautiful café has been a favorite of writers and jazz artists, and it continues to be a staple for the city's fashionable residents. Sit back, enjoy afternoon tea, or unwind with their famous "Laurent" cocktail.

name: Bar Hemingway
description: This iconic hotspot has long been a favorite of the city's jet set, who come here to enjoy classic drinks and high-end French fare. An ideal place to unwind after a long day of sightseeing or shopping - if budget allows.

name: Café de la Nouvelle Mairie
description: A beloved local spot that has been serving classic French fare for over 15 years. The worn wooden tables and zinc-topped bar create a warm and inviting atmosphere. Visit for coffee during the day, or go for dinner come the evening.

name: Café Méricourt
description: Offers a variety of both sweet and savory options. Their renowned all-day brunch menu features shakshuka and orange-blossom pancakes.

name: Boot Café
description: A proven - yet humble - coffee shop and gathering place in the heart of Paris. Offers a small, but carefully curated, selection of coffee beans from the Oslo-based roastery Fuglen. Trumps the mainstream caffeine vendors.

name: Fogon Ultramarinos
description: Tiny Spanish deli and 15-seat dining room serving serious tapas and rice dishes among shelves of imported groceries. Signature paellas require a full day's notice, landing on tables right under hanging legs of Ibérico ham.

name: Mantchouk
description: Warm, tile-floored Armenian deli and 24-seat dining room serving traditional family recipes. Small tables fill with beef manti, stuffed pirojki, and rich cheese soubeureg paired with Armenian wine.

name: Le Tsuba Hotel
description: Quiet townhouse near the Arc de Triomphe mixing 1920s Parisian style with calm Japanese design. Walnut-paneled rooms sit above a glass-roofed lounge, while the basement hammam and sauna run entirely on private reservations.

name: Christophe Louie
description: Haut-Marais bakery bringing high-end pastry technique to slow-fermented Italian doughs. Huge, airy panettone sits alongside glazed madeleines and sourdough loaves, with slices cut year-round for eating on the pedestrian street terrace.

name: CAFE SHIN
description: Seoul-style cafe pouring black sesame and sweet potato lattes in a room lined with blue ombre tiles. Kimbap rolls and matcha cookies fuel afternoons in the bathhouse-inspired seating nooks.

name: CRAVAN Paris 6e
description: Four-story cocktail house occupying a 17th-century building in Saint-Germain. Three bars and a Rizzoli bookshop spread across the levels, topped by a rooftop kiosk for drinks and open-air cinema.

name: Pâtisserie GINKO
description: Tiny 19th arrondissement shop blending French technique with Japanese and Moroccan accents. The counter serves kinako-spiked choux and sesame cookies ready for a walk in the nearby Buttes-Chaumont.

name: Fenua Ceramics
description: Working studio and retail space selling minimalist, slow-made ceramic tableware. Artist Sophie Leimbacher shapes simple plates and bowls on-site, sharing the floor with hands-on pottery classes.

name: Caviar Kaspia
description: A world-renowned caviar house that has been serving luxurious blini, caviar, and smoked seafood dishes since 1927. Their selection of caviar includes some of the rarest and most sought-after varieties from around the world.

name: Bachir
description: Busy Lebanese parlor serving organic ice cream with the chewy texture of mastic. The signature Ashta scoops are rolled in a thick layer of crushed pistachios.

name: Lolo cave à manger
description: Compact, red-lit cave à manger pouring natural wine and serving seasonal small plates. One long communal table and a vermillion bar fill the loud, tight room, leaving barely enough space to lean over oysters and beef tartare.

name: La Butte Aux Piafs
description: Offers tempero French fusion cuisine, as well as affordable lunch menu items. Expect burgers alongside numerous vegetarian choices. Stunning views of the Auguste Blanqui market can also be enjoyed from the bistro whilst dining.

name: 19th Arrondissement
description: Home to the city's biggest cultural and artistic center - La Villette. Visit one of the many museums or exhibition spaces, catch a show at one of they many venues, or enjoy some leisure time in Parc des Buttes-Chaumont.

name: Dirty Lemon
description: Queer-friendly 11th arrondissement cocktail bar pouring clever drinks and serving late-night Palestinian small plates. Pale walls and a stone counter glow under soft lighting, keeping the room cozy for long dates and shared flatbreads.

name: Le Bistrot Flaubert
description: Polished neighborhood bistro turning out precise French cooking from a former spice shop. Well-spaced marble tables fill with thick slices of pâté en croûte, serious wine, and a caramel hazelnut mille-feuille.

name: Calcifer
description: Warm Haut Marais dining room with large booths and a central open hearth. The Basque-leaning kitchen cooks entirely over live fire, serving shared plates of aged steak, whole turbot, and langoustines.

name: MEHMET
description: Tight, buzzy 18th arrondissement dining room serving plated Turkish döner, meze, and natural wine. Elbow-to-elbow tables fill up late into the night for free-range chicken from the spit and house-baked bread.

name: 11th Arrondissement
description: A confluence of different cultures - Paris' 11th arrondissement is renowned for its energy and atmosphere. From the amazing food to the vibrant nightlife, there's always something to do in the 11th.

name: Bois de Boulogne
description: This scenic park offers lovely views of the native Lac Inférieur - visitors can rent a traditional wooden canoe to explore the lake. There are also bikes available for hire, allowing travelers to cycle around the full 2088-acre plot.

name: Bois de Vincennes
description: A beautiful park ideal for boating, picnics, and spending time with family and friends. With its stunning neoclassical pavilion and 14th century chateau, Bois de Vincennes is arguably a sightseeing spot in its own right.

name: Aux Deux Amis
description: A wine bar and bistro that is known for its home-cooked meals and natural wines. Try their signature Tortilla de Janine, or the Cheval Tartare - ask the knowledgeable service team about the best wine pairing for each dish.

name: Bar 228
description: Iconic bar, housed within the Hôtel Meurice. It has been redesigned, but still retains its old-world charm. Alongside the wide selection of cocktails, their "croque-meurice" (a take on the croque monsieur) is also said to be a must-try.

name: Le Narcisse Blanc
description: Quiet boutique hotel filling a six-story Haussmann building on a leafy 7th arrondissement street. The 37 rooms double as plush, velvet-accented apartments, paired with an underground swimming pool and contemporary French dining.

name: Arts Et Métiers Métro
description: An eye-catching metro station designed by François Schuite - a Belgian comic artist. The aesthetic seeks to blend reality with fantasy. Copper sheets are punctuated by portholes to emphasise the station's subterranean locale.

name: Buttes Snack Bar
description: Rugged, concrete-lined cave à manger pouring natural wines near the Buttes-Chaumont. An open kitchen anchors the energetic room, plating seasonal snacks and sharing dishes on retro Limoges china.

name: Eiffel Tower
description: France's most famous landmark. A tourist trap - without question. But worth ticking off the list nonetheless. Take elevators to the observation deck, or simply view from afar.

name: Batignolles
description: This trendy neighborhood is just 15 minutes on foot from Montmartre, and is full of interesting streets and sights. From the cafes to bars, this is a place where creative minds come to relax and escape the bustle of everyday life.

name: Marché Alimentaire Saint-Germain
description: Refined, stone-arcaded covered market in the 6th arrondissement. Clean, organized stalls stock fresh produce, cheese, and oysters for quick lunches and picnic runs to the nearby Jardin du Luxembourg.

name: Partisan Café Artisanal
description: Specialty coffee roastery pouring two distinct styles: traditional Italian blends and lighter, single-origin roasts. The minimalist, industrial space is strictly laptop-free, with outdoor tables spilling onto the corner.

name: La Sirena
description: Family-run Italian spot on Boulevard Saint-Germain serving wood-fired pizzas and house-made pastas. The tight, cozy dining room has street-facing window seats, a working pizza oven, and a resident cat roaming the floor.

name: Cafe Singulier
description: Spacious, modern café with an open kitchen serving a refined, daily-changing menu of seasonal dishes. Specialty coffee is poured all day, but the homemade cookies are the true local obsession.

name: Rosario
description: Light-filled Spanish restaurant pouring jamón-infused cocktails and passing modern tapas across a central counter. The two-story room fills up late for shared plates of caramelized pork cheeks and Basque cheesecake.

name: Le Progrès Marais
description: Classic North Marais bar-tabac and brasserie on a busy Rue de Bretagne corner. The sprawling terrace runs steady from morning espresso through late-night wine, keeping round marble tables full for neighborhood people-watching.

name: Back In Black
description: Vast industrial space combining an on-site roastery with an all-day brunch counter. Seasonal filter coffees are prepared with precision; everything from the bread to the jam is made in-house.

name: Immersion
description: Bright, modern cafes serving an all-day brunch menu of brioche benedict and chicken & waffles. The exposed-brick rooms are reliably packed on weekends – the crowd thins for a late afternoon meal.

name: Résidence Kann
description: Functioning furniture showroom where the 1950s-inspired interior is completely redesigned every six months. It doubles as a specialty coffee shop, pouring Coutume beans and serving pastries near Canal Saint-Martin.

name: Clove Coffee Shop
description: Specialty coffee poured into handmade ceramics in a minimalist Montmartre space. It’s a quiet, focused retreat from the neighborhood crowds, with the co-owner's pottery for sale and displayed on exposed brick walls.

name: Fringe
description: Specialty coffee shop and photo gallery pouring single-origin espresso and serving house-made cardamom rolls. Photography is the focus: rotating exhibits are printed directly onto the wallpaper, and a library of art books lines the shelves.

name: Tarántula Paris
description: Moody, low-lit 11th arrondissement dining room serving Northern Mexican small plates with French touches. Small tables quickly fill with shared beef tacos, tuna crudo, and hibiscus margaritas.

name: Noir
description: House-roaster pouring single-origin Arabica in minimalist, architect-designed shops. A strict no-laptops policy keeps the cozy spaces focused on conversation, not work.

name: Gramme
description: Creative cantine where fermented potato flatbread and Vietnamese-style stuffed cabbage anchor a weekly menu of small plates. The all-day spot moves from morning coffee to an evening service of shared plates and natural wines.

name: Passager
description: Spacious corner cafe with exposed brick walls, serving an all-day, American-style brunch. The room is bright and always busy – expect a line for a table on weekends.

name: Red Sauce
description: Retro New York-style dining room keeping a loud, fast pace in the 10th arrondissement. Red leather banquettes stay packed as Detroit-style pizza, chicken parm, and spicy house-made pasta hit the tables alongside natural wine.

name: Le Peloton
description: Specialty coffee shop and cycling hub pouring espresso from local roasters and serving house-made waffles. High-end rental bikes hang from the ceiling; organized group rides depart from the front door.

name: Arabica
description: Minimalist Japanese coffee shop pouring rich espresso from globally sourced beans. The Spanish Latte is a house specialty; locals take theirs to the benches outside to watch the street.

name: Coutume
description: Third-wave coffee pioneer with the precision of a science lab, where water arrives in chemist's flasks. Single-origin beans are brewed via siphon and drip; the Anglo-French brunch is a neighborhood fixture.

name: City of Fashion and Design
description: Cultural center in an old industrial space headlined by the French Institute of Fashion. Alongside style and art exhibitions, the complex hosts the Art Ludique museum and a rooftop bar that overlooks the Seine.

name: Caillebotte
description: Bright corner bistro in the 9th arrondissement serving precise, modern French cooking. Pale wood tables and a white marble bar fill a relaxed room built around a busy open kitchen turning out seasonal tasting menus.

name: La Main Noire
description: Australian-inspired cafe on Rue Cavalotti turning out seasonal brunch plates and colorful, scratch-made lattes. The plant-filled industrial room runs quiet on weekdays before filling up for weekend brunch.

name: Marnes Bleues
description: Warm wine bar and bottle shop near Buttes-Chaumont pouring natural wine from a row of chrome taps. Bottles come straight off the shelves to drink alongside vegetable-forward small plates from the open kitchen.

name: Norman Paris Hôtel & Spa
description: Quiet 37-room hotel tucked off the Champs-Élysées with 1960s design and a private club atmosphere. A cozy library lounge doubles as the reception area, pouring cocktails by the fireplace before dinner at the in-house Thai restaurant.

name: Tennis Club de Paris
description: Private 16th-arrondissement sports club with 18 clay and hard tennis courts. The grounds host year-round matches, padel games, and a training pool, while a brutalist gallery doubles as a high-end fashion venue.

name: Espace Niemeyer
description: Modernist political headquarters hosting art exhibitions and fashion shows. Raw concrete interiors and a retro-futuristic hall beneath a stark white dome open up during scheduled cultural events.

name: Glaces Glazed
description: Black-fronted glacerie on rue des Martyrs serving offbeat, rock-themed ice cream and seasonal sorbets. Staff scoop inventive pairings like wasabi dark chocolate and hemp vanilla alongside hot sweet waffles.

name: Le Céleste | Restaurant Halal Paris
description: Chic halal dining room near Place d'Italie pouring zero-proof cocktails alongside a global menu of homemade bistronomy. Evening service runs steady with birthday groups cutting into thick steaks and foie gras.

name: La Crêperie Française
description: Street-side stall making sweet crêpes and savory buckwheat galettes to order on sizzling hot plates. The classic ham and Emmental is a local staple, but the signature Grand Marnier crêpe – flambéed right on the griddle – is the real show.

name: Annette
description: Stylish brasserie on Boulevard Raspail with a chic Art Deco dining room and sidewalk terrace. The menu reworks French classics – the chef’s œufs en meurette is a world champion.

name: Le Discobar
description: Minimalist Belleville listening bar pouring natural wine and cocktails up front. The tiny, neon-lit back room turns into a weekend mini-club, pushing vinyl disco and house through an analog system for a tight, moving crowd.

name: Henri SELMER Paris
description: Historic Parisian showroom and testing ground for the French saxophone and clarinet maker. Dedicated trial rooms run by appointment to test high-end woodwinds, compare mouthpieces, and manage on-site repairs.

name: Nakatsu - Karaage bar
description: Tight, window-fronted dining room serving Japanese fried chicken as sandos, curries, and donburi bowls. Plates of crispy karaage and natural wine land on high tables inside or out on the small sidewalk terrace.

name: Danico
description: Stylish speakeasy-style cocktail bar offering a core collection of artisanal cocktails. New creations frequently make their way onto the menu too - all are equally well-balanced. One of Paris' best.

name: Christophe Gaillard Gallery
description: Contemporary art gallery spanning a Marais mansion. A paved courtyard leads into two bright, clean exhibition spaces showing emerging talent alongside artist estates from the 1960s through the 1990s.

name: PLAQ Chocolat
description: Compact bean-to-bar chocolate shop filling the cobbled Rue du Nil with the scent of roasting cacao. Makers work in plain sight beside a counter serving single-origin bars, hot chocolate, and chocolate puffs to white sidewalk stools.

name: Maslow
description: Post-industrial dining room on the Seine, serving creative, internationally inspired vegetarian small plates. The Portobello Katsu and Fried Cauliflower Wings are signatures.

name: Fromagerie Laurent Dubois
description: Artisanal cheese shop from a Meilleur Ouvrier de France, where wheels are aged and prepared like fine pastries. The display cases showcase creative pairings – Roquefort layered with quince paste or goat cheese with fresh strawberries.

name: Patrick Roger
description: Art gallery-style chocolatier displaying massive cocoa sculptures in its windows. The pristine pralines and ganaches are the main event inside – sold exclusively by the box.

name: La Maison d'Isabelle
description: Latin Quarter bakery serving the region's 2018 prize-winning all-butter croissant. Each is made with organic flour and Charentes-Poitou AOP butter; the queue moves fast.

name: Montijo
description: Terracotta-toned Spanish dining cellar on the ground floor of the Maison Eugénie hotel. The open kitchen turns out rounds of warm tortilla and pan con tomate while the house sommelier pours Mediterranean natural wines.

name: Boulangerie Milligramme
description: Neighborhood bakery near Buttes-Chaumont baking natural sourdough and modern pastries in full view of the street. Fast-moving lines lead to the white tile counter for pistachio cream rolls and seeded buckwheat loaves.

name: @unrêve
description: Warm 11th arrondissement coffee shop serving full brunch plates and French-Chinese pastries. Weekend mornings run loud and busy over lattes, avocado toast, and black sesame croissants.

name: Pat Bing Soo
description: Compact Korean dessert shop tucked onto a quiet street near the Marais. The tight space serves bowls of shaved milk ice dusted with rice cake powder and scoops of lightly sweetened, homemade red bean paste.

name: Adar - Traiteur & épicerie
description: Takeaway deli and grocery in the 11th arrondissement turning out fresh Middle Eastern lunches. Front windows look straight into the kitchen, where cooks prep daily salads, labneh, and börek for a quick midday meal or park picnic.

name: Bontemps Le Restaurant "Jardin secret"
description: Hidden Marais courtyard and powder-pink dining room tucked behind a bustling patisserie. Lunch means savory tarts and house-made gnocchi, but meals always end with the bakery's signature lightly salted shortbreads.

name: Avant Comptoir de la Terre
description: Modern tapas bar with a meat-centric menu and an extensive selection of natural wines. Be prepared, this is a standing-only restaurant.

name: La Dernière Goutte
description: Stone-walled Left Bank wine shop stocking organic and biodynamic bottles from small-scale French producers. English-speaking staff pour tastings in the back room and pack cases of wine for air travel.

name: Le Procope
description: The oldest restaurant in Paris serving traditional French cuisine. The beauty is in the ambiance, building, and historic artifacts (Napoleon, Ben Franklin, and more). Can attract a tourist crowd.

name: Freddy’s
description: Lively, walk-in only Saint-Germain wine bar running steady from midday to midnight. High stools line a long counter facing an open kitchen serving a rotating menu of small plates and wine by the glass.

name: Dents de Loup
description: Working Pigalle butcher shop and neighborhood canteen sharing an open workspace. House-made charcuterie, natural wine, and a single daily hot dish move straight from the meat case to an oversized wooden block.

name: Le Nusa Bistronomie indonesienne
description: Polished Indonesian dining room in the 7th arrondissement filled with carved woodwork and Batik patterns. Big plates of authentic beef rendang and chicken satay arrive beautifully plated for date nights and celebratory dinners.

name: The Socialite Family
description: Italo-French design showroom mixing contemporary furniture and curated antiques into eclectic room setups. Velvet seating and brass lighting sit alongside small vintage plates and decorative objects.

name: Best Tofu
description: Hectic Belleville storefront serving fresh, house-made tofu and traditional Wenzhou snacks. Staff sling savory tofu puddings, steamed pork buns, and hot soy milk for quick meals at cramped tables or fast takeout.

name: Galerie Mark Hachem
description: Contemporary gallery tucked under the vaulted arcades of Place des Vosges. The curation leans into Kinetic and Op Art, filling the space with optical illusions, contemporary sculpture, and modern Middle Eastern works.

name: Louvre Museum
description: Sprawling former royal palace holding tens of thousands of artworks and antiquities across three massive wings. The glass pyramid entrance drops into opulent, winding halls that run warm and loud around the most famous pieces.

name: Hôtel Left Bank Saint Germain des Prés
description: Classic 31-room hotel right on a lively Saint-Germain street. A small elevator leads up to soundproofed rooms with exposed wood beams and classic wallpaper, while the top floors look out at the Eiffel Tower and Notre Dame.

name: Hôtel Dame des Arts
description: Left Bank boutique hotel with compact, wood-detailed rooms and a private garden courtyard. The panoramic rooftop bar stays busy into the night with cocktails and clear views of the Eiffel Tower.

name: Alluma
description: Bright, white-walled 11th arrondissement dining room running a set Levantine tasting menu. An old sculpted fresco sits above the tables as dinner runs through six Mediterranean courses.

name: Billili
description: Warm neighborhood dining room and terrace pouring natural wine and serving French small plates. Classic garlic butter escargots and house terrine share table space with savory dumplings from Reunion Island.

name: Tanguy
description: Intimate, sit-down crêperie serving ultra-thin Breton galettes under a preserved 1930s ceiling fresco. The small room trades typical maritime decor for a white-tiled bar, pouring artisanal ciders alongside crisp buckwheat crêpes.

name: Musée d'Orsay
description: Grand Beaux-Arts railway station holding the world's largest collection of Impressionist art. Galleries sit under a soaring glass roof, rising to top-floor masterpieces and a giant station clock looking out over Paris.

name: TIO BIGOTES
description: Tiny Argentine storefront near République running a steady lunch trade of handmade empanadas. The counter slings everything from classic spicy beef to smash burger fillings, packing orders for takeout or a fast bite at the few tables.

name: O P'ti Paris
description: Unpretentious neighborhood bar sitting along a pedestrian passage in the 10th arrondissement. Cheap pints and Turkish flatbreads cross the counter all night, with the drinking spilling straight out onto the paved laneway.

name: Café Pli - Temple
description: Intimate 11th arrondissement cafe dedicated to writing letters to the future. Specialty lattes come with stationery and wax seals, while a wall of dated cubbies holds sealed messages scheduled for delivery up to twenty years later.

name: Wistaria
description: Serene Taiwanese tea house in the 6th arrondissement steeping single-origin leaves and guiding traditional ceremonies. Antique furniture and ceramic teaware fill a quiet room running slow, deliberate tea service.

name: Club Bus Palladium
description: Basement club and cocktail bar sitting beneath a new Pigalle boutique hotel. Live bands and late-night DJ sets play the central stage, backed by a round-the-clock restaurant upstairs.

name: Musée du Luxembourg
description: Intimate museum on the edge of the Jardin du Luxembourg running two or three temporary shows a year. Without a permanent collection to navigate, visits are brief and focused before stepping straight into the gardens.

name: Cafe Singuliers
description: Spacious 11th arrondissement cafe balancing specialty coffee and laptops with a refined, daily-changing menu. A vintage wood stove sits in the middle of the room, and warm chocolate chip cookies move fast from the open kitchen.

name: Hôtel Balzac Paris & Spa Ikoï
description: Refined hotel in a 19th-century townhouse just off the Champs-Élysées, styled as an intimate Parisian residence. A Japanese-inspired spa offers treatments on tatami mats; a private entrance connects to the three-star Pierre Gagnaire.

name: Le Petit Pontoise
description: Bustling Latin Quarter bistro serving generous plates of traditional French cooking – think 7-hour lamb and duck confit. The small, intimate room is always packed and noisy with a mostly local crowd.

name: Les Vins Du Matin
description: Cozy natural wine bar where bottles are pulled from shop shelves to drink on-site for a corkage fee. The small room gets loud and crowded, fueled by shareable plates of panisse fritters and a standout cheesecake.

name: Aux Prés Cyril Lignac
description: Chic 1950s bistro with its original floral wallpaper and red leather banquettes intact. The menu reworks French classics using global flavors – expect miso-caramelized black cod and satay beef filet.

name: Chez l'Ami Louis
description: Time-capsule bistro with blotchy walls and just a dozen tables set with pink linen. Expect huge portions of classic French country cooking – whole roasted chicken, slabs of foie gras, and towers of crispy frites.

name: La Boîte aux Lettres
description: Cozy neighborhood bistro serving seasonal French dishes in a small, book-lined room. The pavé de boeuf is a staple, but the "pour les indécis" sampler lets tables share multiple desserts.

name: Le P'tit Troquet
description: Cozy, old-fashioned bistro serving generous plates of market-based French classics. The two intimate dining rooms fill up quickly – book ahead for a table.

name: Popote Bébé
description: Batignolles boutique selling organic, French-made baby food and infant formula. The shop stocks additive-free meals, single-ingredient purees for starting solids, and convenient pouches for feeding on the go.

name: Les Arlots
description: Classic Parisian bistro that built its reputation on one dish: a legendary sausage and mash. The small room is packed nightly, with a long zinc bar and wine bottles lining the walls.

name: Molitor Hotel & Spa Paris - MGallery Collection
description: Five-star hotel built into a restored 1920s bathhouse in the 16th arrondissement. Rooms wrap around a massive heated outdoor pool lined with yellow and blue Art Deco galleries, while a second pool and sprawling spa sit underground.

name: Le temps des cerises
description: Old-school Parisian bistro occupying a medieval house with a bright mosaic facade. A classic zinc bar anchors the 1930s interior, where blackboard menus list seasonal French staples like steak frites and escargots.

name: Café Rhum Marin
description: Intimate 11th arrondissement bar lined with large glass jars of house-infused rums. The relaxed room pours sweet carambar and skull-marked chili blends alongside simple charcuterie boards.

name: Café Des Délices
description: All-day Belleville café with a polished zinc bar and a large pedestrian terrace. The kitchen runs steady from morning coffee through casual lunches of lamb kebabs on flatbread, shifting to shared small plates late into the night.

name: La Bourse et La Vie
description: Intimate bistro with green velvet banquettes, serving perfected versions of French classics. The steak au poivre is the standout dish – book well in advance for one of the few tables.

name: Fréquence
description: Listening bar where shelves of vinyl replace the usual rows of liquor, with funk and soul spinning all night. Cocktails are inventive and precise, using house infusions and hand-carved ice.

name: Catacombs of Paris
description: A renowned tourist attraction that allows visitors to explore the labyrinths of tunnels and chambers beneath the streets of Paris - they've been used as cemeteries for over two thousand years. A unique perspective of the city.

name: Sugaar
description: Intimate, candle-lit dining room serving refined Basque country cooking. Everything is cooked over charcoal – the main event is a matured Txuleta steak sourced from a single farm in Spain.

name: U’s Canteen - Paris 11eme
description: American-style takeaway dishing up smash burgers and crispy fried chicken. A popular last stop after a night out in Belleville – the house-made fries are essential.

name: Le Bar à sushi Izumi
description: Traditional sushi bar with just a handful of counter seats for watching the Japanese chef at work. The menu is classic and seasonal, focusing on fatty tuna, grilled eel, and a tight selection of sakes.

name: Creamy Daily
description: Compact Rue Sainte-Anne cafe whisking specialty matcha and slicing Japanese mille crepe cakes. The soft-hued room fills fast, sending most orders for signature cheese-foam drinks and light yuzu slices out the door.

name: Kura-ge
description: Minimalist matcha house whisking high-grade, unsweetened Uji tea over solid oak counters. Small, potent drinks sit alongside creative pastries and shelves stocked with ceramic bowls and bamboo brewing tools.

name: Laïzé Sainte-Avoye
description: Quiet Marais cafe matching exposed stone walls with the wooden drawers of a traditional Chinese pharmacy. The tiny room holds just a few seats for traditionally whisked matcha, specialty espresso, and Taiwanese tea.

name: Aux Crus de Bourgogne
description: 1930s Montorgueil bistro serving hearty, wine-fueled lunches of boeuf bourguignon and escargots. White-clothed tables sit close together under vintage mirrors, filling a cozy room lined with dark wood and red leather banquettes.

name: Le Petit Vendôme
description: Packed, old-school bistro serving hearty French classics right off Place Vendôme. The loud, elbow-to-elbow dining room runs on steak frites and heavy pours of wine, with hanging sausages and a busy zinc bar up front.

name: Brutos
description: Low-lit Brazilian steakhouse serving flame-grilled meats and natural wine in a stripped-back stone room. Bar seats face the open charcoal grill, while tables spill out onto a terrace next to Square Gardette.

name: Mmmozza..!
description: Tiny Marais deli slinging made-to-order sandwiches packed with fresh Campania mozzarella and cured meats. The small shop runs primarily on takeaway, with orders carried directly across the street to the Square du Temple.

name: Focaccia NOVETTINO - Bastille
description: Modern sandwich counter turning out thick, custom-built focaccia for a fast lunch. Touchscreen kiosks keep the line moving for quick takeaway orders loaded with cured meats, artichoke cream, and fresh mozzarella.

name: La Baguette du Relais
description: Fast-paced Marais takeaway stuffing classic steak-frites straight into fresh baguettes. Sliced sirloin, shoestring fries, and a famous secret sauce pile into a heavy lunch eaten on the move or at a few outdoor high-tops.

name: Bremond Capela
description: Discreet Marais gallery sitting under a large glass roof. The space shows contemporary art focused on social and political themes, with directors often walking the floor to talk through the work.

name: Pozzetto 2
description: Compact Marais gelateria and espresso counter with minimal seating and a takeaway window. Staff serve small-batch gelato from covered metal wells with traditional spatulas, pulling quick espresso shots and pouring thick hot chocolate.

name: Pierre Hermé
description: Sleek patisserie with elegant, brightly lit glass cases. Perfectly uniform macarons come in unconventional flavors like rose and lychee, carefully packed into sturdy boxes for takeaway.

name: Shodai Matcha
description: Japanese-style tea room serving savory Korean bowls alongside a massive menu of matcha desserts. The space runs steady late into the night, sending out layered mille-crêpes, sweet milk teas, and towering shaved ice.

name: Manteigaria
description: Takeaway Portuguese bakery turning out endless rounds of warm Pastéis de Nata. A bell rings as each fresh batch leaves the open kitchen, served straight across the marble counter with ground cinnamon and a quick espresso.

name: La Pâtisserie Cyril Lignac
description: Warm neighborhood pastry shop serving elevated French classics across carved oak counters. Pure butter croissants handle the morning rush, while signature Equinoxe cakes are boxed up for celebrations.

name: La Panifacture
description: Narrow, pale-wood bakery in the 11th arrondissement baking ancient-flour breads and flaky pastries. The small takeaway counter faces a glass wall looking directly into the active production space.

name: Basilique du Sacré-Cœur de Montmartre
description: Bright white basilica marking the highest point in Paris. Steep front steps double as a casual grandstand for sunset views over the skyline, giving way to a quiet nave filled with prayer candles and a massive gold mosaic.

name: Le Pain Retrouvé
description: Takeout-only bakery on Rue des Martyrs turning out slow-fermented loaves, braided brioche, and almond croissants. Fast-moving lines stretch onto the sidewalk while bakers shape dough in full view behind the service counter.

name: Hôtel Elysées Union
description: Quiet 19th-century residence turned unfussy hotel in the 16th arrondissement. Superior rooms open onto balconies facing the Eiffel Tower, while larger apartments provide a practical base near the Arc de Triomphe.

name: Juicy Cave à Manger
description: Intimate Canal Saint-Martin wine bar pouring natural bottles alongside simple plates of cheese, charcuterie, and hot dogs. The Franco-American owners work the small room, guiding relaxed tastings and talking through the wines.

name: Restaurant Guy Savoy
description: Grand dining rooms on the Seine serving elaborate French tasting menus. Long meals run through a series of slate-gray salons, moving from iced oysters to artichoke and black truffle soup with warm brioche for dipping.

name: Passerina
description: Tiny, no-reservations Italian wine bar near the Marché d'Aligre serving house-made pasta and Roman sharing plates. The midcentury-styled room stays laid-back, pouring natural wine for casual, spontaneous dinners.

name: Gilou
description: Warm neighborhood bistro next to Buttes-Chaumont serving handmade pastas, seasonal plates, and natural wine. Paper tablecloths sit under exposed beams in the restored butcher shop, which opens onto a hidden upstairs terrace.

name: The Red Wheelbarrow Bookstore
description: Independent English-language bookstore facing the Luxembourg Gardens, packed floor-to-ceiling with curated titles. Staff trade recommendations in the sunlit main room, while an adjacent storefront holds a bilingual children's shop.

name: Smith & Son
description: Historic English-language bookstore on Rue de Rivoli stocking thousands of titles, international press, and British groceries. Wood-paneled rooms lead to an upstairs tea room facing the Tuileries Garden.

name: Jeu de Paume
description: Art center located in the Jardin des Tuileries curating multimedia exhibits from the 19th to 21st centuries. The institution also displays other avant-garde works. A beautiful space for photography and video enthusiasts.

name: La Bellevilloise
description: Sprawling multi-level music venue running late-night gigs and club events that stretch into the early morning. Weekend crowds fill the glass-roofed indoor garden for live jazz brunches under century-old olive trees.

name: La Cave de Belleville
description: Airy Belleville wine shop and deli stacked floor-to-ceiling with natural and biodynamic bottles. The stone-walled room centers on a busy retail counter for takeaway cheese and charcuterie, while the marble bar pours casual glasses.

name: Villa La Roche
description: Home designed by renowned architect Le Corbusier that now serves as a museum for his works, paintings, and plans. The building was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2016. Architecture meets art.

name: The Centre Pompidou
description: Cultural complex that houses the National Museum of Modern Art and is known for its eccentric exterior. Alongside artwork, the forum also contains a library and music center. A multifaceted space.

name: Lafayette Anticipations
description: Restored 19th-century Marais warehouse operating as a free contemporary art space and studio. Motorized platforms in the central glass tower physically shift the floors to build a custom layout for each new show.

name: Pluto
description: Minimalist concrete restaurant sitting in the hidden courtyard of the Lafayette Anticipations art foundation. Dinner brings inventive sharing plates and natural wine to blonde wood tables near the open kitchen.

name: La Patate Douce Coffee Shop & Radio
description: 1970s-style cafe and listening bar tied to an independent Parisian web radio station. Specialty coffee and Mamiche pastries run the daytime hours before the room shifts to tequila cocktails and live DJ sets.

name: Musée des Arts Décoratifs
description: Vast design museum filling the western wing of the Louvre. Seven floors of dimly lit galleries and reconstructed period rooms hold centuries of French furniture, fashion, and jewelry.

name: Fou de Pâtisserie
description: Small pastry shop on rue Montorgueil gathering signature desserts from top Parisian chefs into a single room. The counter holds a rotating greatest hits collection of French baking, with delicate cakes boxed up for takeaway.

name: Musée National Picasso-Paris
description: Restored 17th-century Marais mansion displaying the world's largest collection of Pablo Picasso's art. Grand Baroque stairs and historic salons open into crisp white galleries filled with his paintings, ceramics, and sculptures.

name: Le Clown Bar - Restaurant
description: Historic bistro next to the Cirque d'Hiver covered in 1920s ceramic clown tiles. The busy dining room serves modern French small plates and pours natural wine from a classic zinc bar.

name: Pizzeria Iovine's
description: Bustling Neapolitan pizzeria serving traditional, puffy-crusted pizzas from an open kitchen. Simple wooden tables sit against exposed brick walls for fast-paced dinners of classic margheritas and fresh burrata.

name: Galerie Sobering
description: Compact, glass-fronted gallery in the Marais showing contemporary painting. The minimalist street-level room hangs emerging talent alongside established artists in quiet, thoughtful exhibitions.

name: Now Reformer
description: Serene Pilates studio near the Opéra running intense Reformer sessions on seven machines. The minimalist, mirror-lined room smells of amber and black pepper, with a small counter pouring matcha and coffee after class.

name: Augustin Marchand d'Vins
description: Intimate, stone-walled Saint-Germain wine bar and cellar run by its namesake owner. He pours rare bottles and shares the stories behind them over small plates of fresh scallops, rillettes, and cheese.

name: Tuileries Garden
description: Vast formal garden stretching between the Louvre and Place de la Concorde. Wide gravel paths run past manicured lawns toward large stone fountains, where loose green metal chairs are pulled right to the water's edge.

name: Grand Palais
description: Massive Beaux-Arts exhibition hall with a soaring glass and iron roof. The cavernous, light-filled nave stages a steady rotation of blockbuster art fairs, runway shows, and major cultural events.

name: Little Red Door
description: A constant on The World's 50 Best Bars radar for a decade, Little Red Door has made a name for itself in the cocktail scene. Drinks here are well thought-out and the menu evolves further each year. A fun atmosphere.

name: Galerie Amélie du Chalard
description: Contemporary art gallery set up as a private Saint-Germain-des-Prés apartment. Abstract paintings, ceramics, and sculptures sit alongside modern furniture in quiet, domestic rooms that open to a garden.

name: Angelina
description: Famous tearoom noted for its elegant pastries, rich hot chocolate, and belle époque aesthetic. Located just five minutes from the Louvre. Though Angelina doesn't take reservations, the line tends to move quickly.

name: Carré Pain de Mie
description: Minimalist Japanese bakery baking soft, square shokupan loaves on Rue Rambuteau. The airy cafe serves thick-cut tonkatsu sandos and sweet French toast alongside stacks of fresh bread ready for takeout.

name: Chanceux
description: Narrow Latin Quarter cafe pairing specialty coffee with hot, thick sandwiches. Formica tables line the compact, unfinished room, squeezing in space for morning egg buns, grilled mushroom melts, and house-made pastrami.

name: iRASSHAi
description: Sprawling Japanese grocery and food hall shifting gears for dinner. A bright ground-floor canteen pairs casual plates with cocktails, while an intimate basement izakaya serves tasting menus.

name: Café Berry
description: Stylish Marais coffee shop serving all-day brunch plates like Turkish eggs and black avocado toast. The homemade pastries are the real draw – expect a weekend queue for the cinnamon rolls and Basque cheesecake.

name: Café Nuances
description: Striking modern espresso bar pouring single-origin coffee and rose matcha lattes across a glowing neon counter. Steady queues move fast for takeaway cups and cinnamon rolls, with a handful of sleek stools for a quick stop.

name: Hotel Hana
description: Boutique hotel balancing Japanese simplicity and Parisian opulence: rooms feature iroko wood, straw walls, and bicolored marble. The bar specializes in cocktails made exclusively from French and Japanese spirits.

name: Harry's New York Bar
description: A Paris classic and a staple for many big names. Harry's New York Bar has welcomed the likes of Hemmingway and Coco Chanel - even James Bond. Good drinks and live music accompany the bar's rich history.

name: Hôtel Le Grand Mazarin
description: Maximalist Marais hotel layering antique furniture, tapestry canopy beds, and dense patterns across the rooms. A mosaic-tiled pool sits underground for quiet afternoons, while the main floor pours cocktails alongside Ashkenazi dishes.

name: Foodi Jia-Ba-Buay
description: Cozy Taiwanese restaurant serving traditional dishes alongside European-style desserts. A great spot for casual dining and pan-Asian flavors.

name: Les enfants du marché
description: Energetic natural wine counter open to the walkways of the Marché des Enfants Rouges. Ambitious seafood and daily plates pass straight from the open kitchen to tight rows of crowded bar stools.

name: Le Voltaire
description: Le Voltaire serves exquisite French flavors with a variety of decadent meal options. A visit to this chic Parisian establishment set against the picturesque view of the Seine, and the Louvre Museum is the perfect cap-off for any Paris trip.

name: Grande Brasserie
description: Wood-paneled Bastille brasserie pairing reliable French classics with natural wine. The room runs steady with orders of fresh oysters, pâté en croûte, and generous desserts meant to share.

name: Sammy and Joe paris
description: Compact 11th arrondissement cafe run by a local couple serving American comfort food. Hot grilled cheese sandwiches and thick BLTs share table space with fresh cinnamon rolls and mugs of filter coffee.

name: MERLO CAFFÈ
description: Warm Marais cafe pouring specialty espresso and black sesame matcha around a wood-paneled bar. The quiet, flower-filled room serves thick banana bread and seasonal lattes across small bistro tables.

name: Babka Zana
description: Levantine bakery in South Pigalle baking braided sourdough babkas and challah sandwiches in an open workshop. Warm chocolate-hazelnut rolls and savory borekas go straight from the takeaway counter to the sidewalk benches.

name: HolyBelly
description: Upbeat, brick-lined cafe slinging specialty coffee and savory pancake stacks from morning through late afternoon. The loud, diner-style room runs strictly walk-in with a steady wait for snug leather booths.

name: La Fontaine de Mars
description: Classic Parisian bistro serving rich Southwest cooking in a room lined with dark wood and checkered tablecloths. Meals start with sliced salami and bread before moving to heavy plates of duck confit and cassoulet.

name: Lac de la Sourderie
description: An ensemble of subsidized apartment buildings referred to as the "Versailles for the People" when it was first built. For those interested in architectural history, this is a great stop.

name: Aillaud Towers
description: Townhouse complex on the outer fringes of Paris. Built in 1976, these residential buildings are worth a visit for 70s architecture buffs.

name: Picasso's Arenas
description: Brutalist apartment complex on the outer edges of Paris. A stop for architecture and gaming lovers as it can also be found in the "Seine-Saint-Denis" version of Monopoly.

name: WAX
description: Minimalist audiophile bar pouring complex cocktails and playing vinyl through a high-fidelity sound system. DJs spin jazz and electronic tracks in the raw concrete room, keeping the space loud and heavily social.

name: STÉRÉO
description: Cozy South Pigalle wine bar pouring natural wines and serving shared plates to a strict vinyl soundtrack. Turntables spin funk and disco behind the bar, bringing lively pocket-club energy to the candlelit stone room.

name: Patine Bistrot
description: Minimalist, brick-walled bistro in the 11th arrondissement pairing natural wine with modern French cooking. The dining room runs loud and lively through the evening service over set menus and warm tarte tatin.

name: doublevie
description: Three-story Montmartre venue splitting the night between Mediterranean dining and a hidden basement vinyl bar. Small plates and natural wine fill the upper floors, while the cellar runs late with cocktails and DJ sets.

name: Notre-Dame Cathedral of Paris
description: Newly restored Gothic cathedral sitting on the Île de la Cité with flying buttresses and stone gargoyles. The massive interior takes a half hour to walk through, passing beneath soaring vaults and surviving 13th-century rose windows.

name: Listener
description: Warm audiophile bar pouring natural wine and coffee over a curated vinyl soundtrack. Downstairs, groups book soundproof basement rooms by the hour to play records on high-end audio systems.

name: La Crèmerie
description: Petit Italian-inspired wine bar serving fresh, comforting, and unique dishes. Their kitchen also offers a selection of cheese and small bites. Perfect to pair.

name: NOTRE DAME Music Bar
description: Hushed, low-lit listening bar lined with thousands of vinyl records. Vintage speakers play full albums from start to finish alongside a steady flow of craft cocktails and natural wine.

name: Les Deux Abeilles
description: Homey and elegant, this tea house is a great place to stop for lunch or afternoon tea. Only a few minutes walk from the Eiffel Tower, it's a perfect place to relax after a morning of touring the city.

name: Hauser & Wirth
description: Contemporary art gallery taking over a grand 19th-century townhouse near the Champs-Élysées. Free, rotating exhibitions run through four floors of high-ceilinged rooms linked by a prominent spiral staircase.

name: Les Espaces d'Abraxas
description: This housing complex comprises three monumental buildings with classic post-modern style and accommodates approximately 600 residential units. It is a must-see for architecture enthusiasts and fans of the Hunger Games movies.

name: Boulangerie-Pâtisserie Terroirs d'Avenir
description: Small takeaway bakery on Rue du Nil making slow-fermented breads and seasonal pastries. A steady line spills out the door for warm croissants and large loaves baked from ancient wheat.

name: Au Passage
description: French restaurant with a lean towards tapas-style dining. The modern dishes pair well with the venue's selection of natural wines. Cozy atmosphere - an ideal spot for sharing plates with a group of friends.

name: JJ Hings Ice Cream
description: Colorful ice cream shop turning out mix-in-heavy scoops and fresh brown butter waffle cones. Fast-moving lines wrap past the yellow metal benches outside, with most heading down to the nearby Canal Saint-Martin to eat.

name: Enishi
description: Intimate Japanese dining room in Montmartre run by a mother-and-daughter team. Tables fill fast for traditional home cooking, with hot pots, tonkatsu, and bento boxes passed across the tight, minimalist room.

name: Yvonne
description: Warm, subdued 11th arrondissement bistro serving sharp updates to French classics. Plates of miso leeks and beef tartare sit alongside glasses of wine and thick slices of tarte tatin.

name: Sam So – Korean Noodles
description: Compact Korean shop on Rue de Richelieu serving daily hand-pulled noodles. Bar seats line the small room for quick dinners of rich jajangmyeon, spicy seafood soup, and traditional banchan.

name: Ojii
description: Moody Japanese restaurant in Saint-Germain modeled after a 1970s Tokyo bar. Intimate rosewood booths fill with plates of Hokkaido wagyu, tuna carpaccio, and wasabi margaritas.

name: Panpan Pizza
description: Minimalist Sentier pizzeria baking thick Detroit-style pies with crispy, caramelized edges. Deep rectangular pans hit the table for mixing and matching slices or splitting whole pizzas in a warm, stylish dining room.

name: FACE B
description: Intimate neighborhood izakaya serving Japanese small plates and natural wine. The owner spins vinyl in the stone-walled room while tables fill with shared dishes and open bottles for the evening.

name: La Cave à Michel
description: Little wine bar where the owner himself often works the counter. Large selection of natural wines that the friendly staff will go over while also recommending excellent small plate food pairings.

name: Le Pigalle
description: An elegant 4-star hotel located near Sacré-Cœur, featuring vintage furniture and neoclassical decor. The hotel offers a restaurant, bar, café, and a basement lounge with a jukebox.

name: General Fermentation
description: Small 11th arrondissement micro-bakery turning out hand-kneaded sourdough and house-made ferments alongside natural wine. The cash-only shop relies on natural starters, packing seasonal kimchi and fresh kombucha into returnable jars.

name: Le Syndicat
description: Cocktail bar hidden behind a poster-covered storefront on Rue du Faubourg Saint-Denis. The dim, concrete-lined room runs on a steady hip-hop soundtrack, pouring cocktails made exclusively with traditional French spirits.

name: La Dame De Canton
description: Unique location offering live music, dinner, and drinks on a wooden boat by the River Seine. Highlights include their pizzas which are great to enjoy on the outdoor terrace.

name: Experimental Cocktail Club
description: Dimly lit Montorgueil bar mixing craft cocktails behind an unmarked street door. Velvet booths and exposed brick walls fill up fast as the music gets loud into the night.

name: Prescription Cocktail Club
description: Dimly lit cocktail speakeasy behind a discreet wooden door in Saint-Germain-des-Prés. Theatrical, fabric-draped rooms operate at two speeds, keeping the ground floor loud with a DJ while the upstairs runs as a moody, low-slung lounge.

name: Arc de Triomphe
description: Iconic monument on Place Charles de Gaulle that finds its way onto every Paris itinerary - at the very least, bear with the tourists for a quick pitstop. Built to commemorate Napolean's victories and includes a skyline observation deck.

name: Paulownia
description: Relaxed 20th-arrondissement bistro in a former factory space pairing ambitious French cooking with all-natural wines. Counter seats face an open kitchen turning out seasonal plates like hot puff pastry pâté and roasted squab.

name: Mensch
description: Compact New York-style deli turning out house-made corned beef, fresh bagels, and crispy latkes from an open kitchen. Thick Ashkenazi sandwiches fill the bright yellow Formica counter and small wooden tables.

name: OTTO - MOUFFETARD
description: Minimalist Latin Quarter izakaya built around a central open kitchen and a binchotan grill. High stools line the counter for French-Japanese sharing plates passed straight off the fire, with the walk-in-only room packing out early.

name: L'Altro Frenchie
description: Energetic 40-seat dining room on Rue du Nil turning out modern Italian plates from an open kitchen. Orders of ricotta gnudi and rabbit ragù hit the tables alongside a deep lineup of natural Mediterranean wines.

name: L'Arlequin
description: Three-screen arthouse cinema on rue de Rennes screening independent, foreign, and classic films in their original language. The Art Deco main auditorium runs 70mm prints, while a small bar pours pre-show drinks.

name: Carboni's
description: Plant-filled Marais dining room serving fresh handmade pasta and warm focaccia across marble tables. Dinner naturally spills into the hidden basement bar, pouring late-night cocktails and vermouth to a vinyl soundtrack.

name: GRAMME PARIS
description: Minimalist 11th arrondissement bistro running with dense, candlelit energy through the evening. The kitchen serves seasonal French cooking alongside a deep rotation of natural wine.

name: Woo Jung
description: Elegant dining room near the Trocadéro pairing authentic Korean cooking with a curated French wine list. The family-run kitchen sends out spicy stews, raw crab, and marinated beef to tables dressed in white linens.

name: EnYaa - Saké & Champagne
description: Intimate Japanese dining room near the Palais Royal serving traditional Kaiseki menus on handmade ceramics. Counter seats face the chef for multi-course dinners paired with pours from a thousand-bottle saké and champagne cellar.

name: Shang Palace
description: Opulent Cantonese dining room with jade columns, marble tables, and crystal chandeliers. Two-course Peking duck and delicate dim sum arrive in family-style portions for quiet, shared meals.

name: Jugaad - Restaurant Indien Paris 2
description: Modern Indian restaurant mixing original Parisian bistro features with vibrant saffron and moss green walls. An open kitchen with two golden tandoors fires regional sharing plates and fresh naan, served alongside gin and house tonics.

name: Bonvivant Pizza
description: Lively 5th arrondissement pizzeria serving thin, crispy Roman pies and natural wine. The chic, cozy room stays crowded, and pizzas arrive with scissors for cutting.

name: Casimir
description: Lively 10th arrondissement bistro with a terrace on a pedestrian square near Gare du Nord. The busy room runs on low-intervention wine and rustic French sharing plates like whole roasted chicken and Beef Wellington.

name: Causier - Coffee & Brunch
description: Warm 11th arrondissement cafe pairing specialty coffee with sweet and savory morning plates. Tables fill early for breakfast burritos, blueberry pancakes, and long conversations over flat whites.

name: Calice
description: French-Japanese wine bar pairing natural vintages with refined, binchotan-grilled small plates. A lively granite counter faces the open kitchen, leading back to leather banquettes set under a large glass skylight.

name: Sobremesa
description: Intimate, candlelit Montmartre wine bar centered on an open kitchen and a monthly lineup of resident chefs. Chrome stools line the counter for sharing small plates and off-menu natural wines.

name: Ici-même
description: Rustic neighborhood wine bar and bottle shop pouring a daily rotation of natural wines. Bottles come straight from the retail shelves to the table, opened alongside simple plates of local cheese and charcuterie.

name: Fringe upside
description: Sprawling consignment shop running with the tight curation of a modern concept store. Racks of premium second-hand labels fill the two-level industrial space, meticulously sorted by size and color.

name: RoseMarket Vintage
description: Intimate vintage shop in the 9th arrondissement selling high-end designer pieces from the 1970s and 1980s. Carefully sorted racks carry Yves Saint Laurent, Chanel, and Hermès garments for slow, unpressured browsing.

name: Les Archives Vintage
description: Curated designer vintage boutique in the 6th arrondissement stocking rare pieces from the 1970s to the early 2000s. Every garment hangs alongside a Polaroid of its original runway debut.

name: Vintage shop de Chloé
description: Intimate Rue de Charonne boutique filled with carefully sourced garments and designer accessories from the 1920s to the 1980s. The owner works the floor daily, detailing the exact fabric, construction, and history of each piece.

name: Bobby
description: Busy Montmartre trattoria serving generous plates of fresh pasta and Neapolitan pizza from an open kitchen. Warm evenings push tables out onto the terrace for late dinners and limoncello spritzes.

name: La Grande Épicerie
description: Sprawling Left Bank food hall and high-end grocery packed with specialty produce, fresh baguettes, and a massive cheese counter. Busy aisles lead past cases of lunchtime sandwiches and vacuum-sealed French butter ready for the flight home.

name: MATIERE PREMIERE Parfums - Paris Saint-Honoré
description: Minimalist Rue Saint-Honoré boutique selling perfumes built around single, high-dose raw ingredients. Staff lead detailed smelling sessions at the counter, breaking down the botanical origin of each scent.

name: AT
description: Minimalist dining room with concrete floors and light wood, serving a singular, artistic tasting menu. Each course arrives as a surprise, plated on bespoke ceramics from Scandinavian and Japanese artists.

name: Hôtel Grand Powers
description: Grand Haussmann corner building in the Golden Triangle mixing heritage moldings with Art Deco interiors. Upper-floor balconies look directly onto the Eiffel Tower, while a full marble spa sits below.

name: Bercy Village
description: White stone wine warehouses line a pedestrian street of shops and restaurants. Old rail tracks cut through the cobblestones past busy terraces and a massive cinema.

name: Les Pavillons de Bercy - Musée des Arts Forains
description: Fantastical museum of 19th-century fairground arts where the rides and games still run. Visits are hands-on, with chances to hop on bicycle carousels and play mechanical races in theatrical, darkened halls.

name: Café Nuances - Vendôme
description: Specialty roaster inside a protected 1920s building, where original Art Deco details meet a futuristic, glowing orange interior. Single-origin espresso and fresh pistachio babka are served at the satin-finish steel bar.

name: The Hood
description: Neighborhood canteen shifting from morning coffee to Singaporean dinner service. The kitchen turns out Hainanese chicken rice and kaya toast in a casual room with natural wine and a communal piano.

name: OFR Bookshop
description: Marais bookshop and gallery specializing in fashion, photography, and art. Stacks of rare zines and international magazines fill the front; the back room hosts a constant rotation of exhibitions and artist events.

name: Cypsèle
description: Intimate Île Saint-Louis dining room serving a tasting menu that changes every service. An open kitchen warms the retro-modern space, sending out elemental wood-fired dishes and sharp wine pairings.

name: Blois
description: City on the banks of the Loire. Home to a number of historic landmarks including the Château de Blois, which was once home to a number of French kings. The castle has been beautifully preserved and is now open to the public for tours.

name: Chez Nous
description: A chic wine bar with indoor counter seats and tables outside. Alongside an impressive vino menu, Chez Nous also serves appetizers, small plates, and charcuterie boards. Ideal for alfresco drinks in the afternoon sun.

name: Au Paradis du Gourmand
description: Traditional boulangerie formerly supplying the Elysée Palace with its prize-winning baguette. Pistachio pastries sell out early, while the counter stacks savory curry and squid ink loaves.

name: E. DEHILLERIN
description: Historic kitchenware warehouse packed floor-to-ceiling with copper pots and obscure molds. Finding a price means checking codes in a binder, and staff wrap purchases in brown paper and string.

name: KAMA-ASA
description: Tokyo kitchenware specialist hidden in a Saint-Germain alley, stocking hundreds of Japanese knives and cast iron pans. Staff guide detailed consultations to match blades with specific cooking styles and sharpen knives on-site.

name: Westfield Forum des Halles
description: Massive underground mall descends four levels beneath an undulating glass canopy. Sunlit concourses connect global brands and a cinema directly to Paris’s busiest transit hub.

name: Fondation Cartier pour l'art contemporain
description: Glass-walled art center that merges its exhibition space with a wild garden. Rotating shows and massive site-specific commissions fill the transparent, light-soaked floors.

name: L’Ecrin Gourmand
description: Corner boulangerie in the 12th baking one of the city's top ten baguettes. Glass cases distract from the daily bread run with rows of intricate cakes and fresh lunch sandwiches.

name: A. Simon
description: Historic supplier dense with professional-grade kitchen tools and tableware. Floor-to-ceiling shelves hold heavy Mauviel copper pans, baking molds, and classic bistro glassware sold by the piece.

name: Boulangerie Guyot Ferreira
description: Compact Rue Monge bakery consistently ranked among the city's best for traditional baguettes. The tiled shop is strictly takeaway, with a fast-moving line for fresh loaves and sandwiches.

name: Fondation Le Corbusier
description: White concrete villas tucked into a private cul-de-sac. The interior guides movement up a curved ramp through geometric rooms and a double-height gallery.

name: Haikara Izakaya
description: Tiny, rowdy izakaya blasting hip-hop and pouring natural wine. Counter seats face an open kitchen turning out shareable duck tataki and okonomiyaki.

name: Tapisserie - Charonne
description: Septime’s rustic bakery offshoot baking with seasonal fruit and heritage flours. Sticky maple tarts and caramelized choux stack up on the wooden counter.

name: Nami Coffee Shop - Étienne Marcel
description: Tokyo-style coffee bar spinning vinyl at the Passage du Grand-Cerf entrance. Spiral stairs climb to low-lit seating for spicy matcha and sesame miso cookies.

name: La Cave Pigalle
description: Pigalle wine shop stocking a rigorous lineup of natural vintages and grower champagnes. Vinyl spins on the turntable while owners help navigate the shelves of living wines.

name: Le Wallace Hôtel & Bar
description: Retro-modern hotel in the 15th channeling the Italian Riviera with glossy wood and terrazzo. A glass-roofed bar anchors the courtyard, while the rooftop terrace serves cocktails facing the Eiffel Tower.

name: Waly-Fay
description: Traditional Senegalese dishes served in an industrial-chic setting with an open kitchen. Highlights include Yassa chicken, jumbo shrimp creole, and soursop sorbet.

name: La Renommee
description: Dimly lit dining room with leather banquettes, serving French classics and New York steaks like filet au poivre. A hushed speakeasy lounge is tucked into the vaulted cellar below for classic cocktails.

name: Adraba
description: Corner bistro with a large open kitchen and the smell of charcoal coming from the grill. Modern Levantine sharing plates and Georgian wines fuel a festive, late-night scene – especially for those sitting at the counter.

name: Jais
description: Lively modern bistro where tables are packed tight around a large zinc bar. The semi-open kitchen serves refined French classics like roasted octopus and sole meunière, keeping the room loud and energetic all night.

name: Alleno
description: Grand dining room in a neoclassical pavilion where modern French cuisine is built around intensely pure sauces. Service is highly personalized, starting with a pre-visit call to tailor the menu for each table.

name: Oktobre
description: Seasonal tasting menus build on classic French technique with inventive Asian spices and complex sauces. The intimate room has an autumnal palette, with smoked oak tables and confidential lighting at night.

name: Chez Marius
description: This old-school restaurant serves French-Italian food in a cozy and friendly environment. The menu and wine list change regularly, so be ready to try something new.

name: Mova
description: Restaurant blending traditional French cuisine with innovative flair, offering adaptable multi-course menus that cater to various tastes. The atmosphere is inviting, with seasonal focus on fish and vegetables enhancing each dish.

name: Soces
description: Belleville seafood spot serving raw shellfish and seasonal plates to share. The stone-walled room gets loud and tight, with candlelit tables full of whole fish and natural wine.

name: Dandelion
description: Spacious bistro mixing limestone pillars and concrete floors in a village-like pocket of the 20th. The kitchen sends out sharp, creative plates like barbecue sweetbreads and monkfish alongside a tight rotation of natural wines.

name: Café du coin
description: Lively corner bistro serving affordable lunch sets and evening small plates. The tiled room gets loud as locals crowd the formica counter for natural wine and sourdough pizzettes.

name: Masaikuta
description: Intimate, stone-walled dining room serving Masahide Ikuta’s precise French-Japanese tasting menus. Blond wood counters face an open kitchen grilling over binchotan while vinyl records spin.

name: Winkel 43
description: Winkel 43 is a casual lunch spot with simple, tasty sandwiches and plates. But the real draw here is the apple pie, said by many to be the best in Amsterdam. Stop by for some coffee and cake.

name: Hilversum
description: Hilversum is less than a 40-minute drive from the capital - an ideal escape. Once called the "Garden of Amsterdam", many visit for its walking and cycling opportunities. The town itself is also nice, with a few interesting buildings.

name: Groente & Fruit Zuid
description: Neighborhood corner greengrocer stacked with fresh produce, olive oils, and Turkish pantry staples. Sidewalk bins hold daily fruits and vegetables, while the clean interior stocks ready-to-eat feta and lentil salads for quick lunches.

name: Rotterdam
description: Rotterdam, located just thirty minutes by train from Amsterdam, is one of the largest cities in the Netherlands. Its post-WWII revival has led the city to become most famous for its modern, innovative architecture.

name: Gouda
description: The eponymous home of Gouda cheese, about an hour drive south of Amsterdam. There are plenty of cheese related activities here, including a museum and traditional market. Non-cheese interests include architecture and stroopwafels.

name: Zuid
description: Popular with locals and tourists, Zuid is one of Amsterdam's most happening neighborhoods. It's also known as the Museum Quarter, harboring both the Rijksmuseum and the Van Gogh Museum. Shopping and dining options are abundant too.

name: China Sichuan Restaurant
description: Busy central dining room serving unapologetic Sichuan food with serious, numbing heat. Large shared plates of spicy Dan Dan noodles and roasted seabass arrive alongside a custom-brewed peppercorn beer.

name: Krua Thai Classic
description: Long-running family dining room on a quiet street near Rembrandtplein serving traditional Thai curries and salads. Steamed fish and spicy papaya salad arrive on elevated platters for shared evening meals.

name: The Coffee District
description: A recipient of rave reviews since its opening in 2019; The Coffee District is a modern coffee shop (now with two branches) known for its speciality coffee and selection of baked goods. Don't miss the sea-salt chocolate chip cookies.

name: Rem Eiland
description: Rem Eiland was once a broadcasting station 9 kilometers off the coast in The North Sea. Now it's much closer to shore and home to an upscale bar and restaurant. You'll dine surrounded by an arcade machine, neon smiley, and disco balls.

name: Paon Bali
description: Small, two-person Balinese warung on KNSM Island serving a daily-changing Nasi Campur menu. Lines form outside before dinner as the tiny space fills up for plates piled with rice, spicy roast pork, and sambal.

name: Nemo Science Museum
description: The Nemo Science Museum is a spot for those traveling with children - with five floors of interactive exhibits, there is enough for a full day out. It's a hard place to miss too, given its boat-like appearance.

name: Toki
description: This café is a local's favourite, serving great coffee and a wide selection of tea. They have a few pastries and desserts available, along with a tasty brunch menu. Just know, finding a seat can sometimes be a task.

name: Zaanse Schans
description: One of the Netherlands' most touristic locales, but worth a visit nonetheless. The Zaandam neighborhood is headlined by its bevy of waterside windmills - many having been relocated to create the feel of 18th-19th century village.

name: Restaurant Vermeer
description: Michelin-starred fine dining restaurant serving creative, eclectic Mediterranean cuisine, paired with a diverse wine selection. Choose from four, five, or six courses curated by Chef Chris Naylor and his talented team.

name: The American Book Center
description: This is one of the largest English book stores in Amsterdam; with a huge variety of genres: from manga and sci-fi, to poetry. There is also a small café with coffee and snacks on the first floor.

name: Eastern Docklands
description: Amsterdam's Eastern Docklands neighborhood is populated with former warehouses that have come to be transformed into modern homes, storefronts, and art spaces. The area, now a cultural hub for the city, is a great place to explore.

name: Noordermarkt
description: On Saturdays and Monday mornings this market opens to sell a variety of goods: including food and produce, vintage items, books, and more. It's a great place to stroll through and find a few Amsterdam keepsakes.

name: Leiden
description: An hour south of Amsterdam is the historic town of Leiden; famous for its historic architecture and university - the country's oldest. There are a few interesting museums, including one with works from the locally-born Rembrandt.

name: Venus & Adonis
description: Venus & Adonis' menu features a blend of grilled classics alongside more delicate, modern dishes. Whilst known for its offering of steak and ribs, the restaurant also serves up some popular veggie options. Enjoy a Dutch beer too.

name: Wilde Zwijnen
description: Choose between the three, four, or five-course tasting menus - with or without a beverage pairing. The dishes are creative and mostly feature traditional Dutch favourites turned modern. Expect locally sourced ingredients too.

name: Wolf Atelier
description: This fine-dining restaurant offers guests the chance to customize their own dinner. The bold can choose the 15-course tasting menu - those those wanting a little less can choose a smaller tasting menu. Or just order dishes à la carte.

name: Muiden
description: Just a quick 20-minute drive from Amsterdam is the town of Muiden. The town is most famous for its 13th-century castle, which even has a moat and drawbridge. Other highlights include boat trips along the River Vecht.

name: Thull's Deli
description: This little deli has a wide assortment of quality products and wine; but the main focus is on fermented foods. It's a great place to pick up a sandwich for lunch, along with homemade water kefir flavoured with figs and lemons.

name: Pathé Tuschinski
description: For an opulent move night. The Pathé Tuschinski is a picture house that features a combination of highbrow design influences - Art Deco, Art Nouveau, and Jungendstil. Patrons can enjoy oversized seats with footrests and side tables.

name: Janine Bakery & Restaurant
