description: Casual bakery service at the front shifts into a warmer, wood-fired restaurant in the back. The Italian menu spans from morning cinnamon rolls to slow lunches of pizza and carpaccio.

name: Pompadour
description: Nine Streets chocolaterie and tearoom wrapped in antique wood paneling. The counter stocks Valrhona truffles, while the small back room serves coffee and handmade pastries in a quiet, salon-style setting.

name: Erik's Delicatessen
description: Amsterdam Oost staple stocking a massive selection of Dutch cheeses, charcuterie, and wines. Fresh loaves sell out early, while the counter team freely slices samples for tasting.

name: Haarlemmerstraat
description: Lively shopping street running west from Centraal Station that trades big chains for independent retail. Historic storefronts are dense with vintage clothing, specialty delis, and design boutiques.

name: Maastricht
description: Visit one of the oldest, and possibly, most beautiful cities in the Netherlands. Located two and a half hours from Amsterdam, the city of Maastricht offers plenty of sightseeing opportunities, restaurants, cultural experiences, and more.

name: Vindict Wine
description: Approachable merchant trading technical jargon for clear advice. The selection mixes global standards with deep cuts from Germany and the Netherlands, plus a fridge of cold bottles for immediate pours.

name: Salvo
description: Creative Italian bakery mixing tradition with modern, indulgent fillings. Queues form early for pistachio cornetti and gooey cookies, often taken to go given the limited seating.

name: Casa Gitane
description: Design agency and showroom specializing in raw materials and a nomadic aesthetic. The headquarters functions as a private daylight studio for shoots rather than a walk-in retail shop.

name: Bakhuys
description: Spacious open bakery centered on a wood-fired stone oven turning out slow-fermented sourdough and pizza. The canteen-style room stays busy with laptop workers and locals at long communal tables.

name: The Hoxton, Amsterdam
description: Canalside hotel with great amenities within the lively 9 Straatjes (The Nine Streets) district. The décor features vintage furniture and mid-century themes. Lotti's is an in-house brasserie serving dishes, daytime drinks, and cocktails.

name: Foam
description: Photography museum spread across a maze of three connected canal houses on the Keizersgracht. The space runs a constant rotation of exhibitions, mixing established masters with new work from emerging talent.

name: Vuurtoreneiland
description: This restaurant takes the dining experience to a new level. Located on a little island, the experience starts with a boat ride. Then it moves on to a creative, multicourse menu. Just be sure to book ahead, over a month prior is advised.

name: Jinweide
description: Compact Halal spot serving authentic Lanzhou beef soup with noodles hand-pulled in an open kitchen. The tight, simple room fills quickly for custom-thickness soups and complimentary sides from the self-service bar.

name: Teds
description: All-day brunch spot running a heavy comfort food menu from morning until late afternoon. Waffle fries, French toast, and cocktails fill the tables regardless of the hour – booking ahead is essential to secure a seat.

name: Janine
description: Bright bakery counter up front serves matcha croissants and coffee. A warmer dining room hides in the back, firing Italian lunches from an open wood-fired oven.

name: PizzaPezzi
description: Family-run Roman counter serving rectangular pizza al taglio by weight. Crispy, airy slices are topped with seasonal combos like pumpkin gorgonzola or spicy salami, finished with house olive oil.

name: Shiraz Jardin des Vins
description: Intimate wine bar on the Lijnbaansgracht stocking over 600 labels. Rare bottles are poured by the glass alongside charcuterie, while a terrace and docked boat extend the seating right onto the canal.

name: NOT JUST A GIFT
description: Compact Czaar Peterstraat shop stocking Japanese tableware, wool throws, and soft toys. The counter stays busy with locals dropping off parcels or grabbing last-minute gifts.

name: FLOW BRUNCH & SPECIALTY COFFEE
description: Sleek De Pijp cafe pouring single-origin coffee alongside seasonal all-day brunch. The minimalist room and street-side terrace fill up fast for Turkish eggs and spicy pulled chicken.

name: Satay Club
description: Javanese street food bar centered on a smoking charcoal grill. Marinated skewers arrive fast at the mahogany counter, served with rice cakes and fiery sambal.

name: Fabel Friet Runstraat
description: Narrow fry shop drawing a steady line for fresh-cut potatoes fried in their skins. Paper cones heavy with truffle mayonnaise and parmesan are eaten on the canal bridges just outside.

name: Lourens
description: Tiny Jordaan corner spot serving viral croissant-cookie hybrids and rich pastries. The counter is takeaway only, so the canal wall outside acts as the main dining room for boxes of pistachio-filled dough.

name: Café De Zwart
description: Historic brown café on a busy corner of the Spui. The Art Deco bar pours specialty beers and jenever, while the sidewalk terrace fills up for coffee and apple tart.

name: Door 74
description: Unmarked black doors hide a dark, Art Deco cocktail den. A ring of the bell grants entry to the seated-only room, a quiet spot for conversation and complex drinks.

name: Tony's Chocolonely Superstore
description: High-energy flagship in the old stock exchange stocking the brand's full ethical range. Rows of iPads let shoppers design personalized wrappers and flavor combos, with finished blocks ready for pickup two hours later.

name: Manneken Pis Damrak
description: Busy walk-up counter on the Damrak slinging thick-cut Flemish fries in massive paper cones. The line moves fast for double-fried potatoes topped with a choice of over 20 sauces.

name: Coffee District Willemsparkweg
description: Compact espresso bar pouring Five Ways coffee for a steady queue near Museumplein. The standing-room layout pushes the crowd to the sidewalk bench or Vondelpark with sticky cardamom buns.

name: QV Winebar
description: Warm, low-lit osteria on Beethovenstraat running from casual drinks to intimate dinners. Fresh pasta and imported charcuterie join a list of twenty-five wines poured by the glass.

name: Greenwoods Singel
description: Bustling canal-side spot serving massive English breakfasts and cream teas. The interior is snug enough that the restroom route cuts through the kitchen, while a heated terrace sits right on the water.

name: Zero Zero
description: Italian sandwich shop serving fresh schiacciata to a queue that often spills onto the sidewalk. Seating is scarce, so thick slabs of mortadella and stracciatella are almost always takeaway.

name: Utrecht
description: Less than an hour drive south of Amsterdam is the town of Utrecht. The city center has many historic buildings, along with a stunning canal system. Another main attraction is just outside the city, The De Haar Castle.

name: Mezzave
description: De Pijp deli stuffing freshly steamed pitas with smoked brisket, chicken shawarma, and homemade hummus. Orders cross the counter for takeaway or get carried up to a tiny attic seating area.

name: Edible Treasures
description: Quiet corner shop in Amsterdam Zuid pairing curated kitchen goods with an all-day deli. Ceramics and cookbooks line the shelves, while the counter serves flat whites and chocolate orange babka.

name: Proeflokaal Arendsnest
description: Classic brown café pouring exclusively Dutch craft beer from more than 50 taps. Copper pipes and wood panels line the interior, while the terrace sits directly on the Herengracht.

name: Badhuis Oedipus
description: Perfect spot for beer enthusiasts. Listen to their live radio and sip on a unique brew. If peckish, turn to their bistro style menu for hearty eats and snacks. Best enjoyed when on the outdoor terrace in the sun.

name: Papa Aswa
description: Lush, plant-filled Surinamese restaurant on Cruquiuseiland serving modern shared plates. The family-run kitchen turns out crispy chicken, salted fish fried rice, and cocktails poured into fresh coconuts.

name: ImoveAmsterdam
description: Luxury wellness club running challenging yoga, pilates, and barre sessions. Professional dancers lead music-driven workouts, followed by quiet recovery in the sauna and steam room.

name: Barossa
description: Warm, wood-lined dining room and outdoor terrace on the NDSM waterfront serving South American sharing plates. Wide windows face the IJ river, catching the sunset while cooks work the open kitchen.

name: Eye Film Museum
description: Nicknamed "the cinematic memory of the Netherlands", this museum is home to more than 54,000 works of film. The institute comprises four theaters, an exhibition hall, and offers plenty of activities for both adults and children.

name: Two Story
description: Contemporary art gallery and specialty cafe set within a serene canal house. Patrons wander through the rotating exhibitions on both floors, coffee in hand.

name: Sweets Hotel
description: A truly unique hotel experience; rather than traditional hotel rooms, Sweets offer 28 converted bridge houses scattered around Amsterdam. Forgo the traditional lobby and front desk, and check in to each bespoke space using a smartphone.

name: FC Hyena
description: Waterfront warehouse in Amsterdam Noord housing an arthouse cinema, natural wine bar, and wood-fired restaurant. Evenings shift from drinks on the terrace to taking small plates and glasses onto the screening room couches.

name: Euro Pizza Restaurant
description: Revamped Amsterdam Noord garage pouring natural wine alongside seasonal shared plates and unconventional sourdough pizzas. White tables and a large bar fill the minimal dining room built around an open kitchen and central pizza oven.

name: Luuk's Coffee Noordermarkt
description: Minimalist coffee bar with a neighborhood living room feel, directly opposite the busy Noordermarkt. Baristas pull careful espresso shots into oversized, heavy mugs – the food menu is just a few fresh pastries.

name: louf - de pijp
description: Neighborhood bakery serving slow-fermented sourdough and pastries like cardamom rolls. Its sunny, hidden terrace is a quiet escape just off the bustling Albert Cuyp market.

name: Restaurant Barracuda Amsterdam
description: Massive seafood canteen in a converted Amsterdam-Noord warehouse sitting right on the IJ River. Orders run through a central bar for steady rounds of fresh oysters, fritto misto, and wine out on the wide riverside terrace.

name: Hortus Botanicus
description: Quiet, centuries-old botanical garden tucked into the city center. Outdoor paths wind between a massive historic palm house and a three-climate glasshouse where an elevated walkway cuts through the tropical canopy.

name: Vondelpark
description: Sprawling central park with winding paths, wooded sections, and large ponds. Bicycles and runners keep a steady pace on the paths, while wide open lawns fill up with picnic blankets, dog walkers, and afternoon loungers.

name: Restaurant 'Hotel De Goudfazant'
description: Cavernous Amsterdam-Noord warehouse running a loud, high-energy dinner service. Crisp white tablecloths and red canteen chairs sit among retro cars while the open kitchen serves three-course French dinners and fresh homemade bread.

name: Lumen Travo
description: Intimate canal-side gallery focused on contemporary art from a global, non-Western perspective. The exhibitions are pointed, often exploring complex themes of identity, labor, and post-colonialism.

name: louf - oud west
description: Neighborhood bakery turning out long-fermented sourdough loaves, cardamom rolls, and specialty coffee. The small, wood-lined shop moves fast and sells out early, spilling morning coffee and sesame cookies out onto a sunny front bench.

name: Rosalia's Menagerie
description: Intimate canal-house bar pouring craft cocktails made with local Dutch spirits. The moody, eclectic room fills up for pre-dinner drinks and stays busy through late-night conversations.

name: Chenin Chenin | Natural Wine Shop
description: Jordaan bottle shop stocking minimal intervention European wines, cider, and sake. The relaxed space doubles as a neighborhood hangout running casual tastings, DJ sets, and small omakase dinners.

name: Wijnhuis.Amsterdam
description: Oud-Zuid wine shop stocking low-intervention bottles from Germany, Austria, and Luxembourg. A long ash-wood table sits in the center of the room, set up for sampling Rieslings and Spätburgunders before buying.

name: Black Gold Amsterdam
description: Compact coffee bar and record shop running on local espresso and steady vinyl rotations. The small, cluttered room skips laptops entirely, keeping tables open for chess games and digging through crates of funk and afrobeat.

name: Friedhats FUKU Cafe
description: Bos en Lommer specialty coffee bar and public tasting room for the local Friedhats roastery. Baristas pull daily espressos and rare, competition-grade filter pours alongside fresh pastries and retail beans to go.

name: Back to Black
description: Corner cafe near the Rijksmuseum pouring house-roasted espresso and serving thick slices of homemade apple pie. The tight, laptop-free sitting room faces the canal, filled with low tables, resting dogs, and quiet conversation.

name: Bar Babar
description: Intimate neighborhood wine bar pouring natural wines by the glass alongside local sourdough and charcuterie. Heavy candlelight and wine-colored walls keep the room warm and relaxed for date nights and long conversations.

name: De Wijnwinkel
description: Long-running Nine Streets bottle shop packed with natural and biodynamic European wines. The compact space runs regular tastings and stocks a tight lineup of spirits, olive oil, and books.

name: Super Lyan
description: Retro cocktail bar pairing highly technical drinks with 1950s diner aesthetics. Neon purple lights anchor the main counter, leading into a relaxed mid-century lounge serving playful riffs on classics alongside hot Dutch bitterballen.

name: Café Brandon
description: Quintessential brown café on a canal corner, with walls and ceilings stained dark from decades of smoke. The bar pours mostly beer; on busy nights, the small room empties out onto the street.

name: Stacks Diner
description: Dark, cozy diner with leather benches serving refined American comfort food. The best seats are at the bar, watching the open kitchen send out fried chicken biscuits and hashbrowns with roe.

name: De Kookboekhandel
description: Floor-to-ceiling bookshelves define this culinary-only bookshop, run by a well-known food writer. The tightly curated selection covers global cuisines; a small counter in the back serves simple sandwiches and coffee.

name: Enkhuizen
description: Coastal city an hour north of Amsterdam by train that was once one of the most prosperous in the Netherlands. Local highlights include the settlement's 16th-century walls and the Zuiderzeemuseum.

name: M pies
description: Neighborhood bakery making individual British-style savory pies with thin, crispy crusts. The daily menu runs through creative fillings like cheddar and marmite or pork and jam, boxed up for easy takeaway lunches.

name: Restaurant Bougainville
description: Plush third-floor dining room sitting right above Dam Square with lush fabrics and black chandeliers. The Michelin-starred kitchen serves tasting menus mixing French technique with global flavors and paired wines.

name: Salvo Basement
description: Compact basement bakery serving modern Italian pastries and specialty coffee. Vinyl plays behind the sleek counter as espresso and cream-filled maritozzi head out to a small bench on the canal.

name: Miuz Gelato & Coffee
description: Busy Overtoom gelateria and espresso bar spinning fresh seasonal flavors daily in a back lab. Classic Italian scoops and hot affogatos cross the counter in a compact room with a steady line stretching out the door.

name: Belly Pepper
description: Intimate Oud-West cafe turning out traditional Turkish breakfast in a tight, bustling room. Tables fill fast for plates of creamy cilbir, fresh simit, and hot Turkish tea.

name: Polish supermarket Costa
description: Large Amsterdam Noord supermarket loaded with Polish, Romanian, and Ukrainian daily staples. Aisles are stacked with imported kovbasa, fermented cabbage, and regional dairy rarely found in standard Dutch grocery chains.

name: Nikotin
description: Industrial corner restobar in Amsterdam-Noord wrapped in windows and built around an open kitchen. The bar pours natural wine and sake alongside fire-cooked Asian shared plates and tempura snacks.

name: Juno
description: Wood-beamed De Pijp dining room running entirely on open-flame cooking and vinyl records. Cooks grill octopus and ribeye over a live fire, serving shared plates alongside spicy highballs in a deliberately offline space.

name: levain et le vin
description: Compact bakery and bottle shop pairing daily sourdough with natural wine. Fresh canelés and crusty loaves line the counter, sharing the tight space with shelves of unfiltered bottles and a few seats for morning coffee.

name: De Gooyer Windmill
description: Standing since 1814, this is the country's tallest windmill. The landmark is located in the middle of the city, and its interior is closed to the public. The neighboring brewery is great for enjoying a craft beer in view of the windmill.

name: Brouwerij 't IJ
description: A brewery next to a windmill? It doesn't get more Dutch than that. Nice spot for any type of beer on the river. They also offer cheap tours of the factory on the weekends for just over the price of a drink.

name: Uncommon Bar
description: Warm, minimalist Oud-West space running as a coffee bar by day before shifting to plant-based dinners on weekend nights. The open kitchen turns out fermented, vegetable-focused plates meant for splitting over glasses of natural wine.

name: Pulitzer Amsterdam
description: A luxury hotel comprising 25 renovated canal houses originally built in the 17th and 18th century. This stylish, well-designed hotel features suites with additional living spaces, a restaurant, bar, and a tranquil courtyard garden.

name: Bierfabriek
description: Centrally located brewery with a down-to-earth crowd. Expansive indoor space serving a selection of their own beers alongside hearty dishes. Grab a streetside table for alfresco drinks - daytime or evening.

name: Bar Basquiat
description: Bar-restaurant space with interior design inspired by its namesake artist, Jean-Michel Basquiat. Street food-style breakfast and lunch dishes served throughout the day. But it's best at night for drinks and real Dutch "gezelligheid".

name: De L'Europe
description: Grand 1896 hotel sitting right on the Amstel river, mixing classic European interiors with heated marble bathrooms. Mornings run on breakfasts by the water, and nights wrap up with cocktails at Freddy’s Bar.

name: Dak Showroom by Dak Coffee Roasters
description: Minimalist tasting room for a specialty coffee roaster in a Noord industrial park. Experimental, lightly roasted single origins pour at a hammered stainless steel bar surrounded by soft clay walls and shelves of retail beans.

name: Van Stapele Koekmakerij
description: Single-item bakery making a dark chocolate cookie with a melted white chocolate center. Fresh batches come straight from the oven all day, keeping a steady line moving through the chandelier-lit shop until the daily supply runs out.

name: Chun Café Berenstraat
description: Tiny Nine Streets cafe serving thick, Korean-style brioche toasts and Uji matcha lattes. A constant queue stretches down the block for the few tables, keeping the takeaway counter busy with rib eye bulgogi and strawberry matcha.

name: Choux
description: Choux features a creative, gastronomic multi-course tasting menu that leans heavily on vegetarian dishes. Their sister company is a natural wine importer, so indulge in a few glasses of red or white too.

name: Beré Nali Amsterdam
description: Spacious Overtoom brunch restaurant turning out Turkish-leaning Mediterranean plates like çılbır and Borek Florentine. The warm dining room easily handles large tables and long, unrushed mornings.

name: Gifu Ramen Bar
description: Sleek Jordaan ramen bar serving handmade noodles and izakaya plates. Concrete and wood line the dimly lit room, with counter seats running steady for bowls of creamy tonkotsu and cold draft beer.

name: The National Maritime Museum
description: Beginning life as a naval warehouse, several centuries and renovations have turned this building into The National Maritime Museum. Visit this interactive space to enjoy virtual voyages, and a replica of an 18th-century merchant ship.

name: MONTY'S Toasties
description: Tiny Jordaan shop serving elevated sourdough toasties for a quick lunch on the go. The focused menu sticks to a rich three-cheese blend layered with sharp additions like kimchi, marmite, or red onion chutney.

name: Van Gogh Museum
description: The largest collection of Van Gogh paintings and drawings in the world. The museum itself is architecturally interesting and houses a pleasant cafe that's perfect for lunch. Can get busy so be sure to get tickets ahead.

name: Museum Het Schip
description: A hot spot for architecture fans. Originally an apartment building, this museum is arguably the best existing example of the Amsterdam School style of architecture. The complex offers guided tours in multiple languages.

name: De School
description: Named for its former purpose as a technical college, De School is a multi-purpose space that boasts a youthful vibe. The facility comprises a restaurant, café, gym, and exhibition spaces - it also hosts some of the best local music acts.

name: Het Twiske
description: A large park and reserve that provides the people of Amsterdam with a place to relax, enjoy nature, and partake in outdoor activities. With one-third of the park being water, visitors can swim, sail, and kayak at their leisure.

name: Our Lord in the Attic Museum
description: In a time when the city forbade Catholic worship, this secretive attic church provided a space for prayer. The museum now serves as testament to the then hidden coexistence of religious denominations in the seventeenth century.

name: Tropenmuseum
description: Tropenmuseum celebrates the cultures of the world. They have permanent and temporary exhibits that explain cultural differences from areas all around the globe. The establishment also hosts a variety of spaces for its younger visitors.

name: Alkmaar
description: Small city located 40 kilometers north of Amsterdam. The historic cheese market, with over 30,000 kilos of product, is the main attraction here - artisans and vendors use traditional methods to weigh, carry, and sell their goods.

name: Delft
description: City southwest of Amsterdam intersected by canals and famous for being the manufacturing hub of Delftware - a brand of handpainted blue and white pottery. Visitors often spend their days wandering the old town and market square.

name: cafe De Kleine Bes
description: Blue-walled corner cafe in Amsterdam Oost with a small terrace and casual bar seating. The space runs steady from morning coffee straight into evening wine, bitterballen, and a simple warm dinner.

name: cafe wilhelmina
description: Dimly lit Helmersbuurt neighborhood cafe running steady into the night as a casual bistro. Evening menus stick to European classics like mussels with smoked beurre blanc and half chicken alongside glasses of natural wine.

name: Fort Negen
description: Neighborhood bakery with a city-wide reputation. Swing by in the morning for a coffee and Instagram-worthy croissant. Grab a loaf of sourdough for brunch or lunch too. Its popularity leads to queues, but the goods are worth the wait.

name: Bakkerij Wolf - Wolvenstraat
description: Lively De 9 Straatjes bakery and café turning out fresh sourdough, cinnamon buns, and espresso. The cozy room runs a steady brunch service, landing plates of shakshuka and French toast on tables right beside the open ovens.

name: grammes
description: Tiny Rivierenbuurt storefront baking classic French viennoiserie and laminated pastries. Morning queues stretch past the single outdoor bench for buttery kouign-amann and flaky croissants, with most orders packed strictly to go.

name: Uncommon Cafe
description: Minimalist Oud-West roastery and cafe pouring single-origin espresso and seasonal filter brews. The laptop-free, beige-and-wood dining room stays busy through the morning over large brunch plates, fresh pastries, and conversation.

name: Layers Bakery & Deli
description: Bright, stainless-steel bakery and deli in De Pijp running a split schedule below a glass-walled pastry lab. Mornings mean multi-layered croissants and matcha lattes, while the midday switch brings lobster rolls and burgers.

name: Rosèl Amsterdam - Sandwiches & Coffee
description: Compact lunch shop slinging specialty espresso and a tight menu of airy sourdough focaccia sandwiches. Orders move fast across the main counter, eaten standing at the wooden wall bar or taken to go.

name: Café Soleil Amsterdam
description: Mediterranean spot in a converted boat workshop in Amsterdam Noord. Shared plates of clams and piri piri chicken crowd the large terrace, while the candlelit interior hosts live jazz on Sundays.

name: Morgan & Mees
description: Cozy boutique hotel in Amsterdam West, boasting an elegant ambiance. Enjoy international classics such as bouillabaisse at their stylish restaurant, paired with beer and wine from their cocktail bar.

name: BADHUS Social Sauna
description: Social sauna in a converted warehouse favoring conversation over silence. The floating hot room sits on the canal, with ladders for dropping straight into the open water.

name: P/////AKT
description: Non-profit contemporary art gallery giving an exhibit space for new, emerging artists. The gallery encourages artists to develop work that relates to the specific nature of the exhibition space present within the building.

name: The Dylan
description: Luxurious five-star hotel with 40 rooms in four unique styles, located by the renowned Keizersgracht canal. Guests can enjoy a casual meal at the brasserie or a fine dining experience at the Michelin-starred restaurant on site.

name: Canal District
description: Take a stroll around the Grachtengordal neighborhood, also called the canal district. The canals were dug in the 17th century, for a combination of urban planning and defense purposes, and encompass the city center like a series of rings.

name: W Amsterdam
description: One of several Marriott hotels in the city. The W Amsterdam is a well-designed hotel with five-star amenities, including a modern spa, a rooftop bar, and a pair of restaurants. Far from a unique independent, but proven comfort.

name: Wynand Fockink Tasting Room
description: This distillery has been around from the 17th century; today they are still producing traditional Dutch favorites, like genevers, alongside modern items like prebatched cocktails. Stop by the tasting room of an evening for a drink.

name: Stedelijk Museum
description: This contemporary and modern art museum, often noted for its bathtub like architecture, is populated by both famous and up-and-coming artists. There are over 500 pieces within the museum, so be sure to leave enough time for everything.

name: Akasha Spa
description: Deluxe wellness facility located within the Conservatorium Hotel, offering a fully-equipped gym, fitness and yoga classes, and an underground spa featuring a pool, sauna, and hamam. Day passes and monthly memberships are available.

name: Volkshotel
description: This trendy hotel is an ideal space for digital nomads - take advantage of the free working spaces, and enjoy breaks in the rooftop hot tubs. There are a variety of rooms on offer at Volkshotel, from small cabins to large suites.

name: Grimm Gallery
description: A contemporary gallery featuring Daniel Richter, Charles Avery, and other international artists. Grimm prides itself on representing both established and emerging creators, as well as a variety of new and traditional mediums.

name: Fromagerie Abraham Kef
description: A trio of cheese shops that sell a curated collection of goods from some of the country's top producers. Buy a selection of cheeses and other deli goods for a DIY lunch platter. Book in for one of their Sunday cheese tasting sessions too.

name: JUKI
description: Curated showroom for 20th-century design, with restored furniture and lighting from names like Alvar Aalto. The physical space is only open on Saturdays – new pieces are released online each Thursday.

name: Flevopark
description: Flevopark is a public green space next to Nieuwe Diep Lake. The park can host a range of activities - from walking trails to tennis and outdoor swimming. One of the many places in Amsterdam to spend a sunny afternoon.

name: The Concertgebouw
description: One of the most respected music halls in the world, Amsterdam's Concertgebouw first opened its doors in 1888. The venue hosts an average of 900 concerts and events a year, including a free lunchtime performance each Wednesday.

name: Petit Peche
description: Intimate 28-seat dining room with counter seating facing a busy open kitchen. The fixed tasting menu leans into rich French flavors and dishes like duck hearts or frog legs.

name: Cafe Binnenvisser
description: Traditional corner pub running as a high-energy natural wine bar. The triangular room stays loud and low-lit as crowds share funky bottles and seasonal vegetable plates.

name: Cafe Beurre
description: Intimate Westerpark bistro serving vegetarian small plates with a heavy hand on the butter. Wine and rich dishes like mushroom brioche fill the small tables indoors and out on the terrace.

name: Barracuda
description: Industrial warehouse in Noord serving simple seafood with the energy of a beachside canteen. Vintage school tables crowd with fritto misto and grilled catch near the self-service bar.

name: Kiki
description: Modern riff on the brown café occupying a busy canal corner. The terrace and mahogany bar fill fast for natural wine, oysters, and serious smash burgers.

name: Wolf
description: Glass-walled dining room set on a former railway bridge above the IJ. Creative tasting menus run up to fifteen courses in a raw space of concrete, steel, and panoramic views.

name: A-Fusion Food & Drinks
description: Dimly lit Zeedijk dining room buzzing with steam and noise from the open kitchens. Sushi rolls and Korean beef arrive in rapid-fire rounds that fill every inch of the table.

name: Kim's So Korean Food Centrum
description: Lively three-story kitchen in central Amsterdam turns out sizzling stone bowl bibimbap and spicy fried chicken. Large bulgogi platters feed groups before mango bingsu shaved ice cools the heat.

name: Namaste India
description: Compact De Pijp storefront serving homemade Indian standards and Halal meats. The kitchen dials up the heat on request, feeding a small dining room and a steady stream of takeaway orders.

name: Charcuteria Wine & Foodbar
description: Czaar Peterstraat dining room pairing Spanish charcuterie with a tight list of Italian pastas. High tables and a long bar fill with shared boards of Pata Negra, bowls of ragu, and glasses of Rioja.

name: Tasca Bellota
description: Waterfront Spanish spot in the Western Islands with a terrace facing the harbor. Pitchers of sangria and plates of jamón fill the table during the 45-minute wait for fresh paella.

name: Café Modern
description: Retro dining room in a former bank serving fixed seasonal surprise menus on vintage Formica. An open kitchen drives the unhurried dinner service, while the basement vault takes private groups.
